⟦2𝑟 − 1, 2𝑟 − 2𝑟 − 1, 3⟧ QUANTUM HAMMING CODE [822]  

> quantum_hamming_css
> DESCRIPTION

Member of a family of self-dual CSS codes constructed from [2𝑟 − 1, 2𝑟 − 𝑟 − 1, 3] = 𝐶 𝑋 = 𝐶 𝑍 Hamming codes and their duals, the simplex codes. The code’s stabilizer generator matrix blocks 𝐻 𝑋 and 𝐻 𝑍 are both the generator matrix for a simplex code. The weight of each stabilizer generator is 2𝑟 −1. 

> PROTECTION

Protects against any single qubit error.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Pauli, Hadamard, and CNOT gates.  

> DECODING

⊲ Efficient decoder [3121].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Syndrome measurement can be done with two ancillary flag qubits [ 3122 ]. ⊲ Concatenating a growing sequence of quantum Hamming codes yields fault-tolerant quantum com-putation with constant space overhead and quasi-polylogarithmic time overhead [ 3121 ]. ⊲ Concatenating quantum Hamming codes on top of the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ and 𝐶 6 codes yields fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant space and quasi-polylogarithmic time overheads [ 3123 ]. In the optimized protocol of Ref. [ 3123 ], a level-five 𝐶 4/𝐶 6 code underlies concatenated quantum Hamming codes 

Q5, Q6, Q7, Q7, yielding a 2.5% threshold and space overheads 162 

and 373 physical qubits per logical qubit at physical error rate 0.1% 

for logical CNOT error rates 10 −10 and 10 −24 , respectively. ⊲ Amodified tower of interleaved quantum Hamming codes with re-served qubits and recursive hookless Pauli-product measurements yields fault-tolerant quantum computation on a 1D nearest-neighbor qubit line with asymptotic rate above 5% , constant space overhead, quasi-polylogarithmic time overhead, and a threshold [3124].  

> THRESHOLD

⊲ Concatenated threshold › p. 435 requiring constant-space and quasi-polylogarithmic time overhead [3121].

⟦23 , 1, 7⟧ QUANTUM GOLAY CODE [822] qubit_golay  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Qubit Golay code  

> DESCRIPTION

A ⟦23 , 1, 7⟧ self-dual CSS code with eleven stabilizer generators of each type, and with each generator being weight eight. The code’s 11-by-23 stabilizer generator matrix blocks 𝐻 𝑋 and 𝐻 𝑍 

are both parity-check matrices of the classical Golay code. Equiva-lently, it can be obtained from the [24 , 12 , 8] extended Golay code by shortening on one bit to a self-orthogonal [23 , 11 , 7] code [ 89 , Appx. A.1.5]. It can be punctured twice to obtain a ⟦21 , 3, 5⟧ code [89]. The automorphism group of the code is 𝑀 23 [3129].  

> PROTECTION

Detects up to 6-qubit errors and corrects up to 3-qubit errors.  

> MAGIC

Magic-state distillation scaling exponent 𝛾 = log 2 23 ≈

4.52 [673].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Fault-tolerant depth-7 circuit consisting of 57 CNOT gates and preparing a logical-zero state [ 760 ]. ⊲ Circuit with 56 entangling gates using reinforcement learning [3130].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Single-qubit Clifford group › p. 244 by choosing 𝑈 = 𝑈 ⊗23 for every Clifford unitary 𝑈 [760 ].  

> GATES

⊲ The Golay code can be used to perform magic-state distil-lation for the magic state defined as |𝑇 ⟩⟨ 𝑇 | = 12 (𝐼 + 1√3 (𝑋 + 𝑌 + 𝑍 )) ,where |𝑇 ⟩ is an eigenstate of the Clifford "facet" gate 𝑆𝐻 [3131 ]. 

⊲ Pipelining the ⟦23 , 1, 7⟧ code after ⟦7, 1, 3⟧ and ⟦17 , 1, 5⟧ inner-code stages yields a 95-to-1 seventh-order magic-state distillation protocol [89, Sec. V.B.3].  

> DECODING

⊲ Meggitt decoding for the cyclic CSS structure was used in comparative logical-CNOT simulations [3132].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Fault-tolerant depth-7 circuit consisting of 57 CNOT gates and preparing a logical-zero state [760].  

> THRESHOLD

⊲ 1.32 × 10 −3-per gate error rate for depolarizing noise upon recursive concatenation [ 760 ], improving previous lower bounds [ 492 , 3132 , 3133 ]. A numerical study [ 492 ] found that the Go-lay code achieved the highest threshold among a dozen well-known codes at the time [3132].  

> NOTES

⊲ See Ref. [ 3134 ] for more details. ⊲ Two levels of concate-nation of the qubit Golay code can tolerate high teleportation errors [3135, 3136].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Self-dual CSS code › p. 449 ⊲ Quantum quadratic-residue (QR) code › p. 502 — The Golay code is a qubit quantum QR code [ 791 ,2830 ]. ⊲ Quantum data-syndrome (QDS) code › p. 424 — There exists a ⟦23 , 1, 7 : 18 ⟧ QDS code based on the qubit Golay code, requiring 18 additional stabilizer measurements instead of 24 from the general cyclic construction [2830, Ex. 15].  

> COUSINS

⊲ [23 , 12 , 7] Golay code › p. 175 — The qubit Golay code is a CSS code constructed with the Golay code. ⊲ ⟦11 , 1, 5⟧3 qutrit Golay code › p. 472 — The qubit Golay code is the qubit counterpart of the qutrit Golay code. ⊲ Triorthogonal code › p. 464 — A ⟦95 , 1, 7⟧

triorthogonal code with a transversal 𝑇 gate can be obtained from the qubit Golay code via the doubling transformation [ 3137 ]. ⊲ Small-distance qubit stabilizer code › p. 451 — The quantum Golay code can be punctured twice to obtain a ⟦21 , 3, 5⟧ code. ⊲ Concatenated cat code › p. 519 — Two-component cat codes concatenated with Steane and Golay codes are estimated to be fault tolerant against photon loss › p. 508 noise with rate 𝜂 < 5 × 10 −4 provided that 𝛼 > 1.2 [3138].

⟦2𝑚, 2𝑚 − 2, 2⟧ ERROR-DETECTING CODE [702, 822, 3139] iceberg  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Iceberg code ⊲ ⟦2𝑚, 2𝑚 − 2, 2⟧ quantum parity code  

> DESCRIPTION

Self-complementary and self-dual CSS code for 𝑚 ≥

2 with generators {𝑋 𝑋 · · · 𝑋, 𝑍 𝑍 · · · 𝑍 } acting on all 2𝑚 physical qubits. The code is constructed via the CSS construction from an SPC code and a repetition code [ 737 , Sec. III]. This is the highest-rate distance-two code when an even number of qubits is used [429]. Admits a basis such that each codeword is a superposition of a computational basis state labeled by an even-weight bitstring 𝑏 and a state labeled by the negation of 𝑏 . Its all-zero logical state is a conventional GHZ state. Removing the 𝑍 -type generator expands the number of codewords to all combinations of bitstrings and their negations, yielding a code with 𝑘 = 2𝑚 − 1 [3140]. All of its automorphisms lie in the Clifford group › p. 244 [426 , Thm. 13].  

> PROTECTION

Detects a single-qubit error.  

> ENCODING

⊲ Adaptive constant-depth circuit with geometrically lo-cal gates and measurements throughout [3141, 3142].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Transveral CNOT gates can be performed by first teleporting qubits into different code blocks [ 702 , Sec. VII]. ⊲ For 2𝑚 being a multiple of four, this code houses a transversal representation of the single-qubit Clifford group [ 765 , Sec. 3.1]. Its 𝑛 -block version houses a transversal repre-sentation of the 𝑛 -qubit Clifford group [ 765 , Secs. 3.1 and 3.4]. The commutant of transversal representations of the Clifford group con-tains qubit permutations and projections onto the ⟦2𝑚, 2𝑚 − 2, 2⟧

error-detecting code [766].  

> GATES

⊲ Logical SWAP gates can be performed fault tolerantly using an ancilla qubit [ 702 , Sec. VII]. ⊲ Universal set of gates, each of which is supported on two qubits [ 3143 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant Clifford Trotter circuits that are linear in 𝑘 using flag qubits via a solve-and-stitch algorithm and application of a logical identity circuit [3144].  

> DECODING

⊲ The ⟦2𝑚, 2𝑚 − 2, 2⟧ error-detecting code [ 3145 ] and its relative the code with single stabilizer 𝑋 𝑋 · · · 𝑋 [3146 ] admit autonomous QEC against single AD › p. 508 errors.  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Logical SWAP gates can be performed fault tol-erantly using an ancilla qubit [ 702 , Sec. VII]. ⊲ Two-qubit fault-tolerant state preparation, error detection and projective measure-ments [ 3122 ] (see also [ 3143 ]). ⊲ CNOT and Hadamard gates using only two extra qubits and four-qubit fault-tolerant 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gate [ 755 ]. 

⊲ Fault-tolerant Clifford Trotter circuits that are linear in 𝑘 using flag qubits via a solve-and-stitch algorithm and application of a logi-cal identity circuit [ 3144 ]. ⊲ Weak fault tolerance: any single gate error can be detected by measuring stabilizers and utilizing extra ancillas [3147].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Trapped-ion devices: the 𝑚 = 5 code has been real-ized on a 12-qubit device by Quantinuum [ 3143 ]. The QAOA algorithm has been realized on the 𝑚 = 18 code using 510 two-logical-qubit gates [ 3148 ]. State preparation, measurement, and a partially fault-tolerant simulation of the XY model demonstrated on a 98-qubit Quantinuum Helios device using the code and its concatenated ver-sion [774].

For prime-power dimensions with 𝑞 = 𝑝 𝑚 and 𝑚 > 1,this yields a Galois-qudit code of distance one that is generally not a 343 true stabilizer code because the stabilizer is not closed under multi-plication by arbitrary 𝛾 ∈ F𝑞 . Adding all 𝑀 1 (𝛾 ) and 𝑀 2 (𝛾 ) to the stabilizer group recovers the corresponding true Galois-qudit CSS code of distance two [381, Sec. 8.2.2].

⟦4, 1, 1, 2⟧ FOUR-QUBIT SUBSYSTEM CODE [3, 2947] bacon_shor_4  

> DESCRIPTION

Error-detecting four-qubit subsystem stabilizer code encoding one logical qubit and one gauge qubit. The ⟦4, 1, 1, 2⟧ code can be obtained by picking one of the logical qubits of the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ four-qubit code to be a gauge qubit; e.g., see Ref. [ 3154 ]. One particular gauge configuration has gauge group G

with gauge generators (excluding phases) 

𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 . (218)  

> PROTECTION

The code detects arbitrary single-qubit errors. An equal-weight sum of its gauge generators has energy separation 2(√2 − 1),so encoding into the corresponding ground subspace suppresses arbitrary single-qubit errors using non-commuting two-local Hamil-tonian terms [640].

⊲ Bacon-Shor code › p. 368 — The four-qubit subsystem code is the shortest error-detecting Bacon-Shor code.

⟦4, 1, 2⟧ LEUNG-NIELSEN-CHUANG-YAMAMOTO (LNCY) CODE [820] css_4_1_2  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ ⟦4, 1, 2⟧ Leung code  

> DESCRIPTION

A four-qubit CSS stabilizer code that is the only qubit CSS code with such parameters. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 6] 

𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 . (219) The code is depicted in Fig. 58 › p. 344 .344   

> FIG. 58: Stabilizer generators of the

⟦4, 1, 2⟧ LNCY code. The 4 data qubits (circles) are arranged on a 2 × 2 rotated surface code lattice with open boundaries. The bulk generator is a weight-four (four-body) 𝑍 operator and the two boundary generators are weight-two (two-body) 𝑋 operators. Red regions correspond to 𝑋  

> operators while blue regions correspond to

𝑍 operators. 

The code admits the following basis of codewords, 

|0⟩ = (| 0000 ⟩ + | 1111 ⟩)/ √2

|1⟩ = (| 0011 ⟩ + | 1100 ⟩)/ √2 . (220) It is realized as the {| 00 ⟩, |01 ⟩} subcode of the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ four-qubit code [ 820 ], and the subcodes spanned by |00 ⟩ and any other ⟦4, 2, 2⟧

codeword are equivalent to it. Applying the Pauli string 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 to its codewords yields an equivalent constant-excitation ⟦4, 1, 2⟧ code. The code’s ±-basis codewords can be written as 

|±⟩ = 12 (| 00 ⟩ ± | 11 ⟩) ⊗2 . (221) This code can be thought of as a concatenation of a two-qubit bit-flip with a two-qubit phase-flip code.  

> PROTECTION

Detects a single-qubit error or single erasure as a distance-two code. The code also approximately corrects a sin-gle AD › p. 508 error, with recovery fidelity 1 − 5𝛾 2 + 𝑂 (𝛾 3) [ 820 ]. A complementary-channel › p. 304 analysis shows that the optimal worst-case entanglement-fidelity distance for this code under AD › p. 508 

noise is of order 𝛾 , improving over the uncorrected order √𝛾 , and that no recovery can improve this asymptotic scaling [ 2465 ]. The 

{| 01 ⟩, |11 ⟩} ⟦ 4, 1, 2⟧ subcode [ 3156 ] also approximately corrects a single AD › p. 508 error, and is a constant-excitation code.  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Linear optical networks [3157 , 3158 ]. 

⊲ Superconducting-circuit devices [3159 , 3160 ]. ⊲ Logical gates within one block [ 3161 ] and between two blocks [ 3162 ], with the latter interpreted as lattice surgery between planar surface codes, were realized in superconducting circuits. ⊲ Neutral atom arrays by Atom Computing ran the Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm on up to 28 logical qubits [ 3163 ]. ⊲ Break-even performance has been demonstrated on a superconducting IBM device using the syndrome-based Petz recovery [ 2519 ]. ⊲ Implementation of a universal logical gate set in superconducting circuits by Origin Quantum Computing [3164].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Rotated surface code › p. 448 — The ⟦4, 1, 2⟧ LNCY code is a small planar rotated surface code [ 3159 –3162 ]. ⊲ Quantum parity code (QPC) › p. 427 — The ⟦4, 1, 2⟧ LNCY code is the smallest QPC, i.e., a concatenation of a two-qubit bit-flip with a two-qubit phase-flip repetition code. An ⟦8, 1, 2⟧ QPC correcting a single AD › p. 508 error is equivalent to a concatenation of its constant-excitation version with the dual-rail code [2633, 3156, 3165]. 

⊲ ⟦2(𝑚 + 1), 𝑚, 2⟧ single-loss AD code › p. 337 — The ⟦4, 1, 2⟧

> › p. 508

error. A (( 4, 3, 1)) 2 jump code is a subcode of the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code and contains the ⟦4, 1, 2⟧ LNCY code as a subcode [129].

⟦4, 2, 2⟧ FOUR-QUBIT CODE [3174, 3175] stab_4_2_2  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ 𝐶 4 code ⊲ Little Shor code  

> DESCRIPTION

A four-qubit hyperbolic self-dual CSS stabilizer code that is the smallest two-logical-qubit stabilizer code to detect a single-qubit error. It is unique for its parameters [426, Thm. 8]. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 9] 

𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 . (223) Its stabilizer generator matrix blocks, 𝐻 𝑋 = 𝐻 𝑍 = (1, 1, 1, 1), are both the parity-check matrix of the [4, 3, 2] SPC code. A basis of codewords is 

|00 ⟩ = (| 0000 ⟩ + | 1111 ⟩)/ √2

|01 ⟩ = (| 0011 ⟩ + | 1100 ⟩)/ √2

|10 ⟩ = (| 0101 ⟩ + | 1010 ⟩)/ √2

|11 ⟩ = (| 0110 ⟩ + | 1001 ⟩)/ √2 .

(224)  

> PROTECTION

Detects a single-qubit error [ 3174 ] or single erasure [3175 ]. It cannot correct arbitrary single-qubit errors because 

⌊ 𝑑 −12 ⌋ = 0. An equivalent version of this code can suppress errors in adiabatic quantum computation by being used as an excited-state space of a particular Hamiltonian [2610].  

> MAGIC

Various magic-state distillation protocols exist for the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧

qubit code and the 𝐶 6 code in what are known as Meier-Eastin-Knill (MEK) protocols [ 89 , 675 ]. In the inner/outer-code formulation of Ref. [ 89 ], the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code is a hyperbolic self-dual inner code for quadratic distillation. For example, the magic-state yield parameter is 𝛾 = log 2 5 ≈ 2.322 for a protocol using the ⟦10 , 2, 2⟧ code [ 674 ,Box 2]; see also [672, Table IV].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ A tensor product of Hadamard gates applies a Hadamard gate to both logical qubits, and a tensor product of 𝑆 = √𝑍 gates applies a 𝐶𝑍 gate followed by a logical 𝑍 on both qubits [ 768 ] (see also [ 769 ]). A logical 𝐶𝑍 gate is then realized by √𝑍 ⊗ √𝑍 † ⊗ √𝑍 † ⊗ √𝑍 . With a different logical basis, transversal Hadamard swaps the two logical qubits, enabling control-SWAP and 𝐻 ⊗2-measurement routines for quadratic magic-state distillation [ 89 , Sec. I.B.1]. ⊲ This code is the only four-qubit subspace to house a transversal representation of the single-qubit Clifford group but not of the single-qubit unitary group [ 765 , Eq. (104)]. Equivalently, its projector is the only extra generator of the fourth tensor-power Clifford commutant beyond qubit permutations [ 765 , Thm. 1]. Its 𝑛 -block version is a ⟦4𝑛, 2𝑛, 2⟧ code, which houses a signed permutation representation of the 𝑛 -qubit Clifford group [765, Sec. 3.1 and Appx. B].  

> GATES

⊲ Some inter-block gates can be weight-two (two-body) with the help of perturbative gadgets, making it possible to suppress er-rors in adiabatic quantum computation [ 2610 ]. ⊲ Logical Clifford circuits › p. 244 for various qubit connectivities [3176].  

> DECODING

⊲ Erasure decoder [3177].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Preparation of certain states, both magic and non-magic, along with transversal gates can be performed fault-tolerantly, but requires post-selection because the code cannot cor-rect errors [ 768 ]. Magic states can be injected into surface and color codes since the code is a small instance of both [ 3168 ]. ⊲ Knill’s 

𝐶 4/𝐶 6 architecture uses the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code at the first level and the 

𝐶 6 code at higher levels, together with error-correcting telepor-tation [ 428 ]. Later work refined the postselected-threshold anal-ysis [ 3178 , 3179 ] (see also Ref. [3180 ]). ⊲ Concatenating quan-tum Hamming codes on top of the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ and 𝐶 6 codes yields fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant space and quasi-polylogarithmic time overheads [ 3123 ]. In the optimized protocol of Ref. [ 3123 ], a level-five 𝐶 4/𝐶 6 code underlies concatenated quan-tum Hamming codes Q5, Q6, Q7, Q7, yielding a 2.5% threshold and space overheads 162 and 373 physical qubits per logical qubit at phys-ical error rate 0.1% for logical CNOT error rates 10 −10 and 10 −24 , re-spectively. ⊲ Fault-tolerant implementation of the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm [3181].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ See also [ 3182 , Tab. I] for more details on each experimental realization. ⊲ Trapped-ion device by IonQ [ 3183 ]. 

⊲ Logical state preparation and flag-qubit error correction real-ized in superconducting-circuit devices by IBM [ 3167 , 3184 – 3186 ]. 

⊲ The CZ magic state has been realized on an IBM heavy-hex super-conducting circuit device [ 3168 ]. ⊲ CPC gadgets for the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧

code have been implemented on the IBM 5Q superconducting de-vice [ 3187 ]. ⊲ An FPGA implementation of the collision clustering decoder [ 3188 ] realized on a Rigetti superconducting device [ 3189 ]. 

⊲ Neutral atom arrays: error detection, erasure correction, and post-selected fault-tolerant circuits demonstrated on 24 logical qubits on a 256-qubit device by Atom Computing, with each qubit encoded in the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code [ 3163 ]. Post-selected fault-tolerant realization of a benchmarking protocol [ 768 ], preparation of the ground state of the single-impurity Anderson impurity model, and post-selected fault-tolerant logical Bell-state preparation demonstrated on one copy of the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code on a device by Infleqtion [ 3182 ]. Error correction with mid-circuit erasure measurements and logical tele-portation demonstrated by the Thompson group [ 3190 ]. Logical implementation of Shor’s algorithm on a device by Infleqtion [ 3191 ].

⟦47 , 1, 11 ⟧ QUANTUM QR CODE [3132] stab_47_1_11  

> DESCRIPTION

A ⟦47 , 1, 11 ⟧ self-dual CSS code constructed from a bi-nary quadratic-residue code. It is one of the shortest known qubit stabilizer codes of distance eleven that realizes the full Clifford group transversally [724].  

> PROTECTION

Detects up to 10-qubit errors and corrects up to 5-qubit errors.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ All logical Clifford gates  

> › p. 244

are realized transversally [724].  

> DECODING

⊲ Algebraic decoder [3132].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Self-dual CSS code › p. 449 ⊲ Quantum quadratic-residue (QR) code › p. 502 — The ⟦47 , 1, 11 ⟧ code is a qubit quantum QR code [724, 3132].  

> COUSIN

⟦49 , 1, 5⟧ TRIORTHOGONAL CODE [659, Appx. B] stab_49_1_5  

> DESCRIPTION

Triorthogonal and quantum divisible code which is the smallest distance-five stabilizer code to admit a transversal 𝑇 gate [631 ][ 659 , Appx. B]. It is one example of a level-three generalized divisible code obtainable from the doubling transformation [ 699 ,Sec. VI.D]. Its 𝑋 -type stabilizers form a triply even linear binary code in the symplectic representation › p. 442 . 

> MAGIC

The code yields an exponent 𝛾 = log 49 /log 5 ≈ 2.42 .

⟦5, 1, 3⟧ FIVE-QUBIT PERFECT CODE [2685, 3201] stab_5_1_3  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Laflamme code  

> DESCRIPTION

Five-qubit cyclic stabilizer code that is the smallest qubit stabilizer code to correct a single-qubit error. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 21] 

𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝑍 . (227) A basis of codewords for the above stabilizer is [381, Ch. 3] 

|0⟩ = 14 (| 00000 ⟩ + | 10010 ⟩ + | 01001 ⟩ − | 11011 ⟩+ | 10100 ⟩ − | 00110 ⟩ − | 11101 ⟩ − | 01111 ⟩+ | 01010 ⟩ − | 11000 ⟩ − | 00011 ⟩ − | 10001 ⟩− | 11110 ⟩ − | 01100 ⟩ − | 10111 ⟩ + | 00101 ⟩) |1⟩ = 14 (| 11111 ⟩ + | 01101 ⟩ + | 10110 ⟩ − | 00100 ⟩+ | 01011 ⟩ − | 11001 ⟩ − | 00010 ⟩ − | 10000 ⟩+ | 10101 ⟩ − | 00111 ⟩ − | 11100 ⟩ − | 01110 ⟩− | 00001 ⟩ − | 10011 ⟩ − | 01000 ⟩ + | 11010 ⟩) .

(228) Logical Pauli operators are ¯𝑋 = 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 and ¯𝑍 = 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 [ 381 ,Table 3.4]. The code’s automorphism group is the dihedral group of order 10 [ 3129 ]. A graph-code realization of the code uses a pentagon graph with an additional central input node [ 826 ]. The encoder-respecting form › p. 442 can be taken to have this shape [819]. It is the unique code for its parameters, up to equivalence [ 426 ,Corr. 10]. Any five-qubit 2𝑇 -transversal stabilizer code with distance 

𝑑 > 1 must be the five-qubit code [3202, 3203]. This code is sometimes referred to as the DiVincenzo-Shor code after a paper that studied the code’s syndrome extraction circuits [3204].  

> PROTECTION

Smallest stabilizer code that protects against a single error on any one qubit. Detects two-qubit errors. The five-qubit perfect code approximately corrects a single AD › p. 508 error [820].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Nine single- and two-qubit unitaries, six of which are CNOT gates [ 3205 ]. ⊲ Four generalized control gates, four Hadamard, and one 𝑍 gate [ 3206 , Fig. 10.16]. ⊲ Evolution under stabilizer Hamiltonian [ 3207 ]. ⊲ Four CNOT and five CPHASE gates [ 3208 ]. ⊲ Reinforcement-learning discovery of logical-state-preparation circuits [ 3108 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant logical one and log-ical minus state preparation in all-to-all and 2D grid connectivity [3108].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ A non-Pauli Hadamard-phase "facet" gate 𝑆𝐻 and three-qubit Clifford operation 𝑀 3 [701 ,702 ]. These realize the 2𝑇 binary tetrahedral subgroup of 𝑆𝑈 (2).

⊲ The entire logical Clifford group can be realized using fold-transversal gates [ 686 , 770 , 771 ]. ⊲ The code does not admit any non-Clifford › p. 244 transversal gates [ 426 ]; in particular, see [ 772 ] for the case of collective 𝑍 rotations. ⊲ Transversal gates can be in-terpreted as monodromies under a particular notion of parallel transport [773, Exam. 6.4.2].  

> GATES

⊲ Magic-state distillation protocol [ 658 ]. One protocol distills the state |𝑅 ⟩ = cos 𝛽 |0⟩ + 𝑒 i 𝜋 /4 sin 𝛽 |1⟩, with cos (2𝛽 ) = 1/√3, using the fact that a transversal Clifford gate 𝑅 is a gadget for the code; the protocol projects five noisy |𝑅 ⟩ states onto the code space and suppresses the output error to 𝑂 ( 𝑝 2) for independent input error probability 𝑝 [ 381 , Sec. 13.5.3, Protocol 13.5]. ⊲ Pieceable fault-tolerant CZ, CNOT, and 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gates [770].  

> DECODING

⊲ Ideal transversal computational-basis measurement distinguishes logical basis states by the parity of the outcome string, but this is not a fault-tolerant measurement gadget because a single faulty measurement bit can flip the decoded logical outcome [ 381 ,Sec. 11.4]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction circuits [ 3204 ,3209 ]. ⊲ Syndrome extraction circuit optimized for a linear qubit architecture [ 3210 ]. ⊲ Combined dynamical decoupling and error correction protocol on individually-controlled qubits with always-on Ising couplings [ 3208 ]. ⊲ Syndrome extraction circuit using only CNOT-SWAP gates [ 3211 ]. ⊲ Symmetric decoder correcting all weight-one Pauli errors. The resulting logical error channel after coherent noise has been explicitly derived [ 3212 ]. ⊲ Inspired by the honeycomb Floquet code, various weight-two measurement schemes have been designed [3213].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Pieceable fault-tolerant CZ, CNOT, and 𝐶𝐶𝑍 

gates [ 770 ]. ⊲ A fault-tolerant logical 𝑇 gate can be obtained by en-coding the five-qubit code’s five physical qubits into the five logical qubits of a ⟦31 , 5, 3⟧ outer quantum divisible CSS code preserved by transversal 𝑇 †; this layered construction can be viewed as a fac-torization of a ⟦31 , 1, 3⟧ triorthogonal code and does not require magic-state distillation [ 730 ]. ⊲ Syndrome measurement can be done with two ancillary flag qubits [ 3122 ]. The depth of syndrome extraction circuits can be lowered by using past syndrome values [ 3214 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant logical one and logical minus state prepa-ration in all-to-all and 2D grid connectivity [ 3108 ]. ⊲ Inspired 349 by the honeycomb Floquet code, various weight-two measurement schemes have been designed [3213].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ NMR: Implementation of perfect error correcting code on 5 spin subsystem of labeled crotonic acid for quantum net-work benchmarking [ 3215 ]. Single-qubit logical gates [ 3216 ]. Magic-state distillation using 7-qubit device [ 3217 ]. ⊲ Superconducting qubits [ 3218 ]. ⊲ Trapped-ion qubits: non-transversal CNOT gate between two logical qubits, including rounds of correction and fault-tolerant primitives such as flag qubits and pieceable fault tolerance, on a 12-qubit device by Quantinuum [ 3219 ]. Real-time magic-state distillation [ 3220 ]. ⊲ Nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond: fault-tolerant single-qubit Clifford operations using two ancillas [ 3221 ]. The fault-tolerant circuit yields better fidelity than the non-fault-tolerant circuit.  

> PARENTS

⊲ Twisted XZZX toric code › p. 466 — Twisted XZZX codes are 2D lattice extensions of the five-qubit perfect code. The five-qubit code is a small twisted XZZX toric code [ 418 , Exam. 11 and Fig. 3][ 419 ,Exam. 3][ 408 , Fig. 1]. Its genus-one double cover is a ⟦10 , 2, 3⟧ toric code [ 416 ][ 419 , Exam. 3]. The base code’s transversal 𝑆𝐻 gate lifts to a logical 𝐶 𝑋 · 𝑆𝑊 𝐴𝑃 gate on that double cover [ 416 ]. ⊲ (5, 1, 2)-convolutional code › p. 331 — The (5, 1, 2)-convolutional code is a 1D lattice extension of the five-qubit perfect code, with the former’s lattice-translation symmetry being the extension of the latter’s cyclic permutation symmetry. The (5, 1, 2)-convolutional code reduces to the five-qubit code for a five-qubit chain and periodic boundary conditions. See Ref. ⟦6, 1, 3⟧ SIX-QUBIT STABILIZER CODE [429, 431] stab_6_1_3  

> DESCRIPTION

A degenerate, non-trivial ⟦6, 1, 3⟧ stabilizer code. It is one of two six-qubit distance-three codes that are unique up to equivalence [ 429 ], with the other code being decomposable and an extension of the five-qubit code [ 431 ][ 433 , ID 87]. The code ad-mits fault-tolerant syndrome extraction using only one ancilla per stabilizer generator measurement. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 68] 

𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑌 𝐼 𝑌 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝑋 𝑍 𝐼 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑌 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝑌 . (230) Stabilizer generators and logical Pauli operators are presented in Refs. [ 431 , 3229 ]. The code is equivalent to the graph code in Ref. [3230].

⟦6, 2, 2⟧ 𝐶 6 CODE [428] stab_6_2_2  

> DESCRIPTION

Error-detecting normal self-dual CSS code on three qubit pairs that encodes a logical qubit pair and detects any error acting on one pair [ 428 ]. In Knill’s 𝐶 4/𝐶 6 architecture, this code is used at the second and higher concatenation levels. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 126] 

𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 . (231) Its logical operators are 𝑋 𝐿 = 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 , 𝑍 𝐿 = 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 , 𝑋 𝑆 =

𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 , and 𝑍 𝑆 = 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 [428].  

> PROTECTION

As a distance-two code, the 𝐶 6 code detects any single-qubit error. In the qubit-pair grouping used by Knill, it detects any error acting on one of the three pairs, and therefore can correct a pair error when its location is already known [428].  

> MAGIC

Various magic-state distillation protocols exist for the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧

qubit code and the 𝐶 6 code in what are known as Meier-Eastin-Knill (MEK) protocols [ 675 ]. For example, the magic-state yield parameter 351 is 𝛾 = log 2 5 ≈ 2.322 for a protocol using the ⟦10 , 2, 2⟧ code [ 674 ,Box 2]; see also [672, Table IV].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Transversal physical Hadamards preserve the codespace because the displayed 𝑋 - and 

𝑍 -check spaces coincide, making this a normal self-dual qubit CSS code [774].  

> GATES

⊲ Fault-tolerant magic-state preparation [3231].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Knill’s 𝐶 4/𝐶 6 architecture uses the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code at the first level and the 𝐶 6 code at higher levels, together with error-correcting teleportation [ 428 ]. That paper gives evidence for post-selected thresholds above 0.03 and extrapolates to 0.06 , while the error-correcting architecture has evidence for a threshold above 0.01 .Later work refined the postselected-threshold analysis [ 3178 , 3179 ](see also Ref. [ 3180 ]). ⊲ Concatenating quantum Hamming codes on top of the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ and 𝐶 6 codes yields fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant space and quasi-polylogarithmic time overheads [ 3123 ]. In the optimized protocol of Ref. [ 3123 ], a level-five 𝐶 4/𝐶 6 code underlies concatenated quantum Hamming codes

This code admits a fault-tolerant circuit relevant to magic-state prepara-tion [434].

⟦6𝑘 + 2, 3𝑘, 2⟧ CAMPBELL-HOWARD CODE [718] campbell_howard  

> DESCRIPTION

Family of ⟦6𝑘 + 2, 3𝑘, 2⟧ qubit stabilizer codes with quasi-transversal 𝐶𝐶𝑍 ⊗𝑘 gates that are relevant to magic-state dis-tillation. In the synthillation framework, these distance-two codes realize batches of logical 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gates using physical 𝑇 gates followed by a Clifford correction.  

> PROTECTION

Detects single-qubit errors.  

> RATE

Encoding rate is 3𝑘 /( 6𝑘 + 2), approaching 1/2 as 𝑘 → ∞ . 

> MAGIC

A total of 𝑟 rounds of magic-state distillation yields a magic-state yield parameter 𝛾 → 1+ as 𝑘, 𝑟 → ∞ . This matches the Bravyi-Haah conjectured lower bound 𝛾 ≥ 1 for concatenated triorthogonal-matrix protocols [659, Sec. VI].     

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Quasi-transversal 

𝐶𝐶𝑍 ⊗𝑘 gates [718].  

> PARENT

⊲ Small-distance qubit stabilizer code › p. 451 — The family has distance 2. 

> CHILD

⊲ ⟦8, 3, 2⟧ Smallest interesting color code › p. 357 — The 

⟦8, 3, 2⟧ code is the 𝑘 = 1 member of the ⟦6𝑘 + 2, 3𝑘, 2⟧ Campbell-Howard family with a quasi-transversal logical 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gate [718].  

> COUSIN

⊲ Triorthogonal code › p. 464 — Campbell-Howard codes arise from the generalized-triorthogonal/quasitransversal 𝐺 -matrix framework, which extends Bravyi-Haah triorthogonal matrices by allowing odd pair and triple overlaps entirely within the logical-row block 𝐾 [718, Appx. D].

⟦7, 1, 3⟧ STEANE CODE [3240, 3241] steane  

> DESCRIPTION

A ⟦7, 1, 3⟧ self-dual CSS code that is the smallest qubit CSS code to correct a single-qubit error [ 431 ]. The code is constructed using the classical binary [7, 4, 3] Hamming code for protecting against both 𝑋 and 𝑍 errors. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 226] 

𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 . (236) The code’s stabilizer generator matrix blocks 𝐻 𝑋 and 𝐻 𝑍 are both the parity-check matrix of the [7, 4, 3] Hamming code. The checks can be thought of as lying on the three trapezoids of the following tiling of the triangle. The Steane code can also be thought of as a code on all corners of a cube except one [ 3107 , 3242 ], and the code’s encoder-respecting form › p. 442 is the graph of the full cube [819]. > PROTECTION

The Steane code is a distance 3 code. It detects errors on 2 qubits, corrects errors on 1 qubit.  

> ENCODING

⊲ Nine CNOT and four Hadamard gates [ 3206 , Fig. 10.14]. 

⊲ Evolution under stabilizer Hamiltonian [ 3207 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant logical zero and logical plus state preparation on all-to-all and 2D grid qubit connectivity [ 3108 ]. ⊲ Parity-check encoding with flag-bridge qubits on a square lattice connectivity [3243].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ The single-qubit Clifford group › p. 244 [725 , 740 ]. More generally, 𝑘 copies of the Steane code form a ⟦7𝑘, 𝑘, 3⟧ code that admits a 𝑘 -fold transversal implementa-tion of the full Clifford group › p. 244 on all 𝑘 logical qubits, showing the tightness of a no-go theorem that requires at least 𝑘 -fold transversal gadgets for the full Clifford group [746].  

> GATES

⊲ Fault-tolerant approximations of arbitrary single-qubit gates [ 3244 , 3245 ]. ⊲ Non-fault-tolerant 𝑇 gate [ 3246 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant logical zero and magic state preparation [ 3247 ]. Magic-state preparation converts unbiased noise into biased noise [ 3248 ]. 

⊲ Because transversal Hadamard acts logically on the code, the Steane code serves as a normal self-dual inner code for magic-state distillation. One routine uses 14 noisy 𝑇 gates and one noisy input magic state to produce one output with cubic error suppression, and it can be pipelined with the ⟦17 , 1, 5⟧ code to obtain fifth-order suppression [ 89 , Sec. I.A]. ⊲ Pieceable fault-tolerant 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gate [770].  

> DECODING

⊲ Shor error correction fidelity calculation [ 3249 – 3251 ]. 

⊲ A [15 , 3] syndrome-measurement code yields a QDS extension that uses the same 15 measurements as five-fold repetition of the 354 three syndrome bits while achieving lower syndrome-decoding error [ 2830 , Fig. 1]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant measurement-free error-correction cycle [3252].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ A fault-tolerant universal gate set can be done via code switching › p. 559 between the Steane code and the ⟦15 , 1, 3⟧ code [696 , 751 , 757 , 3111 , 3112 ]. ⊲ A fault-tolerant universal gate set can be done via code switching › p. 559 between the Steane code and the 

⟦10 , 1, 2⟧ code [ 3090 ]. ⊲ A fault-tolerant logical 𝑇 gate can be ob-tained by encoding the Steane code’s seven physical qubits into the seven logical qubits of a ⟦63 , 7, 3⟧ outer quantum divisible CSS code preserved by transversal 𝑇 † [ 730 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant logical zero and magic state preparation [ 3247 ]. Magic-state preparation converts unbiased noise into biased noise [ 3248 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant logical zero and logical plus state preparation on all-to-all and 2D grid qubit connectivity [ 3108 ]. ⊲ Pieceable fault-tolerant 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gate [ 770 ]. 

⊲ Syndrome measurement can be done with ancillary flag qubits [3122 ] or with no extra qubits [ 3253 ]. The depth of syndrome extrac-tion circuits can be lowered by using past syndrome values [ 3214 ]. 

⊲ Computation of ground-state energy of the hydrogen molecule [3254 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant measurement-free error-correction cycle [3252].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Trapped-ion devices: seven-qubit device in Blatt group [ 3255 ]. Ten-qubit QCCD device by Quantinuum [ 3256 ] realiz-ing repeated syndrome extraction, real-time look-up-table decoding (yielding lower logical SPAM error rate than physical SPAM), and non-fault-tolerant magic-state distillation (see APS Physics Synopsis [3257 ]). Fault-tolerant universal two-qubit gate set using T injection by Monz group [ 3258 ]. Logical CNOT gate and Bell-pair creation be-tween two logical qubits (yielding a logical fidelity higher than phys-ical), including rounds of correction and fault-tolerant primitives such as flag qubits and pieceable fault tolerance, on a 20-qubit de-vice by Quantinuum [ 3219 ]; logical fidelity interval of the combined preparation-CNOT-measurement procedure was higher than that of the unencoded physical qubits. Multiple rounds of Steane error cor-rection [ 3259 ]. Fault-tolerant universal gate set via code switching  

> › p. 559

between the Steane code and the ⟦10 , 1, 2⟧ code [ 3090 ]. Post-selected fault-tolerant logical Bell-state preparation with logical error rates at least 10 times lower than physical rate on a device by Quantinuum [ 499 ]. The quantum Fourier transform on three code blocks [ 3260 ]. Fault-tolerant transversal and lattice-surgery state teleportation protocols as well as Knill error correction [ 3261 ]. Rains shadow enumerators have been measured [ 3262 ]. Inter-block CNOT gates have been characterized via cycle reconstruction [ 3263 ]. Code switching › p. 559 between the Steane code and the ⟦15 , 1, 3⟧ code as well as magic-state preparation and logical Bell measurements on the Steane code realized on the 28-qubit H2-1 device by Quantinuum [3113 ]. End-to-end fault-tolerant execution of QAOA and HHL cir-cuits, including logical non-Clifford operations, with up to 12 logical qubits on Quantinuum systems [3264]. 

⊲ Neutral atom arrays: Lukin group. Ten logical qubits, transversal CNOT gate performed, logical ten-qubit GHZ state ini-tialized with break-even fidelity, and fault-tolerant logical two-qubit GHZ state initialized [ 3265 ]. Deep-circuit protocols with dozens of logical qubits and hundreds of logical teleportations [3114].

⟦8, 3, 2⟧ SURFACE CODE ON A CUBE [3095] cubic_surface  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Landahl plucky code ⊲ Cubic surface code  

> DESCRIPTION

An ⟦8, 3, 2⟧ twist-defect surface code whose qubits lie on the vertices of a cube. It is obtained by three-coloring the faces of a cube and placing 𝑋 , 𝑌 , and 𝑍 stabilizer generators on each pair of faces of the same color. Its non-CSS nature is due to twist defects [422] stemming from the geometry of the polytope. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 6851] 

𝐼 𝑌 𝑌 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝑌 𝑌 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑌 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑌 . (248)

⟦9, 1, 3⟧ SHOR CODE [3] shor_nine  

> DESCRIPTION

Nine-qubit CSS code › p. 544 that is the first quantum error-correcting code [ 433 , ID 8802]. Among indecomposable ⟦9, 1, 3⟧ CSS codes, the Shor code has the largest automorphism group [434]. A set of logical codewords is 

|0⟩ = 12√2 (| 000 ⟩ + | 111 ⟩) ⊗3

|1⟩ = 12√2 (| 000 ⟩ − | 111 ⟩) ⊗3 .

(249) A stabilizer tableau for the code is 

𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 . (250) The encoder-respecting form › p. 442 of the Shor code is a star-shaped tree graph [ 819 ]. The code works by concatenating › p. 380 each qubit of a phase-flip repetition code › p. 429 with a bit-flip repetition code › p. 429 .Therefore, the code can correct both types of errors simultaneously. The code is degenerate: for example, two 𝑍 errors in the same three-qubit block act identically on all codewords [381, Ch. 3].  

> PROTECTION

The code detects two-qubit errors or corrects an arbi-trary single-qubit error. Since it corrects the single-qubit Pauli er-rors, linearity implies that it corrects arbitrary single-qubit errors and corresponding single-qubit error channels [ 381 , Ch. 2]. It also corrects two-qubit AD › p. 508 errors [3169].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Fault-tolerant logical zero and logical plus state prepa-ration using reinforcement learning [ 3108 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant measurement-free logical-zero state preparation [3280].  

> DECODING

⊲ Bit- and phase-flip circuits utilize CNOT and Hadamard gates [3206, Fig. 10.6].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Fault-tolerant logical zero and logical plus state preparation using reinforcement learning [ 3108 ]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant measurement-free logical-zero state preparation [3280].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Trapped-ion qubits: state preparation with 98.8(1)% and 98.5(1)% fidelity for state |0⟩ and |1⟩, respectively, by N. Linke group [ 3281 ]. Variants of the code to handle coherent noise studied and realized by K. Brown and C. Monroe groups [ 3282 ]. ⊲ Optical systems: quantum teleportation of information implemented by J.-W. Pan group on a maximally entangled pair of one physical and one logical qubit with a fidelity of up to 78.6% [ 3283 ]. All-photonic quantum repeater architecture tested on the same code [3284].

⟦9, 1, 3⟧ SURFACE-17 CODE [3287] surface-17  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ ⟦9, 1, 3⟧ rotated surface code  

> DESCRIPTION

A ⟦9, 1, 3⟧ rotated surface code named for the sum of its 9 data qubits and 8 syndrome qubits. It is one of the four inequivalent CSS gauge fixings of the nine-qubit Bacon-Shor code [ 434 ]. It uses the smallest number of qubits to perform fault-tolerant error correction on a surface code with parallel syndrome extraction. A stabilizer tableau for the code is given by [433, ID 8519]. 

𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 𝑋 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 . (251) The code is depicted in Fig. 63 › p. 359 .

Independent correction of single-qubit 𝑋 and 𝑍 errors. Correction for some two-qubit 𝑋 and 𝑍 errors. Admits pseudo-thresholds › p. 315 of ≈ 10 −4 under depolarizing noise.

> DECODING

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Measurement-free fault-tolerant logical zero state preparation in nearest-neighbor qubit connectivity [ 3280 ].

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Implemented at ETH Zurich by the Wallraff group [3289 ] and on the Zuchongzhi 2.1 superconducting quantum pro-cessor [ 3290 ]. Both experimental error rates are above the pseudo-threshold › p. 315 for this code relative to a single qubit; see Physics viewpoint for a summary [ 3291 ]. Magic states have been created on the latter processor [ 3292 ]. Lattice surgery on the surface-17 code has been realized by splitting the code into two repetition codes by the Wallraff group [ 3293 ]. The device noise can be used to develop a decoder without relying on a theoretical noise model [3294].

⟦𝑘 + 4, 𝑘, 2⟧ H CODE [3305] quantum_h  

> DESCRIPTION

Family of ⟦𝑘 + 4, 𝑘, 2⟧ self-dual CSS codes (for even 𝑘 )with transversal Hadamard gates that are relevant to magic state distillation. The four stabilizer generators are 𝑋 1 𝑋 2 𝑋 3 𝑋 4, 𝑍 1 𝑍 2 𝑍 3 𝑍 4,

𝑋 1 𝑋 2 𝑋 5 𝑋 6 ...𝑋 𝑘 +4, and 𝑍 1 𝑍 2 𝑍 5 𝑍 6 ...𝑍 𝑘 +4. 

> PROTECTION

Detects weight-one Pauli errors. The 𝑟 -level concate-nated H code detects Pauli errors up to weight 2𝑟 − 1. 

> RATE

The H codes are dense, i.e., the rate 𝑘 𝑘 +4 → 1 as 𝑘 → ∞ . The distance is 2. However an 𝑟 -level concatenation of H codes gives a distance of 2𝑟 . 

> MAGIC

A total of 𝑟 rounds of magic-state distillation yields a magic-state yield parameter 𝛾 → 1+ as 𝑘, 𝑟 → ∞ ; see [ 674 , Box 2]. This matches the Bravyi-Haah conjectured lower bound 𝛾 ≥ 1 for con-catenated triorthogonal-matrix protocols [659, Sec. VI].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Hadamard and 𝑇 𝑋𝑇 †

gates, with the latter Clifford-equivalent to Hadamard, and where 

𝑇 = exp (𝑖𝜋 (𝐼 − 𝑍 )/ 8) is the 𝜋 /8-rotation gate.  

> GATES

⊲ The H codes can be used for high-quality and high-efficiency magic-state distillation [ 3305 ]. Their associated multi-level magic-state protocols have an efficiency advantage over the 10-to-2 and 15-to-1 protocols for output error below 10 −7.

is the 𝐶 6 code.

𝐷 -DIMENSIONAL TWISTED TORIC CODE [61, 3309–3311]  

> higher_dimensional_toric
> DESCRIPTION

Extension of the Kitaev toric code to higher-dimensional lattices with regular or shifted (a.k.a. twisted) boundary conditions. Such boundary conditions yield qubit geometries that are tori R𝐷 /Λ, where Λ is an arbitrary 𝐷 -dimensional lattice. Picking a hypercubic lattice yields the ordinary 

𝐷 -dimensional toric code. It is conjectured that appropriate twisted boundary conditions yield multi-dimensional toric code families with sublinear distance scaling of 𝑛 1− 𝜖 for any 𝜖 > 0 and logarithmic-weight stabilizer generators [ 714 , 3311 ]. At finite 𝑛 , twisting boundary conditions can reduce qubit overhead for a fixed distance [714].  

> PROTECTION

In two dimensions, different choices for the periodic boundary conditions yield higher-rate codes with parameters ⟦𝐿 2 +

1, 2, 𝐿 ⟧ for odd 𝐿 [61 ], and ⟦𝐿 2, 2, 𝐿 ⟧ for even 𝐿 [3310 ]. Cyclic analogs of toric codes with parameters ⟦𝑡 2 + ( 𝑡 + 1)2, 1, 2𝑡 + 1⟧ are constructed in [ 418 ]. Some higher-dimensional toric codes protect against burst errors [3312].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Entangled logical states can be prepared by single-shot techniques [714] for twisted toric codes.  

> GATES

⊲ Higher-dimensional toric codes can admit a cup product structure and can thus have logical gates in the Clifford hierarchy  

> › p. 435

implemented by constant-depth Clifford circuits › p. 244 [1470].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Homological code › p. 400 ⊲ Lattice stabilizer code › p. 551  

> CHILD

⊲ Toric code › p. 461 — The 𝐷 -dimensional twisted toric code reduces to the toric code for 𝐷 = 2 and a square lattice.  

> COUSINS

⊲ Qubit QLDPC code › p. 439 — It is conjectured that appro-priate twisted boundary conditions yield multi-dimensional toric code families with sublinear distance scaling of 𝑁 1− 𝜖 for any 𝜖 > 0

and logarithmic-weight stabilizer generators [ 3311 ]. Assuming this conjecture, Hastings’ weight-reduction construction yields QLDPC families with distance Θ∗ (𝑁 1− 𝜖 ) for any 𝜖 > 0 [2899 ]. ⊲ Higher-dimensional homological product code › p. 399 — The non-twisted 𝐷 -dimensional planar and toric codes on a hypercubic lattice can be obtained from a hypergraph product of 𝐷 repetition codes [1565]. 

𝑘 -ORTHOGONAL CODE [642, 669, 758] quantum_k-orthogonal  

> DESCRIPTION

Qubit stabilizer code whose 𝑋 -type logicals and genera-tors form a 𝑘 -orthogonal matrix (defined below) in the symplectic representation › p. 442 . In other words, the overlap between any 𝑘 𝑋 -type code-preserving Paulis (including the identity) is even. The original definition is for qubit CSS codes [ 642 ], but it can be extended to more general qubit stabilizer codes [ 758 , Def. 1]. This entry is formulated for qubits, but an extension exists for modular qudits [642]. A matrix is 𝑘 -orthogonal [758, Def. 4] if 

|𝑥 1 | ≡ 0 mod 2 (255) 

|𝑥 1 · 𝑥 2 | ≡ 0 mod 2 (256) 

|𝑥 1 · 𝑥 2 · 𝑥 3 | ≡ 0 mod 2 (257) 

... (258) 

|𝑥 1 · 𝑥 2 · 𝑥 3 · . . . · 𝑥 𝑘 | ≡ 0 mod 2 (259) for all its rows 𝑥 𝑗 , where the generalized dot-product notation means a sum of products of the respective coordinates of all vectors.  

> PARENT

⊲ Qubit stabilizer code › p. 441  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Quantum pin code › p. 427 — Quantum pin codes are ℓ-orthogonal, i.e., the overlap between any ℓ stabilizers is even [ 669 ]. 

⊲ Triorthogonal code › p. 464 — 𝑘 -orthogonal codes reduce to triorthog-onal codes for 𝑘 = 3. 

> COUSINS

⊲ Modular-qudit lattice color code › p. 480 — The notion of 𝑘 -orthogonality can be extended to modular-qudit codes and is known as 𝑘 ★-orthogonality [ 642 , Def. 2]. Modular-qudit lattice color codes defined on lattices in 𝐷 spatial dimension whose 𝑋 -type stabilizers are placed on cells of dimension 𝜈 ≤ 𝐷 are 𝑘 ★-orthogonal for all 𝑘 ≤

𝜈 [ 642 , Lemma 5]. ⊲ ⟦2𝑟 −1, 1, 3⟧ simplex code › p. 339 — ⟦2𝑟 −1, 1, 3⟧

simplex codes are (𝑟 − 1)-orthogonal [758, Lemma 2]. 

2D BOSONIZATION CODE [386] 2d_bosonization  

> DESCRIPTION

A mapping between a 2D lattice quadratic Hamiltonian of Majorana modes and a 2D lattice of qubits. The original exact 2D bosonization code [ 386 ] is a stabilizer code whose generators are products of plaquettes and stars of the surface code, with gauge con-straints that project onto a toric-code-like subspace with emergent fermions [ 386 , 387 ]. Finite-depth generalized local unitary Clifford circuits generate a family of equivalent local encodings with qubit-to-fermion ratio 𝑟 = 1 + 12𝑘 for any positive integer 𝑘 ; the square-lattice compact encoding with 𝑟 = 1.5 and the super-compact encoding with 𝑟 = 1.25 are explicit examples [387].  

> PROTECTION

The original code [ 386 ] can be converted via Clifford operations into codes whose distance runs up to 7 while preserving the code rate [3313].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Tensor-network realization [ 3314 ], extended to periodic boundary conditions and sectors of odd fermionic charge [3315].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Bosonization code › p. 371 ⊲ 2D lattice stabilizer code

— The 2D bosonization code encodes fermionic modes into a 2D qubit stabilizer code.  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Ball-Verstraete-Cirac (BVC) code › p. 369 — The BVC code can be obtained from exact 2D bosonization by finite-depth gen-eralized local unitaries after regrouping Majorana modes [ 387 ]. 

⊲ Derby-Klassen (DK) code › p. 384 — On the square lattice, the DK code is the 𝑟 = 1.5 exact-bosonization construction after finite-depth generalized local unitaries and re-pairing of Majorana modes [ 387 ]. ⊲ Majorana loop stabilizer code (MLSC) › p. 417 — The MLSC on a square lattice can be obtained from exact 2D bosonization by finite-depth generalized local unitaries [ 387 ]. ⊲ Super-compact fermion-to-qubit code › p. 459 — The super-compact code is obtained from exact 2D bosonization by finite-depth generalized local uni-taries [387].  

> COUSINS

2D COLOR CODE [411, 677] 2d_color  

> DESCRIPTION

Color code defined on a graph embedded in a two-dimensional surface. Each face hosts two stabilizer generators, a Pauli-𝑋 and a Pauli-𝑍 string acting on all the qubits of the face. Most translation-invariant color codes are defined on trivalent planar graphs with three-colorable faces. The three admissible uniform tilings are the 6.6.6 (honeycomb) tiling, the 4.8.8 (square octagon) tiling, and the 4.6.12 tiling [ 413 , Fig. 1]. Non-uniform tilings include the [4.6.8, 6.8.8] and [4.6.8, 4.8.12] tilings [ 385 ]. More general admissible tilings can be obtained via a fattening procedure [ 411 ]; see also a construction based on the more general quantum pin codes [669]. Logical dimension is determined by the genus of the underlying surface (for closed surfaces) and the types of boundaries (for open surfaces). There are six basic boundary types: three color bound-aries corresponding to the three face colors [ 455 ] and three Pauli boundaries corresponding to the three Pauli labels [425]. String operators are defined on paths along edges of the qubit lattice. These paths can have branching points. Each path has two string operators, one corresponding to the 𝑋 basis and one corre-sponding to the 𝑍 basis. In correspondence with the coloring of the lattice faces, string operators also come in three colors. A string of one color must end in a boundary of that same color.  

> RATE

For general 2D manifolds, 𝑘 𝑑 2 ≤ 𝑐 (log 𝑘 )2𝑛 for some constant 

𝑐 in what can be thought of as an extension of the BPT bound › p. 551 

to codes on hyperbolic geometries [ 799 ], meaning that color codes with finite rate can only achieve an asymptotic minimum distance that is logarithmic in 𝑛 . 

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ CNOT gate because the code is CSS. ⊲ Hadamard gates for any qubit geometry which yields a self-dual CSS code. ⊲ Certain triangular 2D color codes on suitably chosen lattices admit transversal implementations of the full Clifford group, including 𝐻 , 𝑆 †, and 𝐶𝑁𝑂𝑇 , without selective addressing [677].  

> GATES

⊲ Magic-state distillation protocols [ 3317 ]. ⊲ Non-clifford gates can be implemented via code switching › p. 559 [3317].  

> DECODING

⊲ Projection decoder of 𝑂 (𝑛 4) complexity [ 3318 ], mod-ified to account for syndrome errors [ 3319 ]. ⊲ Exact minimum-weight decoding is 𝑁 𝑃 -hard for 2D color codes, including for solely Pauli-𝑍 noise [ 3320 , 3321 ]. ⊲ Chromöbius, an open-source imple-mentation of the Möbius decoder, works for many 2D color codes [3322 ]. ⊲ Concatenated MPWM decoder [ 3323 ]. ⊲ Syndrome extraction circuits based on superdense coding and a middle-out strategy [3322].

⊲ Abelian quantum-double stabilizer code › p. 474 — When treated as ground states of the code Hamiltonian, states of the color code on a torus geometry realize Z2 × Z2 topological order [ 2763 ], equivalent to the phase realized by two copies of the toric code (i.e., the surface code on a torus) via a local constant-depth Clifford circuit › p. 244 [ 403 ]. This process can be viewed as an ungauging [ 216 , 442 –450 ] of certain symmetries.

2D DA COLOR CODE [2459] da_color_2d  

> DESCRIPTION

A 2D dynamical code constructed aperiodically that utilizes measurement sequences to encode logical information with automorphisms of the 2D color code. The code is assembled from short measurement sequences that can realize all 72 automorphisms of the 2D color code. On a stack of 𝑁 triangular patches with a Pauli boundary, the code encodes 𝑁 logical qubits. The measurement sequence cycles the instantaneous stabilizer group (ISG) through different stabilizer groups, where certain mea-surement rounds realize the ISG of the 2D color code. The parent topological phase underlying this dynamical code is realized by two copies of the 6.6.6 (honeycomb) color code [2459, Sec. III.A].  

> GATES

⊲ On 𝑁 layers of triangular patches (which encodes 𝑁 logi-cal qubits) with a Pauli boundary , the measurement sequences can implement all Clifford logical gates via a sequence of two- and three-qubit Pauli measurements [2459, Sec. IV.A].  

> PARENT

⊲ Dynamical code › p. 385 — The 2D DA color code is a dynami-cal code with an aperiodic measurement sequence realizing Clifford logical gates.  

> COUSINS

⊲ Honeycomb (6.6.6) color code › p. 402 — The parent topo-logical phase of the 2D DA color code is realized by two copies of the 6.6.6 color code [ 2459 , Sec. III.A]. ⊲ 2D color code › p. 362 — At certain measurement rounds, the 2D DA color code realizes the in-stantaneous stabilizer group (ISG) of the 2D color code [ 2459 , Sec. III.A]. ⊲ Kitaev surface code › p. 410 — One of the instantaneous sta-bilizer groups of the 2D DA color code is that of stacks of surface codes [2459, Sec. III.A]. 

2D HYPERBOLIC SURFACE CODE [3335–3337]  

> two_dimensional_hyperbolic_surface
> DESCRIPTION

Hyperbolic surface codes based on a tessellation of a closed 2D manifold with a hyperbolic geometry (i.e., non-Euclidean geometry, e.g., saddle surfaces when defined on a 2D plane). For a tessellation involving regular polygons with 𝑟 sides and 𝑠 

polygons meeting at each vertex, the number of logical qubits is given by 𝑘 = (1−2/𝑟 −2/𝑠 )𝑛 +2. Some possible tilings include {𝑟, 𝑠 } :

{7, 3}, {5, 4}. The weights of the stabilizer generators depend on the tiling, with {5, 4} having lower weight than {7, 3}.A semi-hyperbolic surface code [3338 ] is a code defined on a {4, 𝑠 }

tiling, but where each square is replaced with a square region of a 2D lattice.  

> PROTECTION

Protects against Pauli errors with distance 𝑑 ∝ log (𝑛 ).Code parameters are ⟦𝑛, (1 − 2/𝑟 − 2/𝑠 )𝑛 + 2, 𝑂 (log 𝑛 )⟧  

> RATE

2D hyperbolic surface codes have an asymptotically constant encoding rate 𝑘 /𝑛 with a distance scaling logarithmically with 𝑛 

when the surface is closed. The encoding rate depends on the tiling 

𝑟, 𝑠 and is given by 𝑘 /𝑛 = (1 − 2/𝑟 − 2/𝑠 ) + 2/𝑛 , which approaches a constant value as the number of physical qubits grows. The weight of the stabilizers is 𝑟 for 𝑍 -checks and 𝑠 for 𝑋 -checks. For open boundary conditions, the code reduces to constant distance.  

> DECODING

⊲ Due to the symmetries of hyperbolic surface codes, optimal measurement schedules of the stabilizers can be found [2548 ]. ⊲ Bounds on code capacity thresholds using ML decoding can be obtained by mapping the effect of noise on the code to a statistical mechanical model [ 3339 ]. ⊲ Two flag-based decoders [3340].  

> CODE CAPACITY THRESHOLD

⊲ Bounds on code capacity thresholds us-ing ML decoding can be obtained by mapping the effect of noise on the code to a statistical mechanical model [ 3341 ]. ⊲ 1.3% for a phenomenological noise model for the {4, 5}-hyperbolic surface code [3338].  

> THRESHOLD

⊲ 1% - 5 % for a 5, 4 tiling under minimum-weight de-coding [ 3342 ]. For larger tilings, the lower bound on the distance decreases, suggesting the threshold will also decrease.  

> NOTES

⊲ See [ 3343 , Sec. III A] for a description of this code. 

⊲ Connection to percolation theory as shown in [ 3344 ]. ⊲ Adatabase of 2D hyperbolic surface codes is available in QECDB [ 745 ], where the surface codes form the subset of non-self-dual codes.

3D COLOR CODE [411] 3d_color  

> DESCRIPTION

Color code defined on a four-valent, four-colorable 3-colex in a 3-manifold. In the original colex realization, qubits sit on vertices, 𝑋 -type stabilizers are attached to 3-cells, and 𝑍 -type stabilizers are attached to faces [411]. For a closed 3-manifold, the code encodes 𝑘 = 3ℎ1 logical qubits, where ℎ1 is the first Betti number [ 411 ]. Logical operators can be represented by colored strings and colored membranes. Excitations consist of point-like color charges at cell defects and loop-like color fluxes at face defects; winding a 𝑝 -charge around a 𝑝𝑞 -flux produces a −1 phase [411]. There are 101 different types of boundaries for any uniform tiling [3354 ]; this was shown for the great rhombated cubic honeycomb (a.k.a. cantitruncated cubic honeycomb) uniform tiling, but is valid for general uniform tilings.  

> PROTECTION

On a closed 3-manifold with first Betti number ℎ1, the 3D color code encodes 𝑘 = 3ℎ1 logical qubits [411].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Transversal action of 𝑇 

gates on color codes on general 3-manifolds realizes a 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gate on three logical qubits and is related to a topological invariant that is called the triple intersection number; this gate is related to the fact that this code admits a cup product structure [ 670 ]. ⊲ Transversal 

𝑆 gate on color codes on general 3-manifolds corresponds to a higher-form symmetry [ 670 ]. ⊲ Universal transversal gates can be achieved using lattice surgery or code deformation [ 679 , 680 ]. 

⊲ Families of 3D color codes on quasi-hyperbolic, fibre-bundle, and Torelli mapping-torus 3-manifolds support collective logical 

𝐶𝐶𝑍 gates via transversal 𝑇 and individually addressable, paralleliz-able logical 𝐶𝑍 gates via transversal 𝑆 on codimension-1 submani-folds. Their rate-distance scalings are 𝑂 (1/log 𝑛 ) with 𝑑 = 𝑂 (log 𝑛 ),

𝑂 (1/log 2 𝑛 ) with 𝑑 = Ω (log 2 𝑛 ), and 𝑂 (1) with distance scaling unknown, respectively [670].  

> GATES

⊲ Magic-state distillation protocols [ 3317 ]. ⊲ Non-clifford gates can be implemented via code switching › p. 559 [3317].  

> DECODING

⊲ Decoder that maps 3D color code to three copies of the 3D surface code [3355].

3D DA COLOR CODE [2459] da_color_3d  

> DESCRIPTION

A 3D dynamical code constructed aperiodically that utilizes measurement sequences to encode logical information with automorphisms of the 3D color code. The code represents the first step towards universal quantum computation with dynamical auto-morphism codes. The measurement sequence cycles the instantaneous stabilizer group (ISG) through different stabilizer groups, where certain mea-surement rounds realize the ISG of the 3D color code. The parent topological phase underlying this dynamical code is realized by three copies of the cubic honeycomb color code [2459, Sec. VI.A].  

> GATES

⊲ A non-Clifford logical gate can be realized via adaptive two-qubit measurements [2459, Sec. VII].  

> PARENT

⊲ Dynamical code › p. 385 — The 3D DA color code is a dy-namical code with an aperiodic measurement sequence realizing a non-Clifford logical gate.  

> COUSINS

⊲ Cubic honeycomb color code › p. 383 — The parent topo-logical phase of the 3D DA color code is realized by three copies of the cubic honeycomb color code [ 2459 , Sec. VI.A]. ⊲ 3D color code › p. 364 — At certain measurement rounds, the 3D DA color code realizes the instantaneous stabilizer group (ISG) of the 3D color code [2459, Sec. VI.A]. 

3D FERMIONIC SURFACE CODE [601, 3350, 3356, 3357]   

> 3d_fermionic_surface
> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ 3D toric code with emergent fermion 

⊲ Levin-Wen fermion model ⊲ Fermionic-charge bosonic-loop (FcBl) surface code ⊲ Twisted surface code  

> DESCRIPTION

A non-CSS variant of the 3D Kitaev surface code that re-alizes Z2 gauge theory with an emergent fermion, i.e., the fermionic-charge bosonic-loop (FcBl) phase [ 435 ]. The model can be defined on a cubic lattice in several ways [ 436 , Eq. (D45-46)]. Realizations on other lattices also exist [ 437 ], and the phase of this code also exists in the 3D Kitaev honeycomb model [438]. 

3D fermionic toric code often either refers to the construction on the three-dimensional torus or is an alternative name for the general construction. The construction on surfaces with boundaries is often called the 3D fermionic surface code . However, unlike the 3D surface code, an open (a.k.a. rough) boundary is not possible. Twist defects in the form of Kitaev chains can be introduced as in the 2D surface code to store additional logicals [3351, 3352].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ 𝐶𝐶𝑍 and 𝐶𝑆 gates can be obtained for the fermionic 3D surface code on certain manifolds by circuits that can be interpreted as moving and spreading lattice realizations of Kitaev chain and 𝑝 + 𝑖 𝑝 defects [681].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Qubit QLDPC code › p. 439 ⊲ 3D lattice stabilizer code  

> › p. 543

⊲ Abelian topological code › p. 292 — The 3D fermionic sur-face code realizes 3D Z2 gauge theory with fermionic charge and bosonic loop excitations (FcBl), i.e., with an emergent fermion. The fermionic excitations endow the code with an anomalous two-form symmetry, which is argued to induce a non-trivial finite-temperature topological order [2455]. ⊲ Walker-Wang model code › p. 567 — The 3D fermionic surface code is a Walker-Wang model code with pre-modular input category C = sVec consisting of a trivial anyon and a fermion.  

> COUSINS

⊲ 3D surface code › p. 366 — The 3D (fermionic) surface code is a CSS (non-CSS) code which realizes a Z2 gauge theory in 3D (with an emergent fermion). Two copies of the 3D fermionic surface code are equivalent to a copy of the 3D surface code and a copy of the 3D fermionic surface code via anyon relabeling: the two incom-ing fermions, 𝑓 1 and 𝑓 2, can be re-organized into a boson 𝑓 1 𝑓 2 and fermion 𝑓 2. ⊲ Kitaev chain code › p. 409 — The 3D fermionic surface code is the result of applying the 3D bosonization mapping to a trivial fermionic theory [ 3351 ]. 3D SURFACE CODE [460, 3358] 3d_surface  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ 3D toric code ⊲ 3D cubic code ⊲ Bosonic-charge bosonic-loop (BcBl) surface code  

> DESCRIPTION

A generalization of the Kitaev surface code defined on a 3D cubic lattice. Qubits are placed on edges, 𝑍 -type stabilizer gener-ators are placed on square plaquettes oriented in all three directions, and 𝑋 -type stabilizers are placed on the six edges neighboring every vertex [439]. 

3D toric code often either refers to the construction on the three-dimensional torus or is an alternative name for the general con-struction. The construction on surfaces with boundaries is often called the 3D planar code . In the open-boundary hypercubic family of [ 3082 ], setting one linear dimension of the tesseract construction to 1 yields a single-qubit cubic code that interpolates between the planar surface code and the 4D tesseract code. There exists a rotated version of the 3D surface code, the 3D rotated surface code , akin to the (2D) rotated surface code [ 2550 ]. The welded surface code [2943 ]consists of several 3D surface codes stitched together in a way that the distance scales faster than the linear size of the system. In the rectified picture, three 3D surface codes can be supported on the same rectified cubic lattice, and the corresponding cubic-lattice realization is a gauge choice of the 3D Bacon-Shor code [682]. Related models [ 411 , 3359 ] on lattices with certain colorability are equivalent to several copies of the 3D surface code [436].  

> PROTECTION

The planar 3D surface code family on a cubic lattice of length 𝐿 has parameters ⟦2𝐿 (𝐿 − 1)2 + 𝐿 3, 1, 𝑑 𝑋 = 𝐿 2, 𝑑 𝑍 = 𝐿 ⟧,while the 3D toric code has parameters ⟦3𝐿 3, 3, 𝑑 𝑋 = 𝐿 2, 𝑑 𝑍 =

𝐿 ⟧. Rectangular open-boundary 3D versions furnish single-qubit 

⟦71 , 1, 6⟧, ⟦177 , 1, 9⟧, ⟦331 , 1, 12 ⟧, and ⟦616 , 1, 16 ⟧ codes, illustrating an 𝑛 ∝ 3𝑑 2 tradeoff between the 2D surface and 4D tesseract families [3082]. Stability against Hamiltonian perturbations was determined us-ing a tensor-network representation [ 2765 ]. The phase diagram of the perturbed tensor network maps to that of a 3D Ising gauge the-ory.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ For a stack of three 3D surface codes on the same rectified cubic lattice, pairwise logical 

𝐶𝑍 and triple logical 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gates are transversal [682].

|𝑢 ⟩ + | 𝑢 ⟩. In particular, the paper uses nonlinear Constantin-Rao and related Varshamov-Tenengol’ts codes, and also a binary-to-ternary mapping to obtain improved families for short block lengths.

V.B]. ⊲ While check operators are few-body, stabilizer weights scale with the number of qubits, and stabilizer expectation values are obtained by taking products of gauge-operator expecta-tion values. It is thus not clear how to extract stabilizer values in a fault-tolerant manner [ 509 , 3378 ]. ⊲ Autonomous QEC [ 3379 ]. 

⊲ Applying a period-four measurement schedule to the original Bacon-Shor code yields a numerical threshold under circuit-level noise [3372].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Fault-tolerant teleportation-based computation scheme for asymmetric Bacon-Shor codes that is effective against highly biased noise [ 2565 ]. ⊲ Pieceably fault-tolerant circuits can be employed to construct non-transversal gates effectively [3373].  

> CODE CAPACITY THRESHOLD

⊲ The number of check operators scales sublinearly with system size, so the Bacon-Shor codes alone do not exhibit a topological threshold in the 𝑚 1, 𝑚 2 → ∞ limit [ 3380 ]. However, a threshold can be obtained from concatenated Bacon-Shor codes that are further restricted to planar geometries, whose recovery circuit is a subset of a circuit used by a larger bona-fide Bacon-Shor code [ 3381 ]. This threshold differs from a concatenated threshold › p. 435 in that there are no long-range connectivity require-ments. ⊲ Lower bounds for the concatenated threshold › p. 435 of various small Bacon-Shor codes are tabulated in [683, Table I].

BALL-VERSTRAETE-CIRAC (BVC) CODE [3385, 3386] bvc  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Verstraete-Cirac code ⊲ Auxiliary fermion code  

> DESCRIPTION

A 2D fermion-into-qubit encoding that builds upon the JW transformation by eliminating the weight-𝑂 (𝑛 ) non-local 𝑍 -type string at the expense of introducing an auxiliary qubit per site and local gauge constraints. See [387, Sec. IV.B] for details.  

> PROTECTION

Some single-qubit errors are detectable, with the rest inducing low-weight fermionic dephasing noise [3387].  

> PARENTS

⊲ 2D bosonization code › p. 361 — The BVC code can be ob-tained from exact 2D bosonization by finite-depth generalized local unitaries after regrouping Majorana modes [ 387 ]. ⊲ Quantum error-transmuting code (QETC) › p. 315 — The BVC code transmutes all single-qubit errors [2896].  

> COUSIN

⊲ Rotated surface code › p. 448 — An appropriately chosen stabilizer generator set for the BVC code contains the stabilizers of the rotated surface code [3333].

⟦30 , 4, 4⟧ and ⟦48 , 4, 6⟧ [390].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Circuit-level simulations in [ 390 ] use BP-OSD for BB5 and BB6 instances under an ion-chain noise model. ⊲ For physical error rate 10 −3, the ⟦48 , 4, 7⟧ BB5 instance achieves logical error rate per syndrome round and per logical qubit ≈ 5 × 10 −5,about 4× lower than the best BB6 baseline considered in [ 390 ]. In that comparison, it also matches the logical error rate of a distance-7 surface code while using about 4× fewer physical qubits per logical qubit. 370

BINARIZED-AND-CONCATENATED (B&C) PHANTOM CODE [489]  

> bc_phantom
> DESCRIPTION

Member of a family of 𝑘 = 2 CSS phantom codes ob-tained from a 𝑞 = 4 Galois-qudit CSS code by binarizing each F4

qudit into two qubits and then concatenating each qubit pair with the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code [489]. The construction starts from a ⟦𝑛, 1, 𝑑 ⟧4 CSS code satisfying a condition that realizes the Frobenius transform 𝛾 ↦ → 𝛾 2 by a co-ordinate permutation; together with field multiplication 𝛾 ↦ → 𝛼𝛾 ,this supplies all GL (2, F2) transformations on the two binary com-ponents of the logical F4 qudit after concatenation. Binarization uses the self-dual normal basis {𝜔, 𝜔 2 } of F4. The subsequent 

⟦4, 2, 2⟧ layer maps a single F4-qudit Pauli to four-qubit Paulis, e.g., 𝑋 𝜔 ↦ → 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 𝐼 , 𝑋 𝜔 2

↦ → 𝑋 𝐼 𝑋 𝐼 , 𝑋 1 ↦ → 𝐼 𝑋 𝑋 𝐼 , and similarly 

𝑍 𝜔 2

↦ → 𝐼 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 , 𝑍 𝜔 ↦ → 𝐼 𝑍 𝐼 𝑍 , 𝑍 1 ↦ → 𝐼 𝑍 𝑍 𝐼 [489].  

> PROTECTION

A starting ⟦𝑛, 1, 𝑑 ⟧4 CSS code yields a qubit CSS code with parameters ⟦4𝑛, 2, ≥ 2𝑑 ⟧ after binarization and concatenation with the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code [ 489 ]. The inner ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ blocks contribute many weight-four stabilizers, while completing the stabilizer group may require generators whose weight is at least the code distance.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Ordinary CSS self-duality of the starting 𝑞 = 4 Galois-qudit CSS code yields a permutation-assisted logical Hadamard on the resulting qubit code. Hermitian self-duality, meaning that the 𝑍 -type check space is the Frobenius conjugate of the 𝑋 -type check space, additionally yields a logical 𝐶𝑍 gate [489].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Phantom code › p. 422 ⊲ Concatenated qubit code › p. 380 —Each qubit pair obtained by binarizing one F4 qudit is concatenated with the ⟦4, 2, 2⟧ code [489].  

> CHILDREN

BINARY DIHEDRAL PI CODE [3389] binary_dihedral_permutation_invariant  

> DESCRIPTION

Multi-qubit PI code designed to realize gates from the binary dihedral group transversally. Can also be interpreted as a single-spin code. The codespace projection is a projection onto an irrep of the binary dihedral group BD 2𝑁 = ⟨𝜔𝐼, 𝑋, 𝑃 ⟩ of order 8𝑁 ,where 𝜔 is a 2𝑁 th root of unity, and 𝑃 = diag (1, 𝜔 2).The construction includes three families and a handful of particu-lar codes. The first family has parameters (( 2𝑚 + 3, 2, 3)) for 𝑚 not a power of two, realizing binary dihedral transversal gates that are not possible to realize in any qubit stabilizer code [ 3389 , Prop. 1]. The second family is the case of 𝑚 being a power of two, corresponding to (( 2𝑚 −1 + 3, 2, 3)) codes, each realizing a member of the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 transversally. The third family consists of (( 𝑛, 2, 𝑑 )) 

codes with 𝑛 = 14 (3𝑑 2 + 6𝑑 − 7 + 2(𝑑 mod 8)) , realizing 𝑆 and 𝑇 gates transversally. The handful of codes have distance 5 (7, 9, 11, 13) and encode in 27 (49, 73, 107, 147) qubits, all realizing transversal 𝑇 gates.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Binary dihedral group gates can be realized transversally, which include subgroups of any level of the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 and subgroups which cannot be realized by any qubit stabilizer code.  

> PARENT

⊲ PI qubit code › p. 422  

> COUSINS

⊲ Small-distance block quantum code › p. 321 — The first and second families of binary dihedral PI codes have distance three, and the third family has the member (( 27 , 2, 5)) . ⊲ Combinatorial PI code › p. 379 — The 𝑄 3,1,2𝑚 −4,+ and 𝑄 3,1,2𝑚 −4,+ combinatorial PI codes reduce to the (( 2𝑚 + 3, 2, 3)) and (( 2𝑚 −1 + 3, 2, 3)) binary dihedral PI codes, respectively [ 3077 , Prop. 5.6] (see also [ 692 ]). ⊲ XP stabilizer code › p. 468 — Binary dihedral permutation invariant codewords form error spaces of XP stabilizer codes. ⊲ ⟦2𝑟 − 1, 1, 3⟧ simplex code  

> › p. 339

triorthogonal code › p. 347 — The (( 27 , 2, 5)) binary dihedral PI code realizes the 𝑇 gate (strongly) transversally, but requires fewer qubits than the ⟦49 , 1, 5⟧ triorthogonal code. ⊲ Triorthogonal code › p. 464

BIVARIATE BICYCLE (BB) CODE [421] qcga  

> DESCRIPTION

One of several Abelian 2BGA codes which admit time-optimal syndrome measurement circuits that can be implemented in a two-layer architecture, a generalization of the square-lattice architecture optimal for the surface codes. Codes can be classified 371 by the weight of their checks, e.g., by BB 𝑤 where 𝑤 is the check weight. The qubit connectivity graph is not quite a 2D grid and is instead decomposable into two planar subgraphs of degree three; there exists an optimized layout minimizing Euclidean communication distance for check operators [ 3390 ]. There are 𝑛 𝑋 and 𝑍 check operators, with each one of weight six. See Refs. [ 3391 , 3392 ] for examples of self-dual BB codes. Several variants and generalizations exist [ 3393 , 3394 ]. There exist qudit BB codes that achieve 𝑘 𝑑 2/𝑛 = 20 [3395].  

> PROTECTION

Admits an 0.8% pseudo-threshold › p. 315 for circuit-level noise under BP-OSD decoder [421] (cf. [3396]).  

> RATE

When ancilla qubit overhead is included, the encoding rate surpasses that of the surface code. A general ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧ bivariate bicycle code requires 𝑛 ancilla qubits for encoding, meaning that its 

ancilla-added encoding rate is 𝑘 /2𝑛 . 

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Logical Pauli operators and fold-transversal gates studied in Ref. [685, 686].  

> GATES

⊲ Certain bivariate bicycle codes admit a cup product struc-ture and can thus have logical gates in the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 

implemented by constant-depth Clifford circuits [1470].  

> DECODING

⊲ Syndrome extraction circuit requires seven layers of CNOT gates regardless of code length. BP-OSD decoder [ 1200 ] has been extended [ 421 ] to account for measurement errors (i.e., the circuit-based noise model [ 3396 ]). ⊲ The depth-7 syndrome ex-traction schedules studied in Ref. [ 421 ] are not generally distance-preserving › p. 435 ; for the ⟦144 , 12 , 12 ⟧ code, all 936 depth-7 variants obtained by reordering the CNOT layers satisfy 𝑑 circ ≤ 10 < 𝑑 .

⊲ Some long-range check operators can be measured less frequently than others [ 3397 ]. ⊲ Syndrome extraction circuits called morph-ing circuits [3096 ], generalizing circuits for the color code [ 3322 ]. 

⊲ Decoding under circuit-level noise has been studied for the BP, BP+OSD, and AutDEC decoders [ 3110 ]. ⊲ Transformer-based neural-network decoder [3100]. ⊲ Matching decoder [3398].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Fault-tolerant state initialization using lattice surgery techniques [810, 3399] and an ancillary surface code [421].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Superconducting circuits: syndrome extraction has been implemented for the ⟦18 , 4, 4⟧ BB code on a 32-qubit Kunlun device by the Wang, Song, and Deng groups [ 3400 ]. The same is also shown for an ⟦18 , 6, 3⟧ code obtained by removing two check operators from the former code [3400].  

> NOTES

⊲ A database of bivariate bicycle codes is available in QECDB [745].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Generalized homological-product qubit CSS code › p. 393 

⊲ Two-block group-algebra (2BGA) codes › p. 505 — Bivariate bicycle codes are Abelian 2BGA codes over groups of the form Z𝑟 × Z𝑠 .

⊲ Abelian LP code › p. 488 — Bivariate bicycle codes are Abelian LP codes over groups of the form Z𝑟 × Z𝑠 . ⊲ 2D lattice stabilizer code › p. 543 — Bivariate bicycle codes are defined on 2D lattices with periodic boundary conditions, and versions with open boundary con-ditions have been investigated [ 423 , 3401 ]. Bivariate bicycle codes are on par with the surface code in terms of threshold, but admit a much higher ancilla-added encoding rate at the expense of having non-geometrically local weight-six check operators. BB codes have been investigated in terms of their anyons and topological order [2460].

BOSONIZATION CODE [3402–3405] bosonization  

> DESCRIPTION

A mapping that maps a 𝐷 -dimensional lattice quadratic Hamiltonian of Majorana modes into a lattice of qubits. The result-ing qubit code can realize various topological phases, depending on the initial Majorana-mode Hamiltonian and its symmetries. A general mapping for quadratic Hamiltonians was constructed in Ref. [ 3402 ], while others considered higher-order products of Majorana modes that correspond to symmetry constraints [ 3403 ,3404].

BRANCHING MERA CODE [383, 1487, 1488] branching_mera  

> DESCRIPTION

Qubit stabilizer code whose encoding circuit corre-sponds to a branching MERA [ 516 ] tensor network. These codes generalize quantum polar codes by reinstating the disentanglers omitted in the branching-tree tensor-network construction [383].  

> PROTECTION

Numerical evidence indicates that channel polarization rapidly suppresses channels that are bad in both quadratures, allow-ing good performance without entanglement assistance [383].  

> RATE

Numerics on depolarizing and erasure channels indicate low block-error rates at rates approaching coherent information, with better finite-size behavior than quantum polar codes [383].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Encoding uses a reversed branching-MERA CNOT cir-cuit, with non-data inputs frozen to either |0⟩ or |+⟩ according to channel selection [383].  

> DECODING

⊲ Decoding can be formulated as tensor-network contrac-tion and supports successive-cancellation-style decoding inherited 372 from branching-MERA constructions [ 383 , 1487 ]. ⊲ A symmet-ric decoder that jointly uses 𝑥 - and 𝑧 -error information remains efficiently contractible and improves finite-size performance over standard quantum polar decoding [383].  

> PARENT

⊲ EA qubit stabilizer code › p. 387  

> CHILD

⊲ Quantum polar code › p. 427 — Branching MERA codes gener-alize quantum polar codes by restoring the branching-MERA disen-tanglers while retaining efficient tensor-network decoding [383].  

> COUSINS

⊲ Polar code › p. 197 — Classical versions of branching MERA codes can be thought of as extensions of polar codes [ 1487 , 1488 ]. 

⊲ Tensor-network code › p. 324 — Encoders for branching MERA codes are related to branching MERA tensor networks [383, 1487]. 

BRAVYI-BACON-SHOR (BBS) CODE [3232] bravyi_bacon_shor  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Generalized Bacon-Shor code  

> DESCRIPTION

BRAVYI-KITAEV SUPERFAST (BKSF) CODE [530] bksf  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Loop-stabilized fermion simulation (LSFS) code  

> DESCRIPTION

A single-error-detecting fermion-into-qubit encoding defined on a 2D qubit lattice whose stabilizers are associated with loops in the lattice. For the square-lattice edge ordering used in Ref. [387 ], the BKSF logical operators coincide with exact 2D bosoniza-tion on the dual lattice after relabeling 𝑋 and 𝑌 . The code can be generalized to a single error-correcting code (i.e., with distance three) on graphs of degree ≥ 6 [391].  

> PROTECTION

The code can detect single-qubit errors [ 3408 ]. A gener-alized BKSF code has distance 3 on a graph with degree ≥ 6, while original BKSF code cannot correct single-qubit errors on graphs of degree < 6 [391].  

> PARENT

⊲ Majorana loop stabilizer code (MLSC) › p. 417 — The BKSF code can be thought of as a particular MLSC [3408]. 

BRAVYI-KITAEV TRANSFORMATION (BKT) CODE [530] bkt  

> DESCRIPTION

A fermion-into-qubit encoding that maps Majorana op-erators into Pauli strings of weight ⌈log 2 (𝑛 + 1)⌉ . The code can be reformulated in terms of Fenwick trees [ 527 ], and the Pauli-string weight can be further optimized to yield the segmented Bravyi-Kitaev (SBK) transformation code [528] (see also Ref. [529]).  

> NOTES

⊲ Review on the BKT [3409].  

> PARENT

⊲ Fermion-into-qubit code › p. 389  

> COUSINS

⊲ Jordan-Wigner transformation code › p. 408 — The weight of a Majorana operator in the BKT (JW transformation) code scales log-arithmically (linearly) with 𝑛 , with the former demonstrating an ex-ponential improvement [ 3410 ]. ⊲ Ternary-tree fermion-into-qubit code › p. 459 — The ternary-tree fermion-into-qubit code improves over the BKT code by a factor of ≈ 1.58 in the weight of encoded fermionic operators [3410].
