TWISTED XZZX TORIC CODE [418] twisted_xzzx  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ XZZX cyclic code ⊲ Cyclic toric code 

⊲ Generalized toric code (GTC) ⊲ Genus-one genon code  

> DESCRIPTION

A cyclic code that can be thought of as the XZZX toric code with shifted (a.k.a twisted) boundary conditions. Admits a set of stabilizer generators that are equivalent to cyclic shifts of a particular weight-four 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 Pauli string. Codes encode either one or two logical qubits, depending on qubit geometry, and perform well against biased noise [ 2556 ]. See Ref. [ 416 ] for a table of some of these for small instances, where they are called genus-one genon codes.  

> PROTECTION

A family of ⟦𝑎 2 + 𝑏 2, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧ cyclic codes exists for all 

𝑏 > 𝑎 ≥ 1 such that gcd (𝑎, 𝑏 ) = 1 [ 408 , Thm. 3.9]. Here, 𝑘 = 1

(𝑘 = 2) and 𝑑 = 𝑎 + 𝑏 (𝑑 = max (𝑎, 𝑏 )) for odd 𝑛 (even 𝑛 ). The subfamily ⟦𝑑 2 + 1, 2, 𝑑 ⟧ (i.e., 𝑎 = 1, 𝑏 = 𝑑 for odd 𝑑 ) includes 

⟦10 , 2, 3⟧, ⟦26 , 2, 5⟧, ⟦50 , 2, 7⟧, . . . [1269 , Exam. 1]. The subfamily 

⟦𝑡 2 +( 𝑡 +1)2, 1, 2𝑡 +1⟧ (i.e., 𝑎 = 𝑡, 𝑏 = 𝑡 +1) includes ⟦5, 1, 3⟧, ⟦13 , 1, 5⟧,

⟦25 , 1, 7⟧, . . . [1269 , Exam. 4]. Small instances are tabulated in Ref. [ 416 ] as genus-one genon codes. Other types of distances have been considered for this code [2556].  

> DECODING

⊲ Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction circuits using flag qubits [ 2556 ]. ⊲ AMBP4, a quaternary version [ 3636 ] of the MBP decoder [3637]. ⊲ Fault-tolerant BP (FTBP) decoder [4284].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction circuits using flag qubits [2556].  

> CODE CAPACITY THRESHOLD

⊲ Depolarizing noise: 17 .5% under AMBP4 decoding for the ⟦( 𝑚 2 +1)/ 2, 1, 𝑚 ⟧ family [ 3636 , Fig. 10]. ⊲ Biased noise: between 20% and 45% at noise bias ranging from 1 to 10 under MWPM [2556, Fig. 5].  

> THRESHOLD

⊲ Phenomenological noise: between 3% and 10% at noise bias ranging from 1 to 4 under MWPM [2556, Fig. 5].

TWO-FOLIATED FRACTON CODE [447, 4361] two_foliated  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Anisotropic lineon code  

> DESCRIPTION

A type-I fracton code obtained by gauging [ 216 , 442 –450 ] a 3D paramagnet with planar subsystem symmetries in two directions. In that construction, the gauge charges are lineons and the flux excitations are also lineons moving in the same direction, yielding the anisotropic lineon model [447, Sec. 4.1.2].

X-CUBE FLOQUET CODE [4365] floquet_xcube  

> DESCRIPTION

A 3D Floquet code on the truncated cubic honeycomb, built from coupled layers of square-octagon Floquet toric codes. Its original measurement schedule yields ISGs that are stacks of 2D surface codes or are FDLQC-equivalent to the X-cube model code [ 4365 ]. A rewinding period-six schedule 𝐺 𝐵𝑅𝐵𝐺 𝑅 yields only fracton ISGs: the G-round is the canonical X-cube model concate-nated with four-qubit repetition codes on composite green edges, the B- and first R-rounds are FDLQC-equivalent to the product of the X-cube model, a 3D surface code, and a 3-foliated stack of 2D surface codes up to non-local stabilizers, and the second R-round is FDLQC-equivalent to the X-cube model together with a 3-foliated stack of 2D surface codes [ 506 ]. A parent stabilizer code for the rewinding schedule is FDQC-equivalent to a 3-foliated stack of 2D color codes [506].  

> RATE

The original code has subextensive logical dimension [ 4365 ]; for even 𝐿 , the rewinding schedule preserves 6𝐿 − 3 logical qubits on an 𝐿 × 𝐿 × 𝐿 three-torus [506].  

> DECODING

𝐺 𝐵𝑅𝐵𝐺 𝑅 yields ISGs FDLQC-equivalent to the X-cube model to-gether with a 3D surface-code factor and/or a 3-foliated stack of 2D surface codes [506].

X-CUBE MODEL CODE [216] xcube  

> DESCRIPTION

A foliated type-I fracton CSS code on a cubic lattice with qubits on edges, cube stabilizers, and three cross-shaped vertex stabilizers for each vertex [ 216 ]. It supports a subextensive number of logical qubits. In the generalized lattice-gauge-theory construction of Ref. [ 216 ], the X-cube model is the quantum dual of the 3D plaquette Ising model in a transverse field. Its fundamental excitations include immobile fractons created at the corners of membrane operators and dimension-1 quasiparticles, i.e., lineons in later terminology, created at the ends of straight Wilson lines [ 216 ]. On an 𝐿 𝑥 × 𝐿 𝑦 × 𝐿 𝑧 

three-torus, the ground-state degeneracy is 22𝐿 𝑥 +2𝐿 𝑦 +2𝐿 𝑧 −3, reflect-ing the model’s subextensive encoding rate [216]. Variants include several generalized X-cube models [ 1454 ]. A non-stabilizer commuting-projector code constructed by stacking layers of the double-semion string-net model, called the semionic X-cube model [ 507 ], is equivalent to the X-cube model [ 4361 ] (see also Refs. [3876, 4366]).  

> DECODING

⊲ Parallelized matching decoder [3422].  

> CODE CAPACITY THRESHOLD

⊲ Independent 𝑋, 𝑍 noise: minimum threshold ≈ 7.5% , higher than those reported for the 3D surface code and color code [3423].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Qubit CSS code › p. 436 ⊲ Qubit QLDPC code › p. 439 

⊲ Qudit X-cube model code › p. 484 — The qudit X-cube model code reduces to the X-cube model code for 𝑞 = 2. The X-cube model is a foliated type-I fracton code [436, 4367].  

> COUSINS

XP STABILIZER CODE [762] xp_stabilizer  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Weighted hypergraph code  

> DESCRIPTION

The XP Stabilizer formalism is a generalization of the XS and Pauli stabilizer formalisms, with stabilizer generators taken from the group BD ⊗𝑛  

> 2𝑁

= ⟨𝜔𝐼, 𝑋, 𝑃 ⟩⊗𝑛 , which is the tensor product of the binary dihedral group of order 8𝑁 . Here, 𝑁 is called the precision ,

𝜔 is a 2𝑁 th root of unity, and 𝑃 = diag (1, 𝜔 2). The codespace is a 

+1 eigenspace of a set of XP stabilizer generators, which need not commute to define a valid codespace. XP stabilizer states are in one-to-one correspondence with weighted hypergraph states [ 732 , 762 ], which generalize both weighted graph states [ 3456 , 3469 , 3470 ] and hypergraph states [ 3471 –3473 ]. XP stabilizer codes are classified into XP-regular and XP-non-regular, where the former admits logical dimension 𝐾 = 2𝑘 (for some integer 𝑘 ) and can be mapped to a CSS code with the same diagonal logical operators and similar non-diagonal logical opera-tors, while the latter can have arbitrary dimension, are non-additive, and resemble CWS codes [ 762 ]. Measurement of diagonal Pauli op-erators can be classically simulated efficiently on any XP code, but estimating outcome probabilities for general precision-4 XP opera-tors is NP-complete and measurement can take one outside the XP formalism [762].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Initialization of all qubits in the |+⟩ state and action of generalized controlled 𝑍 gates on multi-edges of the underlying hypergraph [732, 762].  

> PARENT

⊲ Clifford-hierarchy stabilizer code › p. 375 — XP stabilizer codes are joint eigenspaces of operators in the binary dihedral group, a subgroup consisting of Pauli strings and elements of a level of the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 . 

> CHILDREN

⊲ XS stabilizer code › p. 469 — The XP stabilizer formalism reduces to the XS formalism at 𝑁 = 4. ⊲ Qubit stabilizer code  

> › p. 441

— XP stabilizer codes reduce to qubit stabilizer codes for 𝑁 = 2. 

> COUSINS

⊲ Qubit CSS code › p. 436 — Each XP-regular code can be mapped to a CSS code with the same diagonal logical operators and similar non-diagonal logical operators [ 762 ]. ⊲ Codeword stabi-lized (CWS) code › p. 378 — The orbit representatives of XP codes play a similar role to the word operators of CWS codes, and non-XP-regular codes have a similar structure [ 762 ]. ⊲ Tensor-network code › p. 324 

— XP stabilizer codes can be understood through the Quantum Lego formalism [ 750 ]. ⊲ Cubic theory code › p. 383 — The cubic theory code can be embedded into a larger codespace such that all diago-nal logical operators are represented by XP operators [ 731 , Sec. 4.3]. 

⊲ Chen-Hsin invertible-order code › p. 374 — The Chen-Hsin invertible-order code can be embedded into a larger codespace such that all diagonal logical operators are represented by XP operators [ 731 , Sec. 4.3]. ⊲ Binary dihedral PI code › p. 370 — Binary dihedral permuta-tion invariant codewords form error spaces of XP stabilizer codes. 

⊲ ⟦2𝐷 , 𝐷, 2⟧ hypercube quantum code › p. 338 — The 𝐷 th hypercube quantum code can be viewed as an XP stabilizer code with precision 

𝑁 = 2𝐷 [ 762 , Exam. 6.10]. ⊲ ⟦8, 1, 2⟧ Shen-Wang-Cao code › p. 356 —The ⟦8, 1, 2⟧ code is an XP-regular code that can be obtained via the XP stabilizer formalism applied to the ⟦15 , 1, 3⟧ Reed-Muller code [750 ]. ⊲ ⟦8, 3, 2⟧ Smallest interesting color code › p. 357 — As the 

𝐷 = 3 member of the hypercube-code family, the ⟦8, 3, 2⟧ code can be viewed as an XP stabilizer code with precision 𝑁 = 8 [762 , Exam. 469 6.10]. ⊲ Cluster-state code › p. 376 — XP stabilizer states are in one-to-one correspondence with weighted hypergraph states [ 732 , 762 ], which generalize both weighted graph states [ 3456 , 3469 , 3470 ] and hypergraph states [ 3471 – 3473 ]. XS STABILIZER CODE [3525] xs_stabilizer  

> DESCRIPTION

A type of stabilizer code where stabilizer generators are elements of the group {𝛼𝐼, 𝑋, √𝑍 }⊗𝑛 , with 𝑆 = √𝑍 = diag (1, 𝑖 ).The codespace is a joint +1 eigenspace of a set of stabilizer genera-tors, which need not commute to define a valid codespace. The phases in the qubit-basis expansion of an XS stabilizer state are polynomials of degree three or below [3525].

XYZ PRODUCT CODE [618, 1564] xyz_product  

> DESCRIPTION

A non-CSS QLDPC code obtained from a three-fold vari-ant of the hypergraph product applied to three classical binary codes with parity-check matrices 𝐻 1, 𝐻 2, 𝐻 3. Unlike CSS three-fold hy-pergraph product codes, the third input code acts through Pauli-𝑌 

checks [ 618 ]. Under mild assumptions, the code dimension is de-termined by a tensor Sylvester equation over F2, and the minimum-distance problem reduces up to constant factors to how closely a related inhomogeneous tensor Sylvester equation can be satisfied [ 618 ]. When the underlying classical codes are repetition codes, the construction yields the Chamon model code › p. 373 . 

> PROTECTION

The natural logical operators are membrane-like two-dimensional objects rather than strings [ 618 ]. For cyclic XYZ prod-uct codes, fractal operators yield large-weight errors with constant-weight syndromes, ruling out local testability [618].  

> RATE

The logical dimension depends on properties of the input clas-sical codes, specifically similarity invariants of the matrices 𝐻 𝑖 𝐻 𝑇 𝑖 .It is conjectured that specific instances of XYZ product codes have a constant encoding rate and a minimum distance of 𝑑 ∈ Θ(𝑛 2/3)

[618].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Quantum spatially coupled (SC-QLDPC) code › p. 431 — XYZ product stabilizer generator matrices can be used as sub-matrices to define a 2D SC-QLDPC code [ 617 ]. ⊲ Generalized homological-product code › p. 546 — The XYZ product code is a non-CSS three-fold 470 variant of the hypergraph product built from three classical linear binary codes [618].  

> CHILD

⊲ Chamon model code › p. 373 — The Chamon model code can be obtained from an XYZ product of three repetition codes [ 1564 ], in a construction different from the 3D surface code; see [ 618 , Sec. 3.4].  

> COUSINS

⊲ Linear binary code › p. 193 — The XYZ product code is a non-CSS three-fold variant of the hypergraph product built from three classical linear binary codes [ 618 ]. ⊲ Higher-dimensional homological product code › p. 399 — The XYZ product code is a non-CSS three-fold variant of the hypergraph product built from three classical linear binary codes [618]. ⊲ Asymmetric quantum code (AQC) › p. 296 — XYZ product codes can be used to protect against bi-ased noise [ 2552 ]. ⊲ Hypergraph product (HGP) code › p. 406 — Hy-pergraph (XYZ) product codes are constructed out of hypergraph products of two (three) classical linear codes.

XZZX SURFACE CODE [418, 2555, 4316, 4373] xzzx  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Wen plaquette model  

> DESCRIPTION

A variant of the rotated surface code whose generators are 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 Pauli strings associated, clockwise, to the vertices of X ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZXZX ZX ZXZ XZXZZXZX  

> FIG. 71: Stabilizer generators of an XZZX planar code with open boundaries. The generators are

𝑋𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 operators on the corners of squares in the bulk and 𝑋𝑍 

> operators on the boundaries.

each face of a two-dimensional lattice (with a qubit located at each vertex of the tessellation). 

XZZX toric code often either refers to the construction on the two-dimensional torus or is an alternative name for the general construc-tion. Twisted XZZX toric code refers to the construction on a torus with twisted (a.k.a. shifted) boundary conditions; these need not be equivalent to twisted toric codes because they can be non-CSS. The construction on surfaces with boundaries is often called the XZZX planar code . On a closed lattice, the Wen plaquette realization of the XZZX toric code has the same Z2 topological order as the toric code, and translation by one lattice unit exchanges the 𝑒 and 𝑚 anyons [445, Appx. C]. Stabilizer generators for this code are shown in Fig. 71 › p. 470 . 

> PROTECTION

As a stabilizer code, ⟦𝑛 = 𝑂 (𝑑 2), 𝑘 = 𝑂 (1), 𝑑 ⟧. 

> DECODING

⊲ MWPM decoder, which can be used for 𝑋 and 𝑍 noise. For 𝑌 noise, a variant of the matching decoder could be used like it is used for the XY code in Ref. [ 4369 ]. Decoding complexity scales as order › p. 161 𝑂 (𝑛 3) because the code is non-CSS [ 3636 ][ 4369 , Sup-plement].  

> CODE CAPACITY THRESHOLD

⊲ For large but finite 𝑋 - or 𝑍 -biased noise, the code’s thresholds exceed the zero-rate hashing bound. The difference of the threshold from the hashing bound exceeds 2.9% 

at a 𝑍 or 𝑋 bias of 300. ⊲ 50% threshold for noise infinitely bi-ased towards 𝑋 or 𝑌 or 𝑍 errors using a maximum-likelihood de-coder. ⊲ Depolarizing noise: 18 .7(1)% under tensor-network de-coder [2551] and 17 .5% under AMBP4 [3637].  

> THRESHOLD

⊲ ≈ 4.5% using minimum-weight perfect matching de-coder for depolarizing noise (bias 𝜂 = 0.5); ≈ 10% for infinite 𝑍 

bias. ⊲ 4.15% when 98% of depolarizing errors are converted into erasure errors with union-find decoder on a planar code, vs. 0.937% 

for pure depolarizing noise. The dominant source of noise in neu-tral atom arrays is spontaneous decay into detectable energy levels outside of the computational subspace. Since that decay occurs in a Rydberg level that is accessible from only one of the hyperfine states used for storage, the resulting channel is biased erasure [ 4374 ]. 

⊲ 0.817% and 0.940% with minimum-weight perfect matching and belief-matching decoder, respectively, for biased circuit-level noise [3767]. 471  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Superconducting circuits: Distance-five 25-qubit code implemented on a superconducting quantum processor by Google Quantum AI [ 3991 ]. This code outperformed the average of several instances of the smaller distance-three nine-qubit 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 

variant of the surface-17 › p. 359 code realized on the same device, both in terms of logical error probability over 25 cycles and in terms of logical error per cycle. This increase in error-correcting capabil-ities while using more physical qubits supports the notion of an error threshold. Braiding of defects has been demonstrated for the distance-five code [ 4375 ]. Leakage errors have been handled in a separate work in a distance-three code [ 3992 ]. Google Quantum AI follow-up experiment realizing distance-5 and distance-7 codes with 100 rounds of correction using the Libra and transformer-based decoders. The logical error rate is suppressed by a factor of ≈ 2,demonstrating beyond-break-even error correction with a block quantum code [ 3993 ]. Magic-state cultivation was demonstrated on a device by Google Quantum AI by code switching between a distance-three 6.6.6 color code and distance-five 𝑋 𝑍 𝑍 𝑋 surface code and decoding with the Tesseract decoder [3645]. 

⊲ Neutral atom arrays: Lukin group. Transversal CNOT gates performed on distance 3, 5, and 7 codes [ 3265 ]. Below-threshold performance on distance 3 and 5 codes with multiple rounds of syndrome extraction and error correction [3114].

YOKED SURFACE CODE [497] yoked_surface  

> DESCRIPTION

Member of a family of ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧ qubit CSS codes re-sulting from a concatenation of a QMDPC code › p. 426 with a rotated surface code › p. 448 . Concatenation does not impose additional con-nectivity constraints and can triple the number of logical qubits per physical qubit when compared to the original surface code. Con-catenation with 1D (2D) QMDPC yields codes with twice (four times) the distance. Using the concatenation convention of the Zoo, the sta-bilizer generators of the inner QMDPC code are referred to as yokes 

in this context; the cited paper [ 497 ] uses the opposite inner/outer terminology.  

> DECODING

⊲ Soft information from the outer surface codes can be utilized via a message passing algorithm [ 2620 ]. ⊲ Yokes can be measured using lattice surgery [497].

⟦3, 1, 2⟧3 THREE-QUTRIT CODE [4376] stab_3_1_2  

> DESCRIPTION

A ⟦3, 1, 2⟧3 prime-qudit CSS code that is the smallest qutrit stabilizer code to detect a single-qutrit error. It has stabilizer generators 𝑍 𝑍 𝑍 and 𝑋 𝑋 𝑋 . The code defines a quantum secret-sharing scheme and serves as a minimal model for the AdS/CFT holographic duality. It is also the smallest non-trivial instance of a quantum maximum distance separable code (QMDS), saturating the quantum Singleton bound. 473 The codewords are 

|0⟩ = 1

√3 (| 000 ⟩ + | 111 ⟩ + | 222 ⟩) |1⟩ = 1

√3 (| 012 ⟩ + | 120 ⟩ + | 201 ⟩) |2⟩ = 1

√3 (| 021 ⟩ + | 102 ⟩ + | 210 ⟩) .

(321) The elements in the superposition of each logical codeword are related to each other via cyclic permutations.  

> PROTECTION

Detects single qutrit errors and protects against a single-qutrit erasure. It is the smallest single-erasure correcting qudit code for 𝑞 > 2, and there does not exist a three-qubit code with analogous properties. The code is an example of a (( 2, 3)) threshold scheme where a secret (the quantum information) is split into 𝑛 = 3 shares and can be reconstructed from any 𝑘 = 2 of them. The key property of this code is that the reduced density matrix of any single qutrit is maximally mixed, meaning no information can be extracted from that qutrit. Therefore, a single qutrit tells you nothing about the encoded message, but access to any pair of qutrits reveals the secret.  

> ENCODING

⊲ In addition to thinking about the encoding of states, it is also interesting to look at the transformation of operators from the physical space into the logical space. Due to the unique structure and recovery protocol of the three-qutrit code, the representation of a logical operator 𝑂 is not unique. Instead, 𝑂 can be constructed from unitary matrices with support on only two out of the three qutrits. Therefore, the logical operator has valid representations supported on different pairs of qutrits. This operator construction is directly analogous to the construction of operators in the bulk (at the center) of the AdS 3-Rindler reconstruction. The three-qutrit code can then be used to describe how these local bulk operators are protected against localized boundary errors [2469].  

> DECODING

⊲ The quantum information (the secret) can be recovered from a unitary transformation acting on only two qutrits, 𝑈 𝑖 𝑗 ⊗ 𝐼 ,where 𝑈 𝑖 𝑗 acts on qutrits 𝑖, 𝑗 and 𝐼 is the identity on the remaining qutrit. By the cyclic structure of the codewords, this unitary trans-formation performs a permutation that recovers the information and stores it in one of the two qutrits involved in recovery.  

> NOTES

⊲ Connections to AdS/CFT from the perspective of how arbi-trary operators are encoded into the logical space. This encoding is analogous and helps explain why operators acting on the bulk are protected against localized boundary errors [2469].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Prime-qudit RS code › p. 483 — The three-qutrit code is the smallest member of a family of ⟦2𝑚 − 1, 1, 𝑚 ⟧𝑝 prime-qudit quantum RS codes for 𝑝 = 3 and 𝑚 = 2 [4376 ]. ⊲ Holographic tensor-network code › p. 308 — The three-qutrit code is a radius-one holographic tensor-network code and serves as a minimal model for holography [ 2469 , 2781 ]. ⊲ Perfect-tensor code › p. 312 — Three-qutrit codewords are AME, and the three-qutrit code stems from the 

⟦4, 0, 3⟧3 AME state › p. 312 [136 , 1867 , 2847 ]. ⊲ Quantum maximum-distance-separable (MDS) code › p. 317 — The three-qutrit code is the smallest nontrivial quantum MDS code. ⊲ Small-distance block quantum code › p. 321

ABELIAN QUANTUM-DOUBLE STABILIZER CODE [404]  

> quantum_double_abelian
> DESCRIPTION

Modular-qudit stabilizer code whose codewords realize 2D modular gapped Abelian topological order with trivial cocycle. The corresponding anyon theory is defined by an Abelian group. The 𝐺 = Z2 instance on a torus is the toric code, and cyclic-group instances reduce to modular-qudit surface codes. All such codes can be realized by a stack of modular-qudit surface codes because all finite Abelian groups are direct products of cyclic groups. There exists an invariant that can be computed to uniquely charac-terize the anyons of a state in an Abelian quantum-double topological phase [2445].  

> PROTECTION

Error-correcting properties established in Ref. [ 3026 ]using operator algebra theory. Correcting the maximum number of correctable errors is 𝑁 𝑃 -complete [4380].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Any geometrically local unitary circuit connecting two quantum double models whose groups are not isomorphic must have depth at least linear in 𝑛 [2445].  

> DECODING

⊲ Efficient decoder correcting below the code distance [4380].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Abelian TQD stabilizer code › p. 475 — The anyon theory corresponding to Abelian quantum double codes is defined by an Abelian group and trivial cocycle. > 𝑖

quantum doubles [ 388 ]. Conversely, every Abelian 475 anyon theory is a subtheory of some Abelian TQD [ 395 , Sec. 6.2]. Upon gauging some symmetries [ 216 , 442 – 450 ], Type-I and II Z32

TQDs realize the same topological order as certain Abelian quantum double models [ 548 , 550 ]. ⊲ Quantum-double code › p. 556 — The anyon theory corresponding to (Abelian) quantum double codes is defined by an (Abelian) group.

DOUBLE-SEMION STABILIZER CODE [388, 3524] double_semion  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Doubled semion model code  

> DESCRIPTION

A 2D lattice modular-qudit stabilizer code with qudit dimension 𝑞 = 4 that realizes the 2D double semion topological phase. The code can be obtained from a Z4 toric-code ground state by condensing › p. 559 the emergent boson 𝑒 2𝑚 2; in the stabilizer con-struction this condensation is implemented by two-body measure-ments [ 388 , 395 ]. Its ground-state subspace can be mapped to that of the double-semion string-net model by a finite-depth quantum circuit with ancillas [388]. This stabilizer code family is inequivalent to a CSS code via a constant-depth Clifford circuit [ 4382 , Thm. 1.1]. Similarly, the dou-ble semion model has a sign problem [ 4382 , 4383 ] that cannot be eliminated via such a circuit. However, the sign problem can be eliminated via a non-local circuit [4384].

FRACTON STABILIZER CODE [2942] fracton  

> DESCRIPTION

A 3D modular-qudit stabilizer code whose codewords make up the ground-state space of a Hamiltonian in a fracton phase. Unlike topological phases, whose excitations can move in any direc-tion, fracton phases are characterized by excitations whose move-ment is restricted. Qubit fracton stabilizer codes are commonly grouped into the following three sub-types [436]: (1) Foliated type-I fracton phase : Excitations are mobile in less than 3 dimensions, but codes can be grown by foliation , i.e., stack-ing copies of the 2D surface code and applying a constant-depth circuit [4385]. (2) Fractal type-I fracton phase : Excitations are mobile in less than 3 dimensions, and codes are not foliated. (3) Type-II fracton phase : Excitations are not mobile in any dimen-sion and there are no string operators. Fracton phases can be understood as topological defect networks, meaning that they can be described in the language of topological quantum field theory with defects [3071, 3072].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Modular-qudit stabilizer code › p. 481 ⊲ 3D lattice stabi-lizer code › p. 543  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Majorana checkerboard code › p. 416 — The Majorana checkerboard code is a foliated type-I fracton code [3876 ].

MODULAR-QUDIT CODE qudits_into_qudits  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Z𝑞 -qudit code ⊲ Modular-qudit subspace code  

> KINGDOM ROOT CODE

for the Modular-qudit Kingdom › p. 13 . 

> DESCRIPTION

Encodes a 𝐾 -dimensional Hilbert space into a 𝑞 𝑛 -dimensional ( 𝑛 -qudit) Hilbert space, with canonical qudit states |𝑘 ⟩

labeled by elements 𝑘 of the group Z𝑞 of integers modulo 𝑞 . Usually denoted as (( 𝑛, 𝐾 )) Z𝑞 or (( 𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )) Z𝑞 , whenever the code’s distance 

𝑑 is defined, and with 𝑞 = 𝑝 when the dimension is prime. There exists an analogue of the Wigner function for modular qudits [4392–4394].  

> PROTECTION

An (( 𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )) Z𝑞 code with distance 𝑑 detects errors act-ing on up to 𝑑 − 1 modular qudits, corrects erasure errors on up to 

𝑑 − 1 modular qudits, or corrects errors acting on up to ⌊( 𝑑 − 1)/ 2⌋

modular qudits. 

> Modular-qudit Pauli-string error basis

A convenient and often considered error set is the modular-qudit analogue [4395, 4396] of the Pauli string basis for qubit › p. 433 codes.  

> Modular-qudit Pauli strings:

For a single qudit, this set consists of products of powers of the modular-qudit Pauli matrices 𝑋 and 𝑍 ,which act on computational basis states |𝑘 ⟩ for 𝑘 ∈ Z𝑞 as 

𝑋 |𝑘 ⟩ = |𝑘 + 1⟩ and 𝑍 |𝑘 ⟩ = 𝑒 𝑖 2 𝜋 𝑞 𝑘 |𝑘 ⟩ , (324) with addition performed modulo 𝑞 . For multiple qudits, error set elements are tensor products of elements of the single-qudit error set. Tensor products of 𝑋 (𝑍 ) modular-qudit Paulis acting on dif-ferent qudits are called 𝑋 -type (𝑍 -type ) modular-qudit Pauli strings. Combining the 𝑋 -type and 𝑍 -type strings with a primitive 2𝑞 th root of unity forms a group called the modular-qudit Pauli group [2052]. For prime 𝑞 , this Pauli structure agrees with the usual prime-qudit Pauli group, but for prime-power 𝑞 = 𝑝 𝑚 with 𝑚 > 1 it differs from the Galois-qudit › p. 493 choice based on field structure. Modular-qudit Pauli matrices [ 4397 , 4398 ] are also known as Weyl operators [ 4399 ], Sylvester-t’Hooft generators [ 4400 , 4401 ], shift and boost operators [4402 ], or clock and shift matrices [ 4403 ]; they are special cases of Manin’s quantum plane [4404–4407]. The Pauli error set is a unitary basis for linear operators on the multi-qudit Hilbert space that is orthonormal under the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product; it is a nice error basis › p. 309 . The distance associated with this set is often the minimum weight of a qudit Pauli string that implements a nontrivial logical operation in the code.  

> RATE

Non-stabilizer states yield higher quantum capacity of the dis-crete beamsplitter channel [4408].  

> GATES

⊲ The normalizer of the modular-qudit Pauli group › p. 478 is the modular-qudit Clifford group [61 , 2052 , 4182 , 4390 , 4395 , 4409 –4412 ]. There is a standard form for modular-qudit Clifford-group operators [ 2052 , Lemma 4], and any modular-qudit Clifford gate can be constructed from phase-shift and quantum Fourier trans-form gates [ 4413 ]. For prime qudit dimension 𝑝 , the discrete Fourier transform, quadratic phase gate, and SUM gate generate the Clif-ford group [ 381 ]. Clifford circuits on prime qudits, together with Pauli measurements and classical feedforward, admit efficient clas-sical simulation by tracking stabilizer and logical generators; when measuring a Pauli outside the stabilizer normalizer, the outcome is uniformly distributed in Z𝑝 [381 ]. Universal computing can be achieved using qudit Clifford gates and a single type of non-Clifford gate, such as the 𝑇 gate [ 642 ]. Non-Clifford gates are typically more difficult to implement than Clifford gates and so are treated as a resource. There is a normal form for Clifford+ 𝑇 operators for qutrits [4414 ] and, more generally, odd prime qudits [ 4415 ]. Optimizing non-Clifford-gate count can be done using various procedures; see Refs. [ 4416 –4420 ] for qutrit codes. There are simulation algorithms for modular-qudit Clifford-dominated circuits [4421]. 

⊲ 

> Qudit Clifford hierarchy:

The modular-qudit Clifford hierarchy [ 764 ,2928 , 3126 , 4422 ] is a tower of gate sets which includes modular-qudit Pauli and modular-qudit Clifford gates at its first two levels, and non-Clifford qudit gates at higher levels. The 𝑘 th level is defined recursively by 

𝐶 𝑘 = {𝑈 |𝑈𝑃𝑈 † ∈ 𝐶 𝑘 −1 } , (325) where 𝑃 is any modular-qudit Pauli matrix, and 𝐶 1 is the modular-qudit Pauli group › p. 478 . Gates for one prime-dimensional qudit have been classified [4083].  

> DECODING

⊲ For few-qudit codes ( 𝑛 is small), decoding can be based on a lookup table. For infinite code families, the size of such a table scales exponentially with 𝑛 , so approximate decoding algorithms scaling polynomially with 𝑛 have to be used. The decoder deter-mining the most likely error given a noise channel is called the 

maximum-likelihood (ML) decoder.

MODULAR-QUDIT CWS CODE [2954, 3483, 4428] qudit_cws  

> DESCRIPTION

A CWS code for modular qudits, defined using a modular-qudit cluster state and a set of modular-qudit 𝑍 -type Pauli strings defined by a 𝑞 -ary classical code over Z𝑞 .The modular-qudit CWS construction takes in Q = (G , C) , where 

G is a graph, and where C is an (𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )Z𝑞 𝑞 -ary code over Z𝑞 .From the graph, we form the modular-qudit cluster state |G⟩ . From the 𝑞 -ary code, we form modular-qudit Pauli 𝑍 -type operators 𝑊 𝑖 =

𝑍 𝑐 𝑖, 1 ⊗· · ·⊗ 𝑍 𝑐 𝑖,𝑛 , where 𝑐 𝑖, 𝑗 is the 𝑗 -th coordinate of the 𝑖 -th classical codeword. The codewords are then |𝑖 ⟩ = 𝑊 𝑖 |G⟩ .In an alternative convention (not used here), CWS codes are de-fined from an underlying modular-qudit stabilizer state that is not necessarily a cluster state.  

> NOTES

⊲ See Ref. [3483] for qudit CWS code tables.  

> PARENT

⊲ Modular-qudit USt code › p. 483 — Any modular-qudit CWS code can be written as a modular-qudit USt whose ( 𝐾 = 1) stabi-lizer code is the modular-qudit cluster state and whose coset rep-resentatives are constructed from the 𝑞 -ary classical code over Z𝑞 .Prime-dimensional modular-qudit CWS codes have a unique repre-sentation as USt codes [ 4429 ]. Conversely, modular-qudit USt codes are equivalent to modular-qudit CWS codes via a single-modular-qudit Clifford circuit as follows [ 3485 , 3487 ][ 3075 , Sec. 10.4]. The set of coset representatives of any modular-qudit USt can be extended to a larger set iterating over the underlying stabilizer code such that all codewords can be obtained from a single stabilizer state. Then, one can apply a single-qudit Clifford transformation to map said modular-qudit stabilizer state into a modular-qudit cluster state.  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Codeword stabilized (CWS) code › p. 378 — Modular-qudit CWS codes reduce to CWS codes for 𝑞 = 2. ⊲ Modular-qudit cluster-state code › p. 477 — A type of modular-qudit cluster-state code can be built from a modular-qudit cluster state by applying the modular-qudit CWS construction using a linear 𝑞 -ary code, in which codewords are obtained by applying modular-qudit 𝑍 -type operators defined by the code to the modular-qudit cluster state; see, e.g., Ref. [3429].  

> COUSINS

⊲ Perfect quantum code › p. 312 — Generalized concatena-tions of modular-qudit CWS codes yield a family of codes that have larger logical dimension than stabilizer codes and that asymptotically approach the modular-qudit Hamming bound [ 2618 ]. 

⊲ Concatenated quantum code › p. 299 — Generalized concatenations of modular-qudit CWS codes yield a family of codes that have larger 480 logical dimension than stabilizer codes and that asymptotically ap-proach the modular-qudit Hamming bound [ 2618 ]. ⊲ Modular-qudit stabilizer code › p. 481 — Modular-qudit CWS codes whose under-lying classical code is a linear 𝑞 -ary code over Z𝑞 are modular-qudit stabilizer codes containing a cluster-state codeword; see [ 4430 , Corr. 4-5], which defines CWS codes as admitting an underlying stabilizer state that is not necessarily a cluster state.

MODULAR-QUDIT LATTICE COLOR CODE [642] qudit_color  

> DESCRIPTION

Extension of the color code to lattices of modular qu-dits. Codes are defined analogously to qubit color codes on suitable lattices of any spatial dimension, but a directionality is required in order to make the modular-qudit stabilizers commute. This can be done by puncturing a hyperspherical lattice [ 455 ] or constructing a star-bipartition; see [ 642 , Sec. III]. Logical dimension is determined by the genus of the underlying surface (for closed surfaces), types of boundaries (for open surfaces), and/or any twist defects present.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ Some modular-qudit lattice color codes on 𝐷 -dimensional lattices can transversally im-plement a gate at the (𝐷 − 1)st level of the qudit Clifford hierarchy  

> › p. 478

[642].  

> GATES

⊲ Modular-qudit lattice color codes whose 𝑋 -type stabilizers are placed on cells of dimension 𝜈 support transversal gates in the 

𝜈 th level of the qudit Clifford hierarchy › p. 478 as long as 𝜈 ! ≠ 0 modulo the qudit dimension [ 642 , Thm. 1]. These codes saturate the Bravyi-Koenig bound › p. 552 . In particular, 3D modular-qudit color codes admit a transversal modular-qudit 𝑇 gate. ⊲ For odd prime qudit dimension, charge-and-color-permuting twist defects can be used to implement generalized Clifford gates › p. 244 [4432].  

> DECODING

⊲ Generalized Color Clustering (GCC) decoder [4433].

MODULAR-QUDIT STABILIZER CODE [701, 4434] qudit_stabilizer  

> DESCRIPTION

An (( 𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )) 𝑞 modular-qudit code whose logical sub-space is the joint eigenspace of commuting qudit Pauli operators forming the code’s stabilizer group S [701 , Sec. 3.6]. Traditionally, the logical subspace is the joint +1 eigenspace, and the stabilizer group does not contain 𝑒 𝑖 𝜙 𝐼 for any 𝜙 ≠ 0. The distance 𝑑 is the minimum weight of a qudit Pauli string that implements a nontrivial logical operation in the code. A modular-qudit stabilizer code encoding an integer number of qudits ( 𝐾 = 𝑞 𝑘 ) is denoted as ⟦𝑛, 𝑘 ⟧Z𝑞 or ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧Z𝑞 . For composite 

𝑞 , such codes need not encode an integer number of qudits, with 𝐾 =

𝑞 𝑛 /| S| [ 4410 ][ 701 , Sec. 3.6]. This is because |S| need not be a power of 𝑞 , as group generators may have different orders. As a result, 

⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧ notation is often used with non-integer 𝑘 = log 𝑞 𝐾 , and the code dimension can be inferred from the prime decomposition of 𝑞 [4435 ]. Prime-qudit stabilizer codes, where 𝑞 = 𝑝 for some prime 𝑝 , do not suffer from this issue and encode 𝑘 logical qudits, with 𝐾 = 𝑝 𝑘 . 

> Modular symplectic representation:

The single modular-qudit Pauli string 𝑋 𝑎 𝑍 𝑏 for 𝑎, 𝑏 ∈ Z𝑞 is converted to the vector (𝑎 |𝑏 ) ∈ Z2 

> 𝑞

.The multi modular-qudit version follows naturally. Each code can be represented by a check matrix (a.k.a. stabilizer generator matrix ) 𝐻 = ( 𝐴 |𝐵 ), where each row (𝑎 |𝑏 ) is the modular symplectic representation › p. 481 of a stabilizer generator. The check matrix can be brought into standard form via Gaussian elimination [4410]. Modular-qudit stabilizer states can be expressed in terms of lin-ear and quadratic functions over Z𝑛 𝑞 [4182 ]. They correspond to the set of states with positive Wigner functions [ 4402 , 4436 ] (see [ 738 ,Thm. 8.4] for a robust version of Hudson’s theorem for odd prime-dimensional qudits). Stabilizer states saturate various uncertainty relations [ 4437 ]. General modular-qudit stabilizer codes can equiv-alently [ 3461 ] be defined using graphs, yielding an analytical form for the codewords [826]. There is a quantum GV bound › p. 298 for modular-qudit stabilizer codes [4438].  

> PROTECTION

Detects errors on up to 𝑑 − 1 qudits, and corrects erasure errors on up to 𝑑 − 1 qudits. More generally, define the normalizer 

N(S) of S to be the set of all Pauli operators that commute with all 

𝑆 ∈ S. A stabilizer code can correct a Pauli error set E if and only if 

𝐸 † 𝐹 ∉ N(S) \ S for all 𝐸, 𝐹 ∈ E . 

> MAGIC

The magic-state yield parameter 𝛾 = log 𝑑 (𝑛 /𝑘 ) quantifies the overhead cost of magic-state distillation per the original protocol [658, 659].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Encoder circuits for prime-qudit stabilizer codes [ 4377 ].  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ All qudit stabilizer codes realize modular qudit Pauli transformations transversally.  

> GATES

⊲ Gates in the qudit Clifford hierarchy › p. 478 can be done us-ing qudit gate teleportation , in which a gate can be obtained from a particular qudit magic state . Magic states that are eigenstates of qudit Clifford operators have been classified for prime qudit dimensions 3 and 5 [4439].  

> DECODING

⊲ Trellis decoder for prime-dimensional qudits, which builds a compact representation of the algebraic structure of the normalizer N(S) [4440].  

> NOTES

⊲ Distance upper bounds for Galois-qudit stabilizer codes for various 𝑛 and 𝑘 , based on algorithms developed in Refs. [ 2596 , 2597 ]and maintained by M. Grassl at this website 63 , hold for general modular-qudit codes because they are based on linear programming. 

⊲ A standardized definition of the qudit stabilizer group is developed in [ 4410 ]. ⊲ The number of modular-qudit stabilizer codes was determined in Refs. [4402, 4441].

𝑡 -design › p. 251 — The prime-qudit Clifford group is a unitary 2-design on 𝑈 ( 𝑝 𝑛 ) [901 ]. ⊲ Complex projective space code › p. 288 — Stabi-lizer states on 𝑛 prime-dimensional qudits form complex projec-tive 2-designs on C𝑃 𝑝 𝑛 −1 [ 896 ]. ⊲ Barnes-Wall (BW) lattice › p. 257 —Modular-qudit stabilizer states can be mapped into the first lattice shell of a BW lattice over a cyclotomic field, while the modular-qudit Clifford group is related to the symmetry group of the lattice [2058 ]. ⊲ Rotor stabilizer code › p. 558 — By combining the paper’s bounded-phase-space and integer-local-dimension constructions, prime-qudit stabilizer codes can be algebraically imported into rotor-code settings [ 4442 , Sec. 3.2]. ⊲ Analog stabilizer code › p. 510 —Prime-qudit stabilizer codes can be transformed into analog stabi-lizer codes on the same number of modes and logical modes, with distance at least as large as that of the original code [ 4442 , Thm. 12]. ⊲ Majorana stabilizer code › p. 417 — Majorana stabilizer codes can be extended to modular qudits, yielding parafermion stabilizer codes [ 3880 ]. ⊲ Subsystem modular-qudit stabilizer code › p. 485 —Subsystem modular-qudit stabilizer codes reduce to modular-qudit stabilizer codes when there are no gauge qudits. ⊲ Galois-qudit stabilizer code › p. 497 — Recalling that 𝑞 = 𝑝 𝑚 , Galois-qudit stabilizer codes can also be treated as prime-qudit stabilizer codes on 𝑚𝑛 qu-dits, giving 𝑘 = 𝑛𝑚 −𝑟 [ 663 ]. The case 𝑚 = 1 reduces to conventional prime-qudit stabilizer codes on 𝑛 qudits. A modular-qudit stabilizer code with composite dimension 𝑞 contains a subcode that is isomor-phic to a 𝑝 -dimensional prime-qudit stabilizer code for every prime factor 𝑝 of 𝑞 , and the distance of the full stabilizer code is bounded by the distance of this subcode [4443].

MODULAR-QUDIT SURFACE CODE [ 61 , 404 , 405 , 4444 ] qudit_surface  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Z𝑞 surface code  

> DESCRIPTION

Extension of the surface code to prime-dimensional [404 , 405 ] and more general modular qudits. Stabilizer generators are few-body 𝑋 -type and 𝑍 -type Pauli strings associated to the stars and plaquettes, respectively, of a tessellation of a two-dimensional surface. Since qudits have more than one 𝑋 and 𝑍 -type operator, various sets of stabilizer generators can be defined. Ground-state degeneracy and the associated phase depend on the qudit dimension and the stabilizer generators. In particular, the torus ground-state degeneracy can depend on the lattice periods, and the model can realize either topological order or symmetry-protected topological order [4444, 4445]. More generally, the Z𝑞 toric-code Hamiltonian admits rotor lim-its related to compact 𝑈 (1) lattice gauge theory and a continuum coupled-oscillator limit whose ground states coincide with those of the CV surface code [2458].  

> PROTECTION

The code distance is the minimum weight of a non-trivial homology or cohomology class, i.e., the length of the shortest non-contractible cycle in the cellulation or in its dual [ 61 ]. Planar discs with holes yield local modular-qudit surface-code families whose logical operators are described by relative homology classes [61].  

> GATES

⊲ A magic-state preparation routine for the Z4 surface code traverses through the 𝐷 4 quantum double model [ 4446 ]. ⊲ Gates can be implemented through topological operations corresponding to elements of the mapping class group, which is generated by Dehn-twists along non-contractible cycles [3735].  

> DECODING

⊲ Renormalization group decoder [3782, 4447].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ State preparation, anyon creation, anyon fusion, and transfer of entanglement between anyons and defects in a 24-qutrit trapped-ion device by Quantinuum [4448]. 483  

> NOTES

⊲ The simplest Decodoku game 64 is based on the qudit sur-face code with 𝑞 = 10 . See related Qiskit tutorial 65 .

SUBSYSTEM MODULAR-QUDIT STABILIZER CODE  

> qudit_subsystem_stabilizer
> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Gauge modular-qudit stabilizer code  

> DESCRIPTION

Modular-qudit generalization of a subsystem qubit sta-bilizer code. Can be obtained by taking a modular-qudit stabilizer code and assigning some of its logical qudits to be gauge qudits. For composite qudit dimensions, such codes need not encode an integer number of qudits. Subsystem stabilizer codes are defined by a gauge group G and a stabilizer group S, both subgroups of the 𝑛 -modular-qudit Pauli group › p. 478 P𝑛 that satisfy Z(G) = S, where Z denotes taking the center of a group. A code can be constructed by starting with either group. Given an 

S, one can pick any G satisfying S ⊆ G ⊆ N(S), where N(S) is the normalizer of the stabilizer group within P𝑛 . Alternatively, given a 

G, one defines S to be the center of the gauge group. The logical Pauli group is N(G)/ S. As such, the case when G = S

reduces to an ordinary stabilizer code, while the case G = N(S)

reduces to a trivial code. One can gauge fix [ 3286 ] an Abelian subgroup of the gauge group by adding it to the stabilizer group.  

> Gauge fixing:

Gauge fixing is a map between subsystem codes that is done using an Abelian subgroup F ⊆ G,

S → ⟨ S, F⟩

G → NG (F) , (336) where NG (F) is the normalizer of F within G.Gauge fixing can be used to switch between different stabilizer codes that yield different gauge sets in a process known as gauge switching . Gauge fixing also encompasses lattice surgery and code deformation [4454]. One can also gauge out a subgroup F of the modular-qudit Pauli group › p. 478 by adding it to the gauge group.  

> Gauging out:

Gauging out is a map between subsystem codes that is done using a subgroup F ⊆ P𝑛 ,

S → Z (⟨ G, F⟩) 

G → ⟨ G, F⟩ . (337) The stabilizer group of the output subsystem code is a subgroup of that of the input code, Z (⟨ G, F⟩) ⊆ Z (G). When F is a subgroup of the logical Pauli group, this is also called gauging . If F is itself a Pauli group of 𝑚 logical qudits of the original subsystem code, then gauging out those qudits is equivalent to treating them as gauge qubits. Gauging out should not be confused with gauging (or un-gauging) symmetries [ 442 , 445 – 447 ], a different process rooted in gauge theory which can be done to stabilizer or subsystem codes and which can change 𝑛 . 

> DECODING

⊲ Syndrome measurements are obtained by first measur-ing gauge operators of the code and taking their products, which give the stabilizer measurement outcomes. The order in which gauge operators are measured is important since they do not commute. There is a necessary and sufficient condition for inferring the stabi-lizer syndrome from the measurements of the gauge generators [ 567 ,Appendix]. ⊲ Decoder for certain geometrically local subsystem codes from hypergraphs [633].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Subsystem modular-qudit code › p. 484 ⊲ Subsystem sta-bilizer code › p. 560  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Subsystem qubit stabilizer code › p. 457 — Subsystem modular-qudit stabilizer codes reduce to subsystem qubit stabilizer codes for qudit dimension 𝑞 = 2. ⊲ Subsystem modular-qudit CSS code › p. 484 — Subsystem modular-qudit CSS codes are subsystem modular-qudit stabilizer codes whose gauge groups admit a gen-erating set of pure-𝑋 and pure-𝑍 Pauli strings. Any ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑟, 𝑑 ⟧Z𝑞 

subsystem stabilizer code can be mapped onto a ⟦2𝑛, 2𝑘, 2𝑟, ≥ 𝑑 ⟧Z𝑞 

subsystem CSS code via symplectic doubling › p. 485 , which preserves geometric locality of a code up to a constant factor. Every subsystem prime-qudit stabilizer code can be constructed from two nested sub-system prime-qudit CSS codes satisfying certain constraints [4304]. 486

ABELIAN LP CODE [643, 1200] abelian_lifted_product  

> DESCRIPTION

A lifted-product code whose lift group 𝐺 is Abelian. The case of 𝐺 being a cyclic group is a GB code (a.k.a. a quasi-cyclic LP code) [ 643 , Sec. III.E]. The Abelian LP construction has been adapted to accommodate noise bias, yielding bias-tailored LP codes [2578 ]. See Refs. [ 643 , 810 ,1200, 1509] for other explicit examples.

APPROXIMATE SECRET-SHARING CODE [2474]  

> quantum_secret_sharing
> DESCRIPTION

A family of ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧𝑞 CSS codes approximately correct-ing errors on up to ⌊( 𝑛 − 1)/ 2⌋ Galois qudits, i.e., with approximate distance approaching the no-cloning bound 𝑛 /2. Constructed us-ing a non-degenerate › p. 304 CSS code, such as a polynomial quantum code, and a classical authentication scheme. The code can be viewed as a 𝑡 -error-tolerant secret sharing scheme. Since the code yields a small logical subspace using large registers that contain both clas-sical and quantum information, it is not useful for practical error 489 correction problems, but instead demonstrates the power of approx-imate quantum error correction.  

> PROTECTION

Corrects up to ⌊( 𝑛 − 1)/ 2⌋ errors with fidelity exponen-tially close to 1.  

> ENCODING

⊲ Uses a quantum authentication scheme, which is a keyed system in which a valid state has high fidelity, and a classical secret-sharing scheme.  

> DECODING

⊲ Decoding is analogous to reconstruction in a secret sharing scheme and is done in polynomial time. The only required operations are verification of quantum authentication, which is a pair of polynomial-time quantum algorithms that check if the fidelity of the received state is close to 1, and erasure correction for a stabilizer code, which involves solving a system of linear equations.  

> PARENT

⊲ Galois-qudit CSS code › p. 493 — The code required to con-struct this code must be a non-degenerate › p. 304 Galois-qudit CSS code.  

> COUSINS

BALANCED PRODUCT (BP) CODE [415] balanced_product  

> DESCRIPTION

Family of CSS quantum codes obtained from two classical-code chain complexes that share a common group sym-metry. The balanced product can be understood as taking the usual tensor or hypergraph product and then quotienting by the shared symmetry action. This can reduce the overall number of physical qubits 𝑛 while, in favorable cases, preserving the number of encoded qubits and the code distance, thereby improving the encoding rate 

𝑘 /𝑛 and normalized distance 𝑑 /𝑛 compared to the underlying tensor or hypergraph product. For trivial group action, the construction reduces to a hypergraph product code. For cyclic groups, it overlaps with fiber-bundle and lifted-product constructions [415].  

> RATE

The original explicit balanced-product family is first con-structed as a horizontal subsystem code with 𝑘 ∈ Θ(𝑛 2/3), 𝑑 𝑋 ∈

Ω(𝑛 1/3), and 𝑑 𝑍 ∈ Θ(𝑛 ); after distance balancing, it yields an LDPC family with 𝑘 ∈ Θ(𝑛 4/5) and 𝑑 ∈ Ω(𝑛 3/5) [ 415 ]. For balanced prod-ucts of two good classical LDPC codes over groups of order Θ(𝑛 ),the original paper proves constant encoding rate and conjectures linear distance [415].  

> GATES

⊲ Logical gates via Dehn twists for balanced products of cyclic codes [3304].  

> DECODING

⊲ BP-OSD decoder [1200].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Galois-qudit CSS code › p. 493 ⊲ Generalized homological-product CSS code › p. 546 — Balanced product codes result from a ten-sor product of two classical-code chain complexes, followed by a factoring out of certain symmetries.  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Fiber-bundle code › p. 390 — Fiber-bundle codes can be formulated in terms of a balanced product [ 415 ]. ⊲ Lossless ex-pander balanced-product code › p. 415 ⊲ Lifted-product (LP) code  

> › p. 500

— Coarsely speaking, a lifted product is a balanced product where the group 𝐺 acts freely. In principle, a lifted product can be defined for rings that are more general than group algebras › p. 224 

F𝑞 𝐺 .

BIPARTITE CYCLIC CLUSTER (BCC) CODE [ 420 ] bipartite_cyclic_cluster  

> DESCRIPTION

Cyclic CSS code constructed from a bipartite cluster state with cyclic invariance, emphasizing simplicity of state prepa-ration over simplicity of stabilizers. A BCC code encodes 𝑘 logical qubits into 𝑛 = 𝑘𝑛 0 physical qubits. Qubits are labeled by pairs (𝑚, 𝑗 ) with 𝑚 defined modulo 𝑛 0 and 

1 ≤ 𝑗 ≤ 𝑘 , partitioned into sets 𝐴 (indices 𝑗 ∈ A ) and 𝐵 (indices 

𝑗 ∉ A). The code is defined by a bipartite graph 𝐺 on the qubits, with edges only between 𝐴 and 𝐵 , that is invariant under cyclic shifts 

(𝑚, 𝑗 ) → ( 𝑚 +1, 𝑗 ). Code states are prepared by initializing 𝐴 -qubits in |±⟩ and 𝐵 -qubits in |0/1⟩, then applying CNOT gates (source in 

𝐴 , target in 𝐵 ) along the edges of 𝐺 . The 2𝑘 resulting basis states confirm that 𝑘 logical qubits are encoded. After a Hadamard on each 𝐵 -qubit, this gives a CSS code. The 𝑋 -type stabilizers arise from conjugating 𝑋 𝑚, 𝑗 𝑋 𝑚 +1, 𝑗 (for 𝑗 ∈A) by the CNOT circuit, and the 𝑍 -type stabilizers from 𝑍 𝑚, 𝑗 𝑍 𝑚 +1, 𝑗 

(for 𝑗 ∈ B ). For 𝑘 = 2, the graph 𝐺 is parameterized by a set S of odd integers modulo 𝑛 = 2𝑛 0: even qubit 𝑚 connects to odd qubit 𝑚 ′ iff (𝑚 ′ −

𝑚 ) mod 𝑛 ∈ S .A related non-CSS construction, the cyclic cluster code , drops the bipartiteness requirement on 𝐺 . For 𝑑 = 3, this construction applied to the ⟦10 , 2, 3⟧ BCC code yields the ⟦5, 1, 3⟧ five-qubit perfect code [420].  

> PROTECTION

The distance satisfies 𝑑 ≤ |S| + 1, since 𝑈 † 𝑋 𝑚, 𝑗 𝑈 for 

𝑗 ∈ A gives a logical operator of weight |S| + 1 [420 ]. A weight-four GB code of odd distance 𝑑 satisfies 𝑛 ≥ 1 + 𝑑 2 [3091 ], so the 

⟦𝑑 2 + 1, 2, 𝑑 ⟧ BCC codes are optimal among weight-four BCC codes.  

> ENCODING

⊲ Initialize 𝐴 -qubits in |+⟩ and 𝐵 -qubits in |0⟩, then apply CNOT gates along edges of 𝐺 , followed by Hadamard on each 𝐵 -qubit.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ For 𝑘 = 2, all BCC codes admit a transversal Hadamard-SWAP logical gate via qubit permu-tation (𝑚, 1) ↦ → (− 𝑚, 2) followed by Hadamard on all qubits [ 420 ]. 

⊲ The ⟦𝑑 2 + 1, 2, 𝑑 ⟧ BCC codes also admit a logical Hadamard with-out SWAP via 𝑚 ↦ → 𝑚𝑑 (mod 𝑛 ) followed by Hadamard [420].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ For distance-3 BCC codes ( |S| = 2), a single error produces at most weight-1 logical error, so fault tolerance is preserved [420].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Generalized bicycle (GB) code › p. 498 — BCC codes are GB codes with weight-two circulant 𝐴 (polynomial 𝑎 (𝑥 ) = 1 + 𝑥 ) [ 420 ]. 

⊲ Cyclic quantum code › p. 301 — BCC codes are invariant under cyclic shifts by construction [420].  

> CHILDREN

⊲ ⟦10 , 2, 3⟧ rotated toric code › p. 332 — The ⟦10 , 2, 3⟧ ro-tated toric code is a ⟦𝑑 2 +1, 2, 𝑑 ⟧ BCC code for 𝑑 = 3 [ 420 ]. A non-CSS cyclic cluster code related to the ⟦10 , 2, 3⟧ rotated toric code yields the ⟦5, 1, 3⟧ five-qubit perfect code for 𝑑 = 3 [420 ]. ⊲ ⟦18 , 2, 5⟧

BCC code › p. 487 — The ⟦18 , 2, 5⟧ BCC code is the smallest BCC code with parameters ⟦𝑛, 2, 5⟧ [420].  

> COUSINS

⊲ Cluster-state code › p. 376 — BCC codes are obtained by applying Hadamard on the 𝐵 -sublattice of a bipartite cluster state, converting CZ-gate preparation into CNOT-gate preparation [ 420 ].

DISTANCE-BALANCED CODE [652, 2899, 4461] distance_balanced  

> DESCRIPTION

Galois-qudit CSS code obtained from a CSS code by in-creasing the smaller of the 𝑋 - and 𝑍 -distances using a homological-product-based balancing step or one of its generalizations. The initial code is said to be unbalanced , i.e., tailored to noise biased toward either bit- or phase-flip errors, and the procedure can result in a code that treats both types of errors on a more equal footing. In the original construction [ 2899 , Sec. 4], if 𝐶 is a QLDPC CSS code then applying the balancing step with parameter 𝑙 yields ˜𝐾 = 𝐾 ,

˜𝑑 𝑋 = 𝑙𝑑 𝑋 , ˜𝑑 𝑍 = 𝑑 𝑍 , and ˜𝑁 = 𝑂 (𝑁𝑙 ), so choosing 𝑙 ≈ 𝑑 𝑍 /𝑑 𝑋 

balances the two distances. In the generalized construction [ 652 ,Thm. 4.2], combining a component quantum code Q with a classical code 𝐶 yields a new code with 𝐾 = 𝑘 (Q) 𝑘 (𝐶 ), 𝐷 𝑋 = 𝑑 𝑋 (Q) 𝑑 (𝐶 ),and 𝐷 𝑍 = 𝑑 𝑍 (Q) , so choosing 𝑑 (𝐶 ) ≈ 𝑑 𝑍 /𝑑 𝑋 balances the two distances. The original distance-balancing procedure [ 2899 ], later generalized in this way, can yield QLDPC codes [2899, Thm. 1].  

> Weight reduction:

Various procedures performing weight reduction 

[ 2899 , 4309 , 4461 ] take in a stabilizer code and output a longer code with bounded stabilizer-generator weight. Hastings’ original con-struction [ 2899 ] makes a qubit CSS code QLDPC while preserving the number of logical qubits and keeping the block length polynomial in the original one. The weight reduction procedure of Ref. [ 4309 ]has been extended to subsystem qubit stabilizer codes [469].  

> DECODING

⊲ If the auxiliary classical LDPC code corrects all error patterns of weight < 𝛼 | 𝐴 |, then the resulting product code has a polynomial-time decoder for 𝑋 -errors of weight < 𝛼 | 𝐴 |𝑑 𝑋 /2, where 

𝑑 𝑋 is the 𝑋 -distance of the component quantum code [ 652 ]. ⊲ If the component 2D complex has a polynomial-time decoder for 𝑍 -errors of weight < 𝑤 , then the resulting distance-balanced code also has a polynomial-time decoder for 𝑍 -errors of weight < 𝑤 

[652 ]. ⊲ The effective distance of single-ancilla syndrome extrac-tion QLDPC code circuits can be preserved under weight reduction [3672 ]. The distance balancing technique of Ref. [ 652 ] preserves the effective distance › p. 435 of single-ancilla syndrome extraction circuits [3672].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ Single-ancilla syndrome extraction circuits that, for the most part, preserve the effective distance › p. 435 of weight-reduced qLDPC codes [ 3672 ]. The distance balancing technique of Ref. [652] preserves effective distance › p. 435 [3672].

EXPANDER LP CODE [169] expander_lifted_product  

> DESCRIPTION

Family of 𝐺 -lifted product codes constructed using two classical expander codes › p. 186 , equivalently two regular Tan-ner codes › p. 241 defined on the same expander graph [ 64 ]. For certain parameters, this construction yields the first asymptotically good QLDPC codes. Classical codes resulting from the same lifted-product complexes are one of the first two families of 𝑐 3-LTCs [169]. An expander lifted-product code family is constructed as follows. First, take the Cayley graph of a finite group 𝐺 . Second, take the double cover of the graph, resulting in a graph that satisfies the 492 requirements of participating in a 𝐺 -lifted product (i.e., the resulting graph is a free F𝑞 𝐺 -module). Third, create two Tanner codes › p. 241 

on that graph, in which parity-check supports are defined by the graph and the local constraints are specified by two short classical codes (chosen randomly in the original proof). Fourth, take the 

𝐺 -lifted product of those two Tanner codes. The small classical codes used in the construction of good QLDPC codes are required to have a certain product-expansion property [169 , Lemma 10 in]; it is proven that random codes satisfy said prop-erty in the thermodynamic limit.  

> PROTECTION

Code performance strongly depends on 𝐺 . Certain non-Abelian groups yield asymptotically good QLDPC codes with param-eters ⟦𝑛, 𝑘 = Θ (𝑛 ), 𝑑 = Θ (𝑛 )⟧ [169 ]. For cyclic Abelian groups 

𝐺 = Zℓ with ℓ = Θ (𝑛 /log 𝑛 ), quasi-cyclic expander LP codes yield families with parameters ⟦𝑛, 𝑘 = Θ (log 𝑛 ), 𝑑 = Θ (𝑛 /log 𝑛 )⟧ [643].  

> RATE

Expander lifted-product codes for non-Abelian groups in-clude the first examples [ 169 ] of (asymptotically) good QLDPC codes ,i.e., codes with asymptotically constant rate and linear distance. For cyclic Abelian groups 𝐺 = Zℓ with ℓ = Θ (𝑛 /log 𝑛 ), quasi-cyclic expander LP codes yield families with parameters ⟦𝑛, 𝑘 =Θ(log 𝑛 ), 𝑑 = Θ (𝑛 /log 𝑛 )⟧ [ 643 ]. Related balanced-product refor-mulations and other explicit Abelian LP constructions appear in [415, 1510].  

> GATES

⊲ Certain qubit expander LP codes can admit a cup product structure and can thus have logical gates in the Clifford hierarchy  

> › p. 435

implemented by constant-depth Clifford circuits [1470].  

> DECODING

⊲ Linear-time decoder [ 4016 ]. ⊲ Logarithmic-time sub-routine [2130].

FOLDED QUANTUM RS (FQRS) CODE [472] galois_fqrs  

> DESCRIPTION

CSS code on 𝑞 𝑚 -dimensional Galois-qudits that is con-structed from folded RS (FRS) codes (i.e., an RS code whose coordi-nates have been grouped together) via the Galois-qudit CSS construc-tion. This code is used to construct Singleton-bound approaching approximate quantum codes. More technically, an 𝑚 -folded quantum RS code is a member of the ⟦𝑛 /𝑚, 𝑅 · 𝑛 /𝑚, 𝑑 /𝑚 ⟧𝑞 𝑚 CSS code family for any 0 < 𝑅 < 1.See [ 472 , Defn. 3.8] for an expression of the codewords. A folded quantum generalized RS (GRS) code can be defined in similar fashion from GRS codes [472, Sec. 3].  

> PROTECTION

For every 𝛾 > 0 and 0 < 𝑅 < 1, there are folded quan-tum RS code families of rate 𝑅 with local dimension 𝑞 = 𝑛 𝑂 (1/𝛾 2 )

that are (( 1 − 𝑅 − 𝛾 )/ 2, 𝑛 𝑂 (1/𝛾 ) )-quantum list-decodable [ 472 , Thm. 3.9].  

> DECODING

⊲ Efficiently (( 1 − 𝑅 − 𝛾 )/ 2, 𝑛 𝑂 (1/𝛾 ) )-quantum list-decodable codes exist for every fixed 𝛾 > 0 and rate 0 < 𝑅 < 1

[472, Thm. 3.9].

GALOIS-QUDIT CODE galois_into_galois  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ F𝑞 -qudit code ⊲ F𝑞 -qudit code ⊲ Galois-qudit subspace code  

> KINGDOM ROOT CODE

for the Galois-qudit Kingdom › p. 13 . 

> DESCRIPTION

Encodes 𝐾 -dimensional Hilbert space into a 𝑞 𝑛 -dimensional ( 𝑛 -qudit) Hilbert space, with canonical qudit states 

|𝑘 ⟩ labeled by elements 𝑘 of the Galois field F𝑞 and with 𝑞 being a power of a prime 𝑝 .Codes can be denoted as (( 𝑛, 𝐾 )) 𝑞 or (( 𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )) 𝑞 , whenever the code’s distance 𝑑 is defined. This notation differentiates between Galois-qudit and (( 𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )) Z𝑞 modular-qudit codes, although the same notation is usually used for both. There exists an analogue of the Wigner function for Galois qudits [4392, 4393].  

> PROTECTION

An (( 𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )) 𝑞 code with distance 𝑑 detects errors acting on up to 𝑑 − 1 Galois qudits, corrects erasure errors on up to 𝑑 − 1

Galois qudits, or corrects errors acting on up to ⌊( 𝑑 − 1)/ 2⌋ Galois qudits. 

> Galois-qudit Pauli-string error basis

A convenient and often considered error set is the Galois-qudit analogue of the Pauli string set for qubit › p. 433 codes.  

> Galois-qudit Pauli strings:

For a single Galois qudit, this set consists of products of 𝑋 -type and 𝑍 -type operators labeled by elements 

𝛽 ∈ F𝑞 , which act on computational basis states |𝛾 ⟩ for 𝛾 ∈ F𝑞 as 

𝑋 𝛽 |𝛾 ⟩ = |𝛾 + 𝛽 ⟩ and 𝑍 𝛽 |𝛾 ⟩ = 𝑒 𝑖 2 𝜋 𝑝 tr (𝛽𝛾 ) |𝛾 ⟩ , (344) where tr is the field trace › p. 164 . For multiple Galois qudits, error set elements are tensor products of elements of the single-qudit error set. Tensor products of 𝑋 (𝑍 ) Galois-qudit Paulis acting on different qudits are called 𝑋 -type (𝑍 -type ) Galois-qudit Pauli strings. Combining the 𝑋 -type and 𝑍 -type strings with a 𝑝 th root of unity forms a group called the Galois-qudit Pauli group on 𝑛 Galois qudits. The Galois-qudit Pauli error set is a unitary basis for linear op-erators on the multi-qudit Hilbert space that is orthonormal under the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product; it is a nice error basis › p. 309 . The distance associated with this set is often the minimum weight of a Ga-lois qudit Pauli string that implements a nontrivial logical operation in the code.  

> GATES

⊲ The normalizer of the Galois-qudit Pauli group › p. 493 is the Galois-qudit Clifford group [4473][4425, Ch. 8].  

> DECODING

⊲ For few-qudit codes ( 𝑛 is small), decoding can be based on a lookup table. For infinite code families, the size of such a table scales exponentially with 𝑛 , so approximate decoding algo-rithms scaling polynomially with 𝑛 have to be used. The decoder determining the most likely error given a noise channel is called the maximum-likelihood (ML) decoder. ⊲ RL-on-Greedy decoder based on reinforcement learning [4474].

GALOIS-QUDIT CWS CODE galois_cws  

> DESCRIPTION

A CWS code for Galois qudits, defined using a Galois-qudit cluster state and a set of Galois-qudit 𝑍 -type Pauli strings defined by a 𝑞 -ary classical code. This entry has not yet been developed explicitly in the literature, so the formulation below is a conjectural Galois-qudit adaptation of the modular-qudit CWS constructions in Refs. [ 2954 , 3483 ]. The Galois-qudit CWS construction takes in Q = (G , C) , where G is a graph, and where C is an (𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )𝑞 𝑞 -ary code. From the graph, we form the Galois-qudit cluster state |G⟩ . From the 𝑞 -ary code, we form Galois-qudit Pauli 𝑍 -type operators 𝑊 𝑖 = 𝑍 𝑐 𝑖, 1 ⊗ · · · ⊗ 𝑍 𝑐 𝑖,𝑛 ,where 𝑐 𝑖, 𝑗 is the 𝑗 -th coordinate of the 𝑖 -th classical codeword. The codewords are then |𝑖 ⟩ = 𝑊 𝑖 |G⟩ . 

> PARENT

⊲ Galois-qudit USt code › p. 498 — Any Galois-qudit CWS code can be written as a USt whose ( 𝐾 = 1) stabilizer code is the Galois-qudit cluster state and whose coset representatives are constructed from the 𝑞 -ary classical code.  

> CHILD

⊲ Codeword stabilized (CWS) code › p. 378 — Galois-qudit CWS codes reduce to CWS codes for 𝑞 = 2. 

> COUSINS

⊲ Graph quantum code › p. 547 — A type of Galois-qudit cluster-state code can be built from a Galois-qudit cluster state by ap-plying the conjectural Galois-qudit CWS construction using a linear 

𝑞 -ary code, in which codewords are obtained by applying Galois-qudit 𝑍 -type operators defined by the code to the Galois-qudit clus-ter state. ⊲ Galois-qudit stabilizer code › p. 497 — Galois-qudit CWS codes whose underlying classical code is a linear 𝑞 -ary code are Galois-qudit stabilizer codes containing a cluster-state codeword.

A member of a family of Galois-qudit CSS codes whose stabilizer generator matrix is obtained from a hypergraph product of two classical linear 𝑞 -ary codes.  

> PARENT

⊲ Lifted-product (LP) code › p. 500 — Lifted-product codes for trivial lift are Galois-qudit hypergraph-product codes.  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Hypergraph product (HGP) code › p. 406 — Hypergraph product codes are Galois-qudit hypergraph-product codes for qudit dimension 𝑞 = 2. ⊲ Galois-qudit expander code › p. 494  

> COUSINS

⊲ Linear 𝑞 -ary code › p. 227 — Galois-qudit HGP codes are constructed out of two classical linear 𝑞 -ary codes. ⊲ Two-block group-algebra (2BGA) codes › p. 505 — A 2BGA code 𝐿𝑃 (𝑎, 𝑏 ) is con-structible as a hypergraph-product code when the support sub-groups generated by 𝑎 and 𝑏 are disjoint. In that case, the commut-ing matrices simultaneously acquire hypergraph-product Kronecker-product form, and the code can be obtained from a pair of classical group-algebra codes [804, Statements 8 and 12].

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ There exists an or-der › p. 161 ⟦𝑛, Θ(𝑛 ), Θ(𝑛 )⟧ 𝑛 2 punctured RS code family that admits transversal 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gates for any three logical qubits [ 698 ]. This code can be treated as a qubit code by decomposing each Galois qudit into a Kronecker product of several qubits; see [ 381 , 663 – 666 ][ 667 , Sec. 5.3]. This yields a qubit code family that is asymptotically good up to poly-logarithmic factors [ 698 ]. ⊲ Quantum RS codes can be con-catenated with quantum multiplication-friendly codes to yield CSS codes over a constant prime-power alphabet 𝑞 admitting a transver-sal 𝐶𝐶𝑍 𝑞 gate (and, for 𝑞 ≥ 5, also a transversal 𝑈 𝑞 gate) with nearly linear › p. 161 code dimension and distance, 𝑘, 𝑑 = Ω (𝑛 /2𝑂 (log ∗ 𝑛 ) ),where log ∗ 𝑛 is the iterated logarithm (the number of times log must be applied to 𝑛 before the result is ≤ 1) [665].  

> FAULT TOLERANCE

⊲ The original prime-field polynomial-code con-struction admits a fault-tolerant universal gate set beyond the standard transversal gates for qudit CSS codes [ 788 ]. Generalized NOT, SUM, SWAP, scalar multiplication, and phase gates are imple-mented transversally. A logical Fourier transform is implemented by weighted physical Fourier transforms followed by code switch-ing › p. 559 : a length-𝑚 degree-𝑑 polynomial code is mapped to the corresponding Fourier-dual polynomial code of degree 𝑚 − 𝑑 − 1.A transversal product gate |𝑎 ⟩| 𝑏 ⟩| 𝑐 ⟩ ↦ → | 𝑎 ⟩| 𝑏 ⟩| 𝑐 + 𝑎𝑏 ⟩ maps into a degree-2𝑑 polynomial code, after which degree reduction switches back to the original degree. ⊲ Aharonov and Ben-Or performed the code switching needed for their Fourier and product gates us-ing concatenation and degree reduction [ 788 ]. The same switching between polynomial codes of different degree can also be imple-mented by teleportation using encoded Bell states; this uses the transversal SUM gate between different-degree quantum RS codes, with the lower-degree code serving as the control. ⊲ Quantum RS codes yield fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant space and optimal time overheads [ 656 ], improving over previous schemes [3121, 3123].

GALOIS-QUDIT STABILIZER CODE [663] galois_stabilizer  

> DESCRIPTION

An (( 𝑛, 𝐾, 𝑑 )) 𝑞 Galois-qudit code whose logical sub-space is the joint eigenspace of commuting Galois-qudit Pauli oper-ators forming the code’s stabilizer group S. Traditionally, the logical subspace is the joint +1 eigenspace, and the stabilizer group does not contain 𝑒 𝑖 𝜙 𝐼 for any 𝜙 ≠ 0. The distance 𝑑 is the minimum weight of a Galois-qudit Pauli string that implements a nontrivial logical operation in the code. A Galois-qudit stabilizer code encoding an integer number of qudits ( 𝐾 = 𝑞 𝑘 ) is denoted as ⟦𝑛, 𝑘 ⟧𝑞 or ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧𝑞 . This notation differentiates between Galois-qudit and modular-qudit ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧Z𝑞 

stabilizer codes, although the same notation is usually used for both. Galois-qudit stabilizer codes need not encode an integer number of qudits, with 𝐾 = 𝑞 𝑛 − 𝑟 𝑚 , where 𝑟 is the number of generators of the stabilizer group, and 𝑞 = 𝑝 𝑚 given prime 𝑝 for all Galois qudits. As a result, ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧ notation is often used with non-integer 𝑘 = log 𝑞 𝐾 .

𝑟 [ 663 ]. In principle, Galois-qudit stabilizer states can be expressed in terms of linear and quadratic functions over Z𝑚𝑛 𝑝 [ 4182 ]. Such states correspond to the set of states with positive Wigner functions [4402, 4436]. Galois-qudit stabilizer codes can equivalently [ 3461 ] (see also [827 ]) be defined using graphs, yielding an analytical form for the codewords [826].  

> PROTECTION

Detects errors on up to 𝑑 − 1 qudits, and corrects era-sure errors on up to 𝑑 − 1 qudits. Corrects errors on ⌊( 𝑑 − 1)/ 2⌋

qudits. There are algorithms to calculate the minimum distance [4189 ]. There are established shortening/lengthening procedures for pure › p. 434 Galois-qudit stabilizer codes [1606][776, Table 1].

⊲ Encoder with 𝑂 (𝑛 2) gates can be determined in classi-cal runtime of order › p. 161 𝑂 (𝑛 3) [4473].

> RATE

GB codes can achieve an asymptotic rate of 1/4 [3091 ]. For an odd prime ℓ, let a prime 𝑝 be a quadratic-residue modulo ℓ,i.e. 𝑝 = 𝑚 2mod ℓ for some integer 𝑚 . Then, 𝑥 ℓ − 1 has only three irreducible factors in F𝑝 [𝑥 ], and there is a quadratic-residue cyclic code [ℓ, (ℓ + 1)/ 2, 𝑑 ] 𝑝 with 𝑑 ≥ √ℓ and an irreducible generator polynomial. Using the GV distance 𝑑 𝐺𝑉 , a prime-field GB code with parameters ⟦2ℓ, (ℓ − 1)/ 2, 𝑑 ≥ ℓ1/2⟧𝑝 exists. There exist GB codes that achieve the Hashing bound [4487].

⊲ BP-OSD decoder [1200].  

> CODE CAPACITY THRESHOLD

⊲ Depolarizing noise: 15% for a family of 6-limited ⟦2𝑚 +1 − 2, 2𝑚 ⟧ GB codes with BP-OSD decoder [ 1200 , Appx. C].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Two-block group-algebra (2BGA) codes › p. 505 — A code GB (𝑎, 𝑏 ) with circulants of size ℓ is a 2BGA code over the cyclic group Zℓ . More precisely, for the cyclic group Zℓ ≡ ⟨ 𝑥 |𝑥 ℓ = 1⟩,any element 𝑎 of the group algebra › p. 224 F𝑞 [Zℓ ] can be seen as a polynomial 𝑎 (𝑥 ) ∈ F𝑞 [𝑥 ] over the group generator 𝑥 , where the polynomial degree deg 𝑎 (𝑥 ) < ℓ . The 2BGA code LP (𝑎, 𝑏 ) is then just a generalized bicycle code GB [𝑎 (𝑥 ), 𝑏 (𝑥 )] constructed from the polynomials 𝑎 (𝑥 ) and 𝑏 (𝑥 ) corresponding to 𝑎, 𝑏 ∈ F𝑞 [Zℓ ].

⊲ Abelian LP code › p. 488 — A code GB (𝑎, 𝑏 ) with circulants of size ℓ is a special case of a lifted-product code LP ( 𝐴, 𝐵 ) code over the Abelian group algebra › p. 224 F𝑞 [Zℓ ] associated with a cyclic group, with 1 × 1 matrices 𝐴 = 𝑎 (𝑥 ), 𝐵 = 𝑏 (𝑥 ) given by the corresponding polynomials. Quasi-cyclic LP codes, i.e., LP codes constructed from cyclic groups, are equivalent to GB codes [643, Sec. III.E]. 

⊲ Lattice stabilizer code › p. 551 — Incommensurate GB codes of row weight 𝑤 are equivalent to CSS codes local in 𝐷 ≤ 𝑤 − 1 Eu-clidean dimensions, or in 𝐷 ≤ 𝑤 − 2 dimensions when ℓ is prime [3091, Statement 13][4488, Sec. II.A].

HERMITIAN GALOIS-QUDIT CODE [663, 2828][505, Corr. 5]  

> stabilizer_over_gfqsq
> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ F𝑞 2 -linear stabilizer code  

> DESCRIPTION

An ⟦𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ⟧𝑞 true Galois-qudit stabilizer code con-structed from a Hermitian self-orthogonal linear code over F𝑞 2 us-ing the one-to-one correspondence between the Galois-qudit Pauli matrices and elements of the Galois field F𝑞 2 .Galois-qudit stabilizer codes are in one-to-one correspondence with trace-alternating self-orthogonal additive codes of length 𝑛 

over F𝑞 2 via the F𝑞 2 representation › p. 497 . Hermitian self-orthogonal linear codes over F𝑞 2 are automatically trace-alternating self-orthogonal, and applying this mapping to such codes yields Hermi-tian codes [776, Corr. 19]. More generally, a trace-alternating self-orthogonal additive code 

𝐶 ⊆ F𝑛 𝑞 2 of size 𝑞 𝑟 yields an ⟦𝑛, 𝑛 − 𝑟 ⟧𝑞 true stabilizer code [ 663 ,Corr. 1]. When 𝐶 is Hermitian self-orthogonal and F𝑞 2 -linear of parameters [𝑛, 𝑘 ]𝑞 2 , the construction specializes to a Hermitian 

⟦𝑛, 𝑛 − 2𝑘 ⟧𝑞 true stabilizer code; this is called the Hermitian Galois-qudit construction [776 , Corr. 19]. The Hermitian construction was first proven via the Galois symplectic representation › p. 497 (showing self-orthogonality under the trace-symplectic inner product; see Ref. [ 663 ], Corr. 1). There is an isomorphism between the Galois-symplectic › p. 497 and F𝑞 2 representations › p. 497 [1966, Thm. 27.4.1]. It has also been extended to 𝑞 2𝑚 -ary Hermitian self-orthogonal linear codes [ 4490 ], and similar constructions were formulated in Ref. [ 4491 ]. Quantum construction X [1966 , Thm. 27.4.4], related to (classical) Construction X and Construction XX, allows for the use of nearly self-orthogonal codes [ 2597 , 4492 , 4493 ]; see Ref. [ 4494 ] for a review.  

> PROTECTION

For a trace-alternating self-orthogonal additive code 

𝐶 ⊆ F𝑛 𝑞 2 , the resulting true stabilizer code has distance 

𝑑 = min {wt (𝑣 ) : 𝑣 ∈ 𝐶 ⊥ \ 𝐶 } , (362) where ⊥ denotes duality under the trace-alternating inner product [663 , Corr. 1]. If 𝐶 is Hermitian self-orthogonal and F𝑞 2 -linear, then 

𝑑 = min {wt (𝑣 ) : 𝑣 ∈ 𝐶 ⊥ℎ \ 𝐶 } , (363) so the code distance is bounded below by the Hermitian dual dis-tance of 𝐶 [776, Corr. 19].  

> PARENT

⊲ True Galois-qudit stabilizer code › p. 504 — Hermitian codes are true stabilizer codes because they are based on Hermitian self-orthogonal linear (as opposed to additive) codes over F𝑞 2 .

LIFTED-PRODUCT (LP) CODE [169, 643, 1200] lifted_product  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Panteleev-Kalachev (PK) code  

> DESCRIPTION

Galois-qudit code that utilizes the notion of a lifted prod-uct in its construction. Lifted products of certain classical Tanner codes are the first (asymptotically) good QLDPC codes .A code can be defined by 𝐿𝑃 ( 𝐴, 𝐵 ), where 𝐴 and 𝐵 are a pair of matrices with elements from a group algebra › p. 224 . Heuristically, the code is constructed as a hypergraph product code over the group algebra › p. 224 , with each entry subsequently extended into a matrix. More technically, a lifted product over a ring 𝑅 is a product of two chain complexes whose chains are free modules over 𝑅 . An interesting case is when 𝑅 = F𝑞 [𝐺 ], the group-𝐺 algebra › p. 224 over the finite field F𝑞 = F𝑞 ; in this case, the product can be called a 𝐺 -lifted product . Just like its further generalization the balanced product, a lifted product code generalizes a hypergraph product code in that a reduction of symmetry is exploited to decrease the number of physical qubits required. The first version of this construction appeared as a family of generalized hypergraph product codes that contains hypergraph product codes in the case where one of the two input parity-check matrices is square [1200]. The key operation behind the 𝐺 -lifted product is the 𝐺 -lift , a group-algebraic › p. 224 version of the lifting › p. 211 procedure of proto-graph LDPC codes. A combination of the lift and the usual hyper-graph product yields lifted-product codes. The two operations com-mute: one can first take the usual hypergraph product of two chain complexes, and then lift the resulting product complex; equivalently, one can take the hypergraph product of the two lifted complexes.  

> PROTECTION

Code performance strongly depends on the group 𝐺 

used in the product [643].  

> RATE

There is no known simple way to compute the logical dimen-sion 𝑘 in the general case [643].  

> GATES

⊲ Transversal dimension jump, a code switching protocol between two LP codes [4495].  

> DECODING

⊲ Linear time iterative decoder [3680].  

> NOTES

⊲ Formerly known as generalized hypergraph product codes 

[1200], and later renamed to lifted-product codes [643, 3343].

QUANTUM AG CODE [4459, 4499] quantum_ag  

> DESCRIPTION

True Galois-qudit stabilizer code constructed from eval-uation AG codes via the Galois-qudit Hermitian construction or the Galois-qudit CSS construction.  

> RATE

Quantum AG codes can be asymptotically good [ 4459 , 4499 ]. There exist three such families [ 662 , 664 , 665 ] that admit a diagonal transversal gate at the third level of the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 . 

> MAGIC

By defining a generalization of triorthogonal matrices to Ga-lois qudits of dimension 𝑞 = 2𝑚 , one can construct an asymptotically good family of quantum AG codes that admits a diagonal transversal gate at the third level of the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 and attains a zero magic-state yield parameter, 𝛾 = 0 [662 ]. This code can be treated as a qubit code by decomposing each Galois qudit into a Kro-necker product of 𝑚 qubits; see [ 381 , 663 – 666 ][ 667 , Sec. 5.3]. Two other asymptotically good families [ 664 , 665 ] admit a transversal 

𝐶𝐶𝑍 gate (a different diagonal gate at the third level of the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 ) and achieve 𝛾 → 0 with constant alphabet size.  

> ENCODING

⊲ Encoding defined in Ref. [ 4459 ] uses a technique from Ref. [3614] to encode quantum stabilizer codes.  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ There exist three asymp-totically good code families [ 662 , 664 , 665 ] that admit a diagonal transversal gate at the third level of the Clifford hierarchy › p. 435 .

⊲ By decomposing each Galois qudit into a Kronecker product of qubits, the family of Ref. [ 664 ] yields an explicit asymptotically good qubit CSS code family with parameters ⟦𝑁, 𝐾 = Θ (𝑁 ), 𝐷 = Θ (𝑁 )⟧ 

on which 𝐶𝐶𝑍 ⊗𝐾 is realized by a transversal application of phys-ical 𝐶𝐶𝑍 gates on a constant fraction of qubits. ⊲ There exists an asymptotically good code family that admits three-Galois-qudit non-Clifford gates for any three logical Galois qudits [698].  

> PARENT

⊲ True Galois-qudit stabilizer code › p. 504 — Quantum AG codes can be constructed via the Galois-qudit CSS construction or the Galois-qudit Hermitian construction.  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Binary quantum Goppa code › p. 489 ⊲ Quantum Hermi-tian AG code › p. 502 ⊲ Quantum plane-curve code › p. 502 ⊲ Galois-qudit GRS code › p. 495 — Galois-qudit GRS codes can be constructed via the CSS construction or the Hermitian construction from GRS codes, which are evaluation AG codes.  

> COUSINS

⊲ Evaluation AG code › p. 219 — Quantum AG codes are quan-tum analogues of evaluation AG codes. ⊲ Triorthogonal code › p. 464

QUANTUM GABIDULIN CODE [2078] quantum_gabidulin  

> DESCRIPTION

A Galois-qudit stabilizer code over 𝑛 Galois qudits of dimension 𝑞 = 2𝑛 that is useful in protecting against faults in qubit Clifford circuits acting on stacked quantum memories. This code can be treated as a code on an 𝑛 × 𝑛 qubit stacked memory by de-composing each Galois qudit into a Kronecker product of 𝑛 qubits; see [381, 663–666][667, Sec. 5.3]. A quantum Gabidulin code is defined using two Gabidulin codes with associated parameters 𝑟, 𝑠 , respectively, such that 𝑟 + 𝑠 = 𝑛 

[2078].  

> PROTECTION

The code distance is the minimum rank distance — the rank of the field element of the lowest-rank undetectable Galois-qudit Pauli error, with the rank calculated by writing the element as an 𝑛 × 𝑛 binary matrix. The code is useful in protecting against faults in 𝑛 -qubit Clifford circuits with 𝑛 layers, which preserve the minimum rank distance.  

> PARENT

⊲ True Galois-qudit stabilizer code › p. 504  

> COUSINS

⊲ Gabidulin code › p. 246 — A quantum Gabidulin code is de-fined using two Gabidulin codes with associated parameters 𝑟, 𝑠 ,respectively, such that 𝑟 + 𝑠 = 𝑛 [2078 ]. ⊲ Rank-metric code › p. 249 

— Quantum Gabidulin code and (classical) rank-metric code dis-tances are based on ranks of the matrix representations of their corresponding errors.
