HYPERBOLIC TESSELLATION CODE [2729] tesselation  

> DESCRIPTION

Homogeneous-space code whose codewords are super-positions of positional delta functions on the hyperbolic plane. The positions are chosen according to regular triangle tessellations, and the code projector picks out an irreducible representation of the corresponding proper triangle group. Examples in Ref. [ 2729 ] are the {5, 5, 5} tessellation realizing the Pauli group of a five-dimensional qudit, the {6, 4, 8} tessellation realizing the single-qubit Clifford group › p. 244 , and the {4, 3, 5} tes-sellation realizing the binary icosahedral group 2𝐼 .563  

> PROTECTION

Protects against sufficiently small position and momen-tum shifts on the hyperbolic plane. In the three explicit examples of Ref. [ 2729 ], position-translation errors are correctable up to res-olutions 𝑑 𝑥 ≈ 1.6169 , 0.6605 , and 0.5011 , respectively. Momentum errors are represented by hyperbolic Laplacian eigenfunctions; the 

{5, 5, 5} example corrects all modes with angular index 𝑛 < 5, and more generally the compact quotient H2/Γ provides a nonzero Lapla-cian gap that acts as a momentum-error distance scale.  

> GATES

⊲ Logical operations are realized by rotations around selected vertices of the hyperbolic tessellation. In the {6, 4, 8} example, 𝑆 

and 𝑈 are implemented by 𝜋 /4 and 𝜋 /3 rotations, while the {4, 3, 5}

example realizes binary-icosahedral non-Clifford gates by 2𝜋 /3 and 

2𝜋 /5 rotations [2729].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Homogeneous-space quantum code › p. 562 — Hyperbolic tessellation codes are defined on the space of functions on the hyper-bolic plane, the symmetric space 𝐺 /𝐻 for 𝐺 = 𝑆𝑂 (2, 1) the proper Lorentz group and 𝐻 = 𝑂 (2). ⊲ Group-representation code › p. 306 

— Hyperbolic tessellation-code projections are onto a copy of an irre-ducible representation of the proper triangle group associated with the tessellation, and the resulting logical gates are implemented geometrically by hyperbolic rotations [2729].  

> COUSINS

⊲ Hyperbolic sphere packing › p. 289 — Hyperbolic tessella-tion codes are quantum counterparts of hyperbolic sphere pack-ings because they store information in quantum superpositions of points on the hyperbolic plane. ⊲ Pauli tessellation QSC › p. 528 —The tessellation-code framework spans spherical, Euclidean, and hyperbolic geometries; the Pauli tessellation QSC is the spheri-cal member [ 2729 ]. ⊲ Qutrit-Pauli tessellation code › p. 530 — The qutrit-Pauli tessellation code is the Euclidean {3, 3, 3} member of the same curvature-dependent tessellation-code framework [ 2729 ]. 

⊲ Concatenated GKP code › p. 519 — The qubit-Pauli tessellation GKP code [ 2729 ] is the Euclidean {2, 4, 4} member of the curvature-dependent tessellation-code framework. It is a two-mode code in which each Cartesian direction is a single-mode qubit GKP code, making the full code a 2-to-1 concatenated qubit encoding. The logi-cal single-qubit Pauli group › p. 433 is implemented geometrically by one 𝜋 rotation and two 𝜋 /2 rotations on the Euclidean tessellation [2729]. 564

CAGE-NET CODE [540, 542] cage_net  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ String-membrane-net code  

> DESCRIPTION

A commuting-projector code family obtained by cou-pling layers of two-dimensional topological orders and condensing extended one-dimensional flux strings [ 540 ]. A modern lattice real-ization starts from isotropic stacks of 𝐺 -graded string-net models [541 ]. The family includes stabilizer examples such as the Z2 string-membrane-net realization of the X-cube model [ 542 ] as well as non-stabilizer examples with non-Abelian restricted-mobility excitations [540 ]. String-membrane-net and cage-net constructions can realize the same fracton phases; for isotropic stacks, this equivalence can be understood via generalized local unitaries [ 541 ]. The cage-net construction can be used to realize various fracton phases, stabilizer and otherwise.  

> PARENTS

⊲ Category-based quantum code › p. 564 ⊲ Commuting-projector Hamiltonian code › p. 298 — Cage-net codewords form ground-state subspaces of frustration-free commuting projector Hamiltonians. ⊲ Frustration-free Hamiltonian code › p. 305 — Cage-net codewords form ground-state subspaces of frustration-free com-muting projector Hamiltonians.  

> CHILD

⊲ Qudit X-cube model code › p. 484 — A field-theoretic descrip-tion of the qudit X-cube model can be obtained by coupling layers of 2D Z𝑞 gauge theory [ 541 ]. For three orthogonal foliations with Z𝑞 lay-ers, the string-membrane-net model is equivalent to the Z𝑞 X-cube model [ 542 ]. String-membrane-net models are phase-equivalent to cage-net models under generalized local unitaries [541].  

> COUSINS

⊲ Fracton stabilizer code › p. 476 — The cage-net construction can be used to realize various fracton phases, stabilizer and other-wise. ⊲ String-net code › p. 566 — Cage-net codes are obtained by coupling layers of 𝐺 -graded string-net models [541]. 

CATEGORY-BASED QUANTUM CODE category_quantum  

> KINGDOM ROOT CODE

for the Category Kingdom › p. 14 . 

> DESCRIPTION

Encodes a finite-dimensional logical Hilbert space into a physical Hilbert space associated with a category. The categories of interest are typically fusion categories, which subsume all finite groups and many state spaces associated with topological codes. Codes on modular fusion categories are often associated with a particular topological quantum field theory (TQFT), as the data of such theories is described by such categories.  

> PARENT

⊲ Quantum error-correcting code (QECC) › p. 314  

> CHILDREN

Extensions of such categories to Lie groups can also be done [ 4924 – 4927 ] (see also [4928]).  

> COUSIN

⊲ Planar-perfect-tensor code › p. 314 — Several modular fusion categories can be used to define planar-perfect tensor › p. 314 s [2865]. 

FIBONACCI STRING-NET CODE [572, 3524] fibonacci  

> DESCRIPTION

Quantum error correcting code associated with the Levin-Wen string-net model with the Fibonacci input category, ad-mitting two types of encodings. The first type of encoding is into the ground-state subspace of the Levin-Wen model Hamiltonian, defined on a cell decomposition (dual to a triangulation) of a surface with a qubit on each link. The code space is the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of a set of vertex operators and plaquette operators, which are defined by the fusion rules and the numerical data of the Fibonacci category, respectively. In the corresponding doubled Fibonacci theory, the anyon types are 

1 × 1, 1 × 𝜏 , 𝜏 × 1, and 𝜏 × 𝜏 [572]. The second type of encoding is into the degenerate fusion space of a number of anyonic quasiparticle excitations of the Levin-Wen model. In the computational scheme of Ref. [ 572 ], logical informa-tion is encoded into pairs of 𝜏 × 𝜏 anyons that fuse to 1 × 1. This can equivalently be constructed by braiding holes in a spherical geometry [572, Sec. 5].  

> PROTECTION

When defined on a 𝐿 × 𝐿 tailed honeycomb tiling on a torus, the code distance for ground-state encoding is 𝐿 . 

> ENCODING

⊲ Code states may not be preparable with an adaptive constant-depth circuit with geometrically local gates and measure-ments throughout [ 4971 ]. ⊲ Ground-state initialization on small lattice [ 5006 ]. ⊲ Fusion-space initialization can be reduced to preparing pairs of 𝜏 × 𝜏 anyons by local cut-and-glue procedures and small projective measurements [572]. 565  

> TRANSVERSAL AND PERMUTATION-BASED GATES

⊲ A universal transversal gate set could be implemented in a folded version of this code using the techniques introduced in Ref [697].  

> GATES

⊲ Universal gate set for the ground-state encoding is imple-mented through topological operations corresponding to elements of the mapping class group, which is generated by Dehn-twists along non-contractible cycles. These Dehn-twists can be implemented using constant-depth circuits when allowing long-range permuta-tions of qubits [ 3735 , 5007 ]. The mapping class group of a disk with 

𝑚 punctures is the braid group of 𝑚 objects. ⊲ Universal gate set for the fusion-space encoding is implemented through braiding of the computational anyons [ 572 , 5008 ]. In the lattice realization of Ref. [ 572 ], these braids and the associated Dehn twists are enacted by local 𝐹 -moves, and readout reduces to measuring anyon labels on a fixed edge after local retriangulations. Circuit-based gates can be converted into braid patterns via quantum compiling algorithms [3879, 5009].  

> DECODING

⊲ Clustering decoder (provides best known threshold for this code) [ 5010 – 5012 ]. ⊲ Fusion-aware iterative minimum-weight perfect matching decoder. Note that ordinary MWPM decoders do not produce a threshold with this code [ 5012 ]. ⊲ Cellular automa-ton decoder [5013].  

> CODE CAPACITY THRESHOLD

⊲ 4.7% for depolarizing noise, 7.3% for de-phasing noise, and 3.8% for bit-flip noise with clustering decoder, as-suming perfect measurements and gates [ 5012 ]. See also Ref. [ 5010 ]. 

⊲ 3.0% for depolarizing noise, 6.0% for dephasing noise, and 2.5% 

for bit-flip noise with fusion-aware iterative MWPM decoder, assum-ing perfect measurements and gates [5012].  

> THRESHOLD

⊲ Between 10 −2% and 5 · 10 −2% for pair-creation and measurement noise [5013].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ NMR: Implementation of braiding-based Hadamard gate on two qubits [ 5014 ]. ⊲ Superconducting qubits: state prepa-ration, fusion, and braiding [ 5015 , 5016 ]. The latter work utilized DSNP and sampled the string-net wavefunction to estimate the un-derlying chromatic polynomial.  

> PARENT

⊲ String-net code › p. 566 — The string-net model code for the category Fib is the Fibonacci string-net code. 

GROUPOID TORIC CODE [5017] groupoid_surface  

> DESCRIPTION

Extension of the Kitaev surface code from Abelian groups to groupoids, i.e., multi-fusion categories in which every morphism is an isomorphism [ 543 ]. Some models admit fracton-like features such as extensive ground-state degeneracy and excitations with restricted mobility. The robustness of these features has not yet been established.  

> PARENT

⊲ Multi-fusion string-net code › p. 565 — Groupoid toric-code categories are unitary multi-fusion categories based on matrix alge-bras [ 5018 ], so groupoid toric codes can equivalently be formulated as multi-fusion string-net codes.  

> COUSIN

⊲ Fracton stabilizer code › p. 476 — Some groupoid toric code models admit fracton-like features such as extensive ground-state degeneracy and excitations with restricted mobility.

STRING-NET CODE [572, 3524, 5026, 5027] string_net  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Levin-Wen model code ⊲ Turaev-Viro code  

> DESCRIPTION

A non-stabilizer commuting-projector code whose code-words realize a 2D topological order rendered by a Turaev-Viro topo-logical field theory. The corresponding anyon theory is defined by a (multiplicity-free) unitary fusion category C. The code is defined on a cell decomposition dual to a triangulation of a two-dimensional surface, with a qudit of dimension |C| located at each edge of the decomposition. For modular input categories, the emergent anyon theory is the doubled category C ⊗ C ∗ [ 572 ]. These models realize local topological order (LTO) [573]. The codespace is the ground-state subspace of the Levin-Wen model commuting-projector Hamiltonian [ 3524 ], a many-body Hamiltonian realizing the 3-manifold Turaev-Viro invariant [ 572 ,5028 ]. For the Z2 input category on a genus-one handlebody, this construction yields the toric code [ 572 ]. This Hamiltonian is defined to act on a constrained Hilbert space defined by vertex constraints. Alternative constructions are possible, encoding information in the fusion space of the low-energy anyonic quasiparticle excitations of the model [ 572 , 5008 ]. The fusion space can have dimension greater than one, allowing for topological quantum computation of logical information stored in the fusion outcomes. Domain walls of string nets can be formulated using bimodule categories [ 5029 ]. Morita-equivalent string-net models are connected by constant-depth lo-cal unitary circuits built from invertible bimodule categories; on a hexagonal lattice, the circuit has depth three and also induces a map between tube-algebra excitations upon adding ancillas [ 3066 ]. Anyon condensation of general string net models is studied in Ref. [5030]. The initial formulation of string-net models [ 3524 ] considered uni-tary fusion categories with an extra tetrahedral symmetry, but this was realized not to be necessary [ 572 , 5026 ]. Explicit Hamiltonians for the more general categories have been studied [5027].  

> PROTECTION

Error-correcting properties established in Ref. [5031].  

> ENCODING

⊲ For an 𝐿 × 𝐿 lattice, deterministic state preparation can be done with a geometrically local unitary 𝑂 (𝐿 )-depth circuit [ 3718 ]or an 𝑂 (log 𝐿 )-depth unitary circuit with non-local two-qubit gates [3714 , 3719 ]. ⊲ Scalable dynamic string-net preparation (DSNP) [5016 ]. ⊲ String nets with solvable anyons and gappable bound-aries [ 5032 , Def. 1.2] can be prepared via an adaptive finite-depth local unitary circuit [ 5033 ]. ⊲ Suitable initial states can be pre-pared by locally cutting and gluing regions of the triangulation, reducing the task to preparing small fusion-space states [572].  

> GATES

⊲ Gates can be implemented through topological operations corresponding to elements of the mapping class group, which is generated by Dehn-twists along non-contractible cycles for trian-gulations of toroidal [ 3735 , 5007 ] and hyperbolic [ 5034 ] manifolds. Whether or not a gate set is universal depends on the choice of in-put category; in some cases such as the Ising category, gates can be complemented by topological charge measurements to obtain a universal gate set. ⊲ Alternatively, one could encode the logical quantum information into the degenerate fusion space of a number of computational anyons. In this case, a universal logical gate set can be implemented through the braiding of the computational anyons [572 , 5008 , 5035 ], e.g., for the case of the Fibonacci › p. 564 input cate-gory. ⊲ In the Levin-Wen realization, braid moves and Dehn twists can be implemented by sequences of local 𝐹 -moves; for general multiplicity-free modular categories these are fixed five-qudit gates, and the same local moves reduce topological-charge measurements to measurements of anyon labels on a fixed edge [572].  

> DECODING

⊲ Syndrome measurement circuits analyzed in Ref. [ 5036 ]. 

⊲ Clustering decoder [5011].  

> PARENT

⊲ Multi-fusion string-net code › p. 565  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Hopf-algebra quantum-double code › p. 565 — String-net model ground states reduce to Hopf-algebra quantum-double ground states for categories Rep (𝐻 ), where 𝐻 is a Hopf algebra [ 564 ]. 

⊲ Fibonacci string-net code › p. 564 — The string-net model code for the category Fib is the Fibonacci string-net code. ⊲ Twisted quan-tum double (TQD) code › p. 560 — String-net models realize TQDs for categories Vec 𝜔 𝐺 , where 𝐺 is a finite group and 𝜔 is a 3-cocycle on 

𝐺 . There is a duality between a large class of string-net models and certain TQD models [544].  

> COUSINS

⊲ Topological code › p. 325 — String-net codes realize 2D topo-logical phases based on unitary fusion categories. Any 2D many-body state satisfying the entanglement bootstrap axioms can be mapped into the ground-state subspace of a string-net model via a constant-depth unitary circuit [ 3065 ]. Different string-net mod-els with Morita-equivalent input fusion categories and the same topological order are connected by constant-depth unitary circuits and therefore lie in the same phase [ 3066 , 3067 ]. ⊲ Cage-net code  

> › p. 564

— Cage-net codes are obtained by coupling layers of 𝐺 -graded string-net models [ 541 ]. ⊲ Walker-Wang model code › p. 567 — The Walker-Wang model is a generalization of the 3D version of the Levin-Wen model [ 3524 , Sec. 5], which realizes gauge theories coupled to bosons and fermions. ⊲ Double-semion string-net code › p. 384 —The string-net model code for the category Vec 𝜔 Z2 for a nontriv-ial cocycle is the double semion string-net code. ⊲ X-cube model code › p. 468 — A non-stabilizer commuting-projector code constructed by stacking layers of the double-semion string-net model, called the semionic X-cube model [ 507 ], is equivalent to the X-cube model [4361 ] (see also Refs. [ 3876 , 4366 ]). ⊲ Toric code › p. 461 — The toric code is the Turaev-Viro/Levin-Wen string-net code for the Z2 input category; equivalently, the construction of Ref. TWO-GAUGE THEORY CODE [589] yetter_gauge_theory  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Higher gauge theory code  

> DESCRIPTION

A code whose codewords realize lattice two-gauge the-ory [ 580 –588 ] for a finite two-group (a.k.a. a crossed module ) in arbi-567 trary spatial dimension. There exist several lattice-model formula-tions in arbitrary spatial dimension [ 589 , 590 ] as well as explicitly in 3D [ 591 – 594 ] and 4D [ 594 ], with the 3D case realizing the Yetter model [595–598]. A two-gauge theory generalizes ordinary gauge theory by replac-ing the gauge group with a two-group (a.k.a. finite crossed module). Lattice formulations place gauge fields not only on edges of a lattice (as they do in ordinary gauge theory), but also on higher-dimensional structures such as faces. Ground-state degeneracy is a topological invariant for 3D mani-folds [ 590 ]; more precisely, it equals the number of homotopy classes of maps from the spatial manifold to the classifying space of the un-derlying finite two-group. Excitations of the 3D models are studied in Refs. [ 4914 , 5037 , 5038 ]. Generalizations of Ocneanu’s tube algebras [4912, 4913] can be used to characterize excitations [4914, 4998].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Category-based quantum code › p. 564 ⊲ Commuting-projector Hamiltonian code › p. 298 — Two-gauge theory code-words span ground-state subspaces of frustration-free commuting-projector Hamiltonians. ⊲ Frustration-free Hamiltonian code  

> › p. 305

— Two-gauge theory codewords span ground-state sub-spaces of frustration-free commuting-projector Hamiltonians. 

⊲ Topological code › p. 325 — Two-gauge theory codes realize lattice two-gauge theory for a finite two-group.  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Dijkgraaf-Witten gauge theory code › p. 545 — Replacing the two-group data in a two-gauge theory with a group and a cocycle reproduces the phase of the Dijkgraaf-Witten gauge theory, with the two theories equivalent in 2D [ 589 ]. Generalizations of Ocneanu’s tube algebras [ 4912 , 4913 ] can be used to characterize excitations in both theories [ 4914 , Sec. 4.2]. A Dijkgraaf-Witten Lagrangian can also be re-expressed as a two-group gauge theory Lagrangian by relating the electric and magnetic gauge fields via the equations of motion [ 589 , 4915 ]. ⊲ Cubic theory code › p. 383 — Cubic theory codes realize higher-form Z32 gauge theories with non-Abelian ex-citations in arbitrary dimensions. ⊲ Chen-Hsin invertible-order code › p. 374 — Chen-Hsin invertible-order codes realize beyond-group-cohomology invertible topological phases of order two and four in arbitrary dimensions. These phases are described by invertible two-gauge theories [551, pg. 11].  

> COUSINS

⊲ 𝐺 -enriched Walker-Wang model code › p. 564 — 𝐺 -enriched Walker-Wang models realize 3D two-gauge theories [ 5005 ]. 

⊲ Walker-Wang model code › p. 567 — Two-gauge theory codes for par-ticular two-groups are dual to certain Walker-Wang models based on Abelian groups [ 591 , Sec. V][ 593 , Sec. 7]. ⊲ Clifford-hierarchy sta-bilizer code › p. 375 — Clifford-hierarchy codes in 𝐷 spatial dimensions include (𝐷 + 1)-dimensional Dijkgraaf-Witten gauge theories with non-Abelian topological order [ 690 ]. A 𝐷 -dimensional code can be constructed from a twisted Z𝐷 +12 gauge theory with Dijkgraaf-Witten twist (− 1)    

> ∫𝑎 1∪𝑎 2∪···∪ 𝑎 𝐷 +1

𝐷 th level of the Clifford hierarchy in addition to Pauli 𝑋 operators. 

WALKER-WANG MODEL CODE [601] walker_wang  

> DESCRIPTION

A non-stabilizer commuting-projector 3D topological code defined by a unitary braided fusion category C (also known as a unitary premodular category). The code is defined on a cubic lattice that is resolved to be trivalent, with a qudit of dimension |C| 

located at each edge. The codespace is the ground-state subspace of the Walker-Wang model Hamiltonian [ 601 ] and realizes the Crane-Yetter model [ 602 –604 ]. A single-state version of the code provides a resource state for MBQC [458].  

> PROTECTION

Codespace dimensions (i.e., ground-state degeneracy) has been calculated for various boundary conditions [453].  

> ENCODING

⊲ For modular chiral anyon theories, a unitary encoder is conjectured to not be implementable in constant depth because it is believed to be an example of a quantum cellular automaton (QCA) (i.e., causal or locality-preserving automorphism) that cannot be locally implemented [ 2978 , 2979 ]. States of modular gapped theories can be initialized in constant depth [5039].  

> PARENT

⊲ 𝐺 -enriched Walker-Wang model code › p. 564 — 𝐺 -enriched Walker-Wang models reduce to Walker-Wang models for trivial 𝐺 

[5005].

CLASSICAL-QUANTUM (C-Q) CODE classical_into_quantum  

> DESCRIPTION

Code designed specifically for transmission of classical information through non-classical channels, e.g., quantum chan-nels, hybrid classical-quantum channels, or channels with classical inputs and quantum outputs. Such codes include maps from a clas-sical alphabet into a quantum Hilbert space.

The capacity above is the regularized version of this because 𝜒 can be super-additive; Hastings’ counterexample shows strict superadditivity for certain random channels [5043]. Corrections to the Holevo capacity and tradeoff between decoding error, code rate and code length are determined in quantum gen-eralizations of small [ 5044 ], moderate [ 978 , 5045 ], and large [ 5046 ]deviation analysis. Bounds exist on the one-shot capacity, i.e., the achievability of classical codes given only one use of the quantum channel. The ideal decoding error is suppressed exponentially with the number of subsystems 𝑛 (for c-q block codes), and the achievable exponent has been studied in Refs. [ 5047 – 5056 ]; see [ 5054 , Table 2] for a summary. Achievable error exponents for communication are related to those for privacy amplification [ 5057 ]. In the high-rate case, a lower [ 5058 ] and upper [ 5059 ] bound on the error expo-nent for general channels matches a conjecture by Holevo [ 5048 ]. A one-shot bound for random codes [ 5060 ] resolves a conjecture by Burnashev and Holevo [5047]. Unambiguous state discrimination (USD) can be used to achieve Holevo capacity on a general pure-state c-q channel [5061].  

> DECODING

⊲ Unambiguous state discrimination (USD) [5061].

In other words, classical codewords are elements of an alphabet, while quantum codewords are functions on the alphabet. EA MIXED-ALPHABET REED-SOLOMON C-Q CODE [1864]

⊲ Mixed-alphabet Reed-Solomon EACC code

> DESCRIPTION

Entanglement-assisted c-q code obtained from a mixed-alphabet Reed-Solomon construction over F𝑞 and F𝑞 2 . A codeword of an [𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ; 𝑐 ]𝑞 code consists of 𝑛 − 𝑐 symbols transmitted directly over 𝑞 -dimensional quantum systems and 𝑐 symbols transmitted through super-dense coding using 𝑐 pre-shared maximally entan-gled qudit pairs. More explicitly, the code evaluates all polynomials 𝑓 ∈ F𝑞 [𝑥 ] of degree at most 𝑘 − 1 at 𝑛 − 𝑐 distinct points 𝛼 𝑖 ∈ F𝑞 and 𝑐 repre-sentatives 𝛾 𝑗 ∈ F𝑞 2 \ F𝑞 , choosing at most one element from each conjugate pair {𝛾, 𝛾 𝑞 }. This yields codewords in F𝑛 −𝑐 𝑞 × F𝑐 𝑞 2 , where each F𝑞 2 symbol is identified with two 𝑞 -ary symbols for dense cod-ing.  

> PROTECTION

> RATE

The construction can have 𝑘 > 𝑛 when 𝑐 > 0, since each dense-coded position carries two 𝑞 -ary symbols. Its length is bounded by

ENTANGLEMENT-ASSISTED (EA) C-Q CODE ea_classical_into_quantum  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Entanglement-assisted classical communica-tion (EACC) code ⊲ Entanglement-assisted classical code  

> DESCRIPTION

Classical-quantum code whose encoding and decod-ing utilize pre-shared entanglement between sender and receiver. The sender encodes classical information into quantum systems sent through a quantum channel, while the receiver decodes using the channel outputs together with retained halves of pre-shared entangled states.  

> PROTECTION

A finite-block EACC code is often denoted by 

[𝑛, 𝑘, 𝑑 ; 𝑐 ]𝑞 , where 𝑛 is the number of 𝑞 -dimensional chan-nel uses, 𝑞 𝑘 is the number of classical messages, 𝑑 is the minimum distance, and 𝑐 is the number of pre-shared maximally entangled qudit pairs. Such a code corrects 𝑑 − 1 erasures or ⌊( 𝑑 − 1)/ 2⌋

errors in the setting of Ref. [1864].  

> RATE

The entanglement-assisted classical capacity 𝐶 ea (𝑇 ) is the highest asymptotic rate for reliable classical communication through a quantum channel 𝑇 when arbitrary pre-shared entan-glement is available [ 5063 , 5064 ]. For lossy bosonic channels with high thermal noise and low transmitted photon number, pre-shared entanglement can yield a capacity ratio scaling as log (1/𝑁 𝑆 ) rela-tive to the unassisted Holevo capacity [ 5065 , 5066 ]. If the encoding and decoding circuits themselves are noisy, the fault-tolerant EA capacity approaches the usual EA capacity as the gate error tends to zero [2669].  

> ENCODING

⊲ Super-dense coding maps two 𝑞 -ary classical symbols to one transmitted qudit when one maximally entangled qudit pair is available [5067].  

> PARENT

⊲ Entanglement-assisted operator-algebra QECC (EAOA QECC) › p. 303 — An EAOA QECC that has no gauge structure (e.g., gauge qubits), that has a block structure that corresponds to a clas-sical code, that stores no quantum information, and that utilizes pre-shared entanglement is an EA c-q code.  

> CHILD

⊲ EA mixed-alphabet Reed-Solomon c-q code › p. 568  

> COUSINS

⊲ Bosonic c-q code › p. 571 — Bosonic EA c-q schemes use pre-shared continuous-variable entanglement to assist bosonic c-q communication, including structured transceivers for lossy thermal-noise channels [ 5065 , 5066 ]. ⊲ Entanglement-assisted (EA) hybrid QECC › p. 302 — EA c-q codes transmit only classical information with entanglement assistance, while EA hybrid QECCs transmit both classical and quantum information with entanglement assistance. 

⊲ Entanglement-assisted (EA) QECC › p. 303 — EA c-q codes transmit classical information with entanglement assistance, while EAQECCs transmit quantum information with entanglement assistance. 570

“It from bit” symbolizes the idea that every item of the physical world has at bottom — a very deep bottom, in most instances — an immaterial source and explanation; that which we call reality arises in the last analysis from the posing of yes-or-no questions and the registering of equipment-evoked responses; in short, that all things physical are information-theoretic in origin and that this is a participatory universe. — John A. ⊲ Lechner-Hauke-Zoller (LHZ) parity code  

> DESCRIPTION

LDPC c-q code designed to convert the long-range inter-actions of a quantum annealer into local constraints. The code maps the pairwise couplings of a fully connected classical Ising model into local fields together with local parity constraints on a lattice of physical qubits. An extension maps more general models onto the same lattice [5070].

> KINGDOM ROOT CODE

for the Binary c-q Kingdom › p. 15 . 

> DESCRIPTION

A qubit code designed for transmission of classical in-formation in the form of bits through non-classical channels.  

> PROTECTION

Performance of a linear binary code over a channel is dual to the performance of its dual over a particular dual channel [5075].  

> DECODING

⊲ Belief propagation with quantum messages (BPQM) de-coder for c-q channel communication [ 5076 ]. The original BPQM proposal used quantum messages to decode pure-state c-q channels, had c-q polar codes in mind, and yielded explicit capacity-achieving decoders for non-Pauli channels [ 5076 ]. BPQM was analyzed for a BPSK-modulated pure-loss › p. 508 channel and shown to be optimal for small tree codes [ 5077 ]. A later quantum message-passing for-mulation proved optimality of BPQM for any binary linear code with a tree Tanner graph, and proposed an extension to factor graphs with cycles using approximate cloning [5078]. BPQM has also been extended to symmetric classical-quantum channels using paired measurements [5079].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Quantum enhancement was demonstrated using a polarization-based non-error-correcting c-q encoding [5080].  

> PARENT

⊲ Classical-quantum (c-q) code › p. 568

## III. ANALOG C-Q KINGDOM 

I like to tell my students: “There is no such thing as classical mechanics!” What I mean by this is that all physical systems are quantum mechanical in nature; the only question is if the classical theory is a sufficiently accurate approximation to reality so that it can be used instead of quantum theory. To use or not to use quantum theory? — That is the question. — Jonathan P. Dowling 

BOSONIC C-Q CODE bosonic_classical_into_quantum  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Bosonic c-q modulation format ⊲ Bosonic c-q modulation scheme ⊲ Bosonic c-q modulation code ⊲ Bosonic c-q signaling format  

> KINGDOM ROOT CODE

for the Analog c-q Kingdom › p. 15 . 

> DESCRIPTION

Bosonic code designed for transmission of classical information through non-classical channels. Encodes classical sym-bols into bosonic quantum states for transmission over a quantum channel and decoding with a quantum-enhanced receiver . This en-try includes bosonic c-q modulation formats and is distinct from a classical modulation scheme › p. 260 , which maps classical symbols into classical electromagnetic signals for transmission over classi-cal channels. A bosonic c-q modulation format instead treats the transmitted signals as quantum states and allows the receiver to use quantum measurements.  

> RATE

The Holevo capacity has been calculated for various bosonic quantum channels [5081–5083] such as the pure-loss bosonic chan-nel › p. 508 [5084 ] or quantum AWGN [ 5085 ]. The energy-constrained capacity of the noiseless bosonic c-q channel is finite due to quan-tum effects [ 5086 , 5087 ], while the Shannon capacity can be infinite. Gordon was the first to calculate such capacities (in a published work) for a specific case [ 5088 – 5090 ], and a related discussion is given by Forney [ 5091 ]. The most information-efficient format of a transmitted message is indistinguishable from black-body radiation [5092].  

> PARENT

⊲ Classical-quantum (c-q) code › p. 568  

> CHILDREN

⊲ Coherent-state c-q modulation format › p. 572 ⊲ Fock-state OOK c-q modulation format › p. 572 ⊲ Niset-Andersen-Cerf code  

> › p. 573

⊲ Squeezed-coherent BPSK c-q modulation format › p. 574  

> COUSINS

⊲ Bosonic code › p. 512 — Bosonic c-q codes are bosonic codes designed to transmit classical information. ⊲ Modulation scheme  

> › p. 260

— Classical modulation schemes transmit classical signals over classical channels, while bosonic c-q modulation formats trans-mit quantum states over quantum channels and can use quantum-enhanced receivers. ⊲ Analog code › p. 256 — Any analog code can be embedded into a bosonic Hilbert space, and thus passed through a bosonic channel, by associating the reals with the configura-tion space of position states of bosonic modes. ⊲ Entanglement-assisted (EA) c-q code › p. 569 — Bosonic EA c-q schemes use pre-shared continuous-variable entanglement to assist bosonic c-q communi-cation, including structured transceivers for lossy thermal-noise channels [5065, 5066].

FOCK-STATE OOK C-Q MODULATION FORMAT [ 5128 ] fock_state_ook  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Number-state OOK c-q modulation format 

⊲ Fock-state OOK c-q modulation code ⊲ Fock-state OOK c-q mod-ulation scheme ⊲ Fock-state OOK c-q signaling format ⊲ Single-photon OOK c-q modulation format ⊲ Single-rail c-q code  

> DESCRIPTION

Bosonic c-q on-off keying (OOK) modulation format whose binary alphabet consists of the vacuum state |0⟩ and the single-photon Fock state |1⟩ of one mode. More generally, the nonzero OOK symbol can be a number state or a mixture of adja-cent number states. Fock-state OOK with photon-number detection was analyzed as a nonclassical alternative to coherent-state OOK for photon-efficient communication [5128].  

> DECODING

⊲ Photon-number detection distinguishes the erasure/loss-degraded output alphabet by detecting whether photons are present in the received mode [ 5128 , 5129 ]. ⊲ Number-state modulation with photon detection, including the numerical observation that the optimal prior distribution can be multimodal, was studied in Ref. [ 5130 , Ch. 5]. Later work on incoherent OOK and PPM quantified improvements from sub-Poissonian nonclassical light and used Fock states as the nonclassical low-photon-number alphabet [5129].  

> PARENT

⊲ Bosonic c-q code › p. 571  

> COUSINS

⊲ On-off keyed (OOK) c-q modulation format › p. 573 — Fock-state OOK and coherent-state OOK both use a vacuum off symbol, but their on symbols are respectively a single-photon number state and a coherent state. ⊲ Fock-state bosonic code › p. 521 — Fock-state OOK transmits classical information using Fock states, while Fock-state bosonic codes store quantum information in subspaces built from Fock states. 

HADAMARD BPSK C-Q MODULATION FORMAT [833]   

> quantum_hadamard_bpsk
> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Hadamard BPSK c-q modulation code 

⊲ Hadamard BPSK c-q modulation scheme ⊲ Hadamard BPSK c-q signaling format  

> DESCRIPTION

Multimode coherent-state c-q code that is a concate-nation of a Hadamard code with a BPSK c-q code. Its codewords are 𝑛 -mode coherent states whose components ±𝛼 are arranged according to rows of a Hadamard matrix.  

> RATE

Using a joint-detection receiver, the code exhibits superaddi-tive capacity relative to symbol-by-symbol detection and approaches the Holevo limit in the low-photon regime [833].  

> PARENTS

⊲ Coherent-state c-q modulation format › p. 572 

⊲ Concatenated c-q code › p. 568 — The Hadamard BPSK c-q code can be thought of as a concatenation of the Hadamard binary 573 linear code with BPSK for the purposes of transmission of classical information over quantum channels.  

> CHILD

⊲ BPSK c-q modulation format › p. 571  

> COUSINS

⊲ [2𝑚 , 𝑚, 2𝑚 −1] Hadamard code › p. 173 — The Hadamard BPSK c-q code can be thought of as a concatenation of the Hadamard binary linear code with BPSK for the purposes of transmission of classical information over quantum channels. ⊲ Binary PSK (BPSK) modulation format › p. 268 — The Hadamard BPSK c-q code can be thought of as a concatenation of the Hadamard binary linear code with BPSK for the purposes of transmission of classical information over quantum channels. 

NISET-ANDERSEN-CERF CODE [4547] niset_andersen_cerf  

> DESCRIPTION

Coherent-state c-q code encoding two-mode coherent states {| 𝛼 ⟩, |𝛽 ⟩} into four modes such that the complex values (𝛼, 𝛽 )

are recoverable after a single-mode erasure. There are two varia-tions of the storage procedure: a deterministic protocol that offers recovery against a single-mode erasure, and a probabilistic one that can protect against multiple errors with post-selection. This code effectively protects classical information stored in (𝛼, 𝛽 ) using quantum operations.  

> PROTECTION

The deterministic protocol protects against a single era-sure error on a known mode. This recovers one state perfectly and the other state with fidelity 𝐹 = 11+𝑒 −2𝑟 for an initial EPR pair squeezed with variance 𝑒 −2𝑟 . The probabilistic protocol utilizes post-selection to protect against multiple erasures with state-dependent fidelity.  

> ENCODING

⊲ After an EPR pair preparation, use 2 continuous CNOT and 2 continuous inverse CNOT gates to entangle a bosonic EPR pair with initial states |𝛼 ⟩ and |𝛽 ⟩. ⊲ Alternate optical encoder using a two-mode squeezed vacuum state and two balanced beam splitters to mix the input coherent states with the EPR pair.  

> DECODING

⊲ Optical decoder using three beam splitters, electronic gain detectors, and two phase-insensitive amplifiers as described in Ref. [4547].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Realized in Ref. [ 5131 ] in an optical system with 3 beam splitters. The fidelity peaked around 0.6 for the deterministic approach, and around 0.77 for the probabilistic approach (with a 25% chance of error).  

> PARENT

⊲ Bosonic c-q code › p. 571  

> COUSINS

⊲ Coherent-state c-q modulation format › p. 572 — The Niset-Andersen-Cerf code uses coherent states but functions as an erasure-protection code rather than as a modulation format. ⊲ Analog repetition code › p. 510 — EPR pairs are used in an encoding of the Niset-Andersen-Cerf code [ 4547 ]. ⊲ Hayden-Nezami-Salton-Sanders bosonic code › p. 523 — The Niset-Andersen-Cerf code can be viewed as a scheme to replicate quantum information in multiple regions [2112]. 

ON-OFF KEYED (OOK) C-Q MODULATION FORMAT [5132]  

> quantum_ook
> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ On-off keyed (OOK) c-q modulation code 

⊲ On-off keyed (OOK) c-q modulation scheme ⊲ On-off keyed (OOK) c-q signaling format  

> DESCRIPTION

Coherent-state c-q binary code whose encoding is either in the vacuum |0⟩ or in a nonzero coherent state |𝛼 ⟩. 

> PROTECTION

For equal priors on the binary alphabet {| 0⟩, |𝛼 ⟩} , the minimum error probability is given by the Helstrom expression

. The mean photon number of the non-vacuum symbol is |𝛼 |2. 

> DECODING

⊲ Dolinar receiver [ 5133 ], which attains the Helstrom limit in the ideal model and has been demonstrated in proof-of-principle experiments [ 5132 ]. ⊲ Superconducting transition edge sensor (TES) photon-number resolving detector [5134].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Proof-of-principle experiments using Dolinar [ 5132 ]and TES receivers [5134].  

> PARENT

⊲ Coherent-state c-q modulation format › p. 572  

> COUSINS

⊲ Fock-state OOK c-q modulation format › p. 572 — Fock-state OOK and coherent-state OOK both use a vacuum off symbol, but their on symbols are respectively a single-photon number state and a coherent state. 

PSK C-Q MODULATION FORMAT [5135] quantum_psk  

> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ PSK c-q modulation code ⊲ PSK c-q modula-tion scheme ⊲ PSK c-q signaling format  

> DESCRIPTION

Coherent-state c-q 𝑞 -ary code whose 𝑗 th codeword cor-responds to a coherent state whose phase is the 𝑗 th multiple of 2𝜋 /𝑞 .These states are also called geometrically uniform states (GUS) [ 834 ].  

> PROTECTION

The error probability for 𝑞 = 4 under an optimal quantum detector is worked out in [ 4756 , Sec. IV.3]; see also [834, 5136, 5137].  

> DECODING

⊲ Multi-stage quantum receivers [5138 – 5143 ]. 

⊲ Bayesian inference [5108].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Unambiguous state discrimination using displacement-based receiver for 4-PSK [ 5144 ]. ⊲ Multi-stage quantum receivers [ 5135 , 5145 – 5147 ]. ⊲ Bayesian inference [5148 ]. ⊲ Time resolving quantum receiver operating in the telecom C band [ 5149 ]. ⊲ Displacements and photon detection [5150 ]. ⊲ Adaptive decoder using linear-optical elements and photon detection [5106].  

> PARENT

⊲ Coherent FSK (CFSK) c-q modulation format › p. 571 — The CFSK c-q code reduces to the 𝑞 -ary PSK c-q code when Δ𝜔 = 0 and 

Δ𝜃 = 2𝜋 /𝑞 . 

> CHILD

⊲ BPSK c-q modulation format › p. 571  

> COUSINS

⊲ Phase-shift keying (PSK) modulation format › p. 273 — PSK (PSK c-q) codes are used to transmit classical information using single-mode coherent states distributed on a circle over classical (quantum) channels. ⊲ Cat code › p. 515 — PSK c-q (cat) codes are used to transmit classical (quantum) information using (superpo-sitions of) single-mode coherent states distributed on a circle over quantum channels. ⊲ Polygon code › p. 273 — The PSK coherent-state constellation forms the vertices of a 𝑞 -gon. 574 

PULSE-POSITION (PPM) C-Q MODULATION FORMAT [5151]  

> quantum_ppm
> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Pulse-position (PPM) c-q modulation code 

⊲ Pulse-position (PPM) c-q modulation scheme ⊲ Pulse-position (PPM) c-q signaling format  

> DESCRIPTION

A 𝑞 -PPM c-q code is a coherent-state c-q code whose 𝑗 th codeword corresponds to a tensor-product state of zero-amplitude coherent states at all modes except mode 𝑗 . For example, a 3-PPM encoding corresponds to the three-mode states |𝛼 ⟩| 0⟩| 0⟩, |0⟩| 𝛼 ⟩| 0⟩,and |0⟩| 0⟩| 𝛼 ⟩ for some complex 𝛼 . The dual of a PPM code is ob-tained by the exchange 0 ↔ 𝛼 . 

> PROTECTION

The error probability under an optimal quantum detec-tor is worked out in [4756, Sec. IV.2].  

> DECODING

⊲ Conditional pulse nulling (CPN) receiver [5152].  

> REALIZATIONS

⊲ Conditional pulse nulling (CPN) receiver [5151].  

> PARENT

⊲ Coherent-state c-q modulation format › p. 572  

> COUSINS

⊲ Pulse-position modulation (PPM) format › p. 274 — PPM c-q codes are quantum analogues of PPM codes. ⊲ Biorthogonal spherical code › p. 268 — PPM c-q codewords are c-q spherical codes whose constellation consists of the standard basis vectors. Adjoining negatives yields the corresponding biorthogonal c-q spherical code. 

⊲ One-hot code › p. 196 — The PPM c-q code is a continuous analogue of the one-hot code designed for transmission through quantum channels. 

SQUEEZED-COHERENT BPSK C-Q MODULATION FORMAT [5153]  

> squeezed_coherent_bpsk
> ALTERNATIVE NAMES

⊲ Displaced-squeezed BPSK c-q modulation for-mat ⊲ Squeezed-state BPSK c-q modulation code ⊲ Squeezed-state BPSK c-q modulation scheme ⊲ Squeezed-state BPSK c-q signaling format ⊲ Two-photon coherent-state BPSK c-q modula-tion format  

> DESCRIPTION

Bosonic c-q binary modulation format whose code-words are antipodal displaced-squeezed states, i.e., states of the form 𝐷 (± 𝛼 )𝑆 (𝜁 )| 0⟩ for a common squeezing parameter 𝜁 . The for-mat was originally formulated using the term two-photon coherent states (TCS), an early name for squeezed states.  

> PROTECTION

Optimizing the displacement and squeezing for fixed mean photon number 𝑁 changes the coherent-state BPSK overlap exponent from 4𝑁 to 4𝑁 (𝑁 + 1) [5153 , Eq. (3.41)]. Thus, in the ideal binary pure-state discrimination expression, the coherent-state BPSK factor exp [− 4𝑁 ] is replaced by exp [− 4𝑁 (𝑁 + 1)] . 

> RATE

The c-q capacity of squeezed-state modulation over a pure-loss bosonic channel › p. 508 with coherent homodyne or heterodyne receivers, including closed-form optima for homodyne detection, was studied in Ref. [5130, Ch. 5].  

> DECODING

⊲ Homodyne detection realizes the field-quadrature mea-surement advantage of antipodal TCS signals in the ideal model [5153 ]. ⊲ Homodyne and heterodyne receivers for squeezed-state modulation are treated in Ref. [5130, Ch. 5].  

> PARENT

⊲ Bosonic c-q code › p. 571  

> CHILD

⊲ BPSK c-q modulation format › p. 571 — Squeezed-coherent BPSK c-q modulation reduces to coherent-state BPSK c-q modulation when the squeezing parameter is zero.  

> COUSIN

⊲ Squeezed cat code › p. 532 — Squeezed-coherent BPSK c-q modulation transmits classical information using displaced-squeezed states, while squeezed cat codes store quantum informa-tion in superpositions of squeezed coherent states. 575
